children.title: Row Normalization
children.top_down_role: Canonical treatment of row orientation, relation sense, plus row metadata.

assumptions_latex: The input row is \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\mathrel{\rho_i}b_i\), where \(\rho_i\in\{\le,=,\ge\}\).
The chosen scale \(s_i\) is finite and nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\mathrel{\rho_i}b_i\iff (s_i a_i)^{\mathsf T}x\mathrel{\rho_i'}s_i b_i\), with \(\rho_i'=\rho_i\) for \(s_i>0\) and the inequality reversed for \(s_i<0\).

notation.meaning: Original row coefficient vector, right-hand side, and relation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence-preserving scaling of one finite LP row, including the sign rule for inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a row \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\mathrel{\rho_i}b_i\), choose a finite scale \(s_i\ne0\), commonly so that \(\lVert s_i a_i\rVert_\infty=1\) when \(a_i\ne0\). Replace the coefficients and right-hand side by \(a_i'=s_i a_i\) and \(b_i'=s_i b_i\). If \(s_i>0\), retain \(\rho_i' = \rho_i\). If \(s_i<0\), retain equality but exchange \(\le\) and \(\ge\). The normalized row has exactly the same satisfying vectors \(x\) as the original row. A zero row is excluded and handled by an empty-row reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale every coefficient and the right-hand side together; a negative scale reverses an inequality. This preserves exactly the row's feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Row Normalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaling rule is mathematically precise and fits the row-normalization container, but the cited Chapter 8 opening page concerns implementation and factorization topics and does not inspectably support row normalization.

children.title: Bound Normalization
children.top_down_role: Canonical treatment of variable limits, bound types, plus internal bound storage.

assumptions_latex: The scalar variable satisfies \(\ell_j\le x_j\le u_j\), where \(-\infty\le\ell_j<u_j\le+\infty\).
All occurrences of \(x_j\) in the objective and rows are transformed consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For finite \(\ell_j\), the substitution \(x_j=\ell_j+y_j\) maps \([\ell_j,u_j]\) bijectively onto \([0,u_j-\ell_j]\).

notation.meaning: Original variable and its extended-real bounds.
Shifted variable with zero lower bound.
Column of the original variable in the constraint matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine normalization of a finite lower bound; free-variable splitting is treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a variable with finite lower bound \(\ell_j\), introduce \(y_j=x_j-\ell_j\). Then \(y_j\ge0\), and a finite upper bound becomes \(y_j\le u_j-\ell_j\). Substitute \(x_j=\ell_j+y_j\) everywhere: the row right-hand side changes from \(b\) to \(b-\ell_jA_{:j}\), and a minimization objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) acquires constant \(d+c_j\ell_j\). If only \(u_j\) is finite, the analogous substitution \(x_j=u_j-y_j\), with \(y_j\ge0\), is valid. Store the affine map for postsolve recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift or reflect a bounded variable to obtain a nonnegative variable, updating rows and the objective constant and recording the inverse map.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Normalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine bound transformations are coherent and algorithm is an appropriate kind, but the cited locator does not inspectably support these substitutions, model updates, and postsolve recovery claims.

children.title: Objective Normalization
children.top_down_role: Objective direction, offsets, coefficients, plus internal objective conventions.

assumptions_latex: The objective is \(f(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) on a fixed feasible set \(F\).
The requested sense is either minimization or maximization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}(-f(x))\), and the optimal values differ by a factor of \(-1\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set, unchanged by objective normalization.
Sense multiplier: one for minimization and minus one for maximization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical conversion of an affine LP objective to minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set and let \(f(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x+d\). Define \(\sigma=1\) for an input minimization problem and \(\sigma=-1\) for an input maximization problem. The normalized objective is to minimize \(\widehat f(x)=\sigma f(x)\) over \(F\). This transformation leaves the optimizer set unchanged after interpreting the original sense. If \(v\) is the normalized optimal value, the original optimal value is \(\sigma v\). The multiplier \(\sigma\) must also be applied when translating objective bounds, reduced costs, and dual objective values back to the input convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent either objective sense as minimization by multiplying a maximization objective by minus one and retaining the sign for result recovery.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Normalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The objective-sign transformation is standard and internally consistent, but the cited locator does not inspectably support the normalization or the claims about translating reduced costs and dual objective values.

children.title: Sense Normalization
children.top_down_role: Internal conventions for constraint senses plus reversibility of sense changes.

assumptions_latex: Each constraint row has relation \(\rho_i\in\{\le,=,\ge\}\).
The canonical row sense is \(\le\), with equalities retained as equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\ge\) row is equivalently replaced by a \(\le\) row through multiplication by \(-1\); \(\le\) and equality rows remain unchanged.

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector, right-hand side, and input row relation.
Normalized coefficient vector, right-hand side, and relation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonicalization of mixed inequality directions while retaining equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each input row \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\mathrel{\rho_i}b_i\), define its canonical representation independently. If \(\rho_i=\ge\), set \(\widehat a_i=-a_i\), \(\widehat b_i=-b_i\), and \(\widehat\rho_i=\le\). If \(\rho_i=\le\), copy the row unchanged. If \(\rho_i=\mathord=\), retain equality. Thus each inequality has canonical sense \(\le\), and the normalized system has exactly the original feasible set. Record whether a row was negated so that dual multipliers, activities, residuals, and diagnostic row statuses can be returned under the input sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negate every greater-than-or-equal row to obtain a less-than-or-equal row, retain equalities, and record the sign change for diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.title: Sense Normalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sense-normalization algorithm is mathematically correct and appropriately scoped, but the cited locator does not inspectably support the transformation and diagnostic-recovery claims.

children.title: Free-Variable Representations
children.top_down_role: Native storage plus solver treatment of variables lacking finite bounds.

assumptions_latex: The scalar decision variable \(x_j\) has domain \(\mathbb R\).
Its constraint column and objective coefficient are \(A_{:j}\) and \(c_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unrestricted domain \(x_j\in\mathbb R\) is represented directly, without imposing either a lower or an upper bound.

notation.meaning: Constraint column and objective coefficient associated with the variable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Native, unsplit representation of one unrestricted LP variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A free-variable representation stores a scalar \(x_j\in\mathbb R\) with lower bound \(\ell_j=-\infty\) and upper bound \(u_j=+\infty\). Its contribution to the constraint system and objective remains \(A_{:j}x_j\) and \(c_jx_j\), respectively. No sign restriction or auxiliary column is introduced. This representation is mathematically complete because every real value is admissible, but an algorithm whose standard form requires nonnegative variables must convert it to an equivalent representation, such as a difference of two nonnegative variables, and retain the recovery map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free variable is stored directly with both bounds infinite; methods requiring nonnegative variables must transform it and preserve a recovery map.
knowledge_statements.title: Free-Variable Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The native unrestricted-variable representation fits the container, but the cited implementation chapter page does not inspectably support the representation or conversion requirement.

children.title: Split-Variable Representations
children.top_down_role: Positive-part versus negative-part representations used for unrestricted variables.

assumptions_latex: The original variable is unrestricted: \(x_j\in\mathbb R\).
The replacement variables satisfy \(x_j^+\ge0\) and \(x_j^-\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-\) maps \(\mathbb R_+^2\) onto \(\mathbb R\), while replacing \(A_{:j}\) by \((A_{:j},-A_{:j})\) and \(c_j\) by \((c_j,-c_j)\).

notation.meaning: Original constraint column and objective coefficient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form replacement of one unrestricted variable by two nonnegative variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replace an unrestricted variable \(x_j\in\mathbb R\) by \(x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-\), where \(x_j^+\ge0\) and \(x_j^-\ge0\). In the constraint matrix, replace column \(A_{:j}\) by the two columns \(A_{:j}\) and \(-A_{:j}\). In the objective, replace coefficient \(c_j\) by \(c_j\) and \(-c_j\). The map from \((x_j^+,x_j^-)\in\mathbb R_+^2\) to \(x_j\in\mathbb R\) is surjective, so the transformed LP has the same attainable constraint activities and objective values as the original LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace an unrestricted variable by the difference of two nonnegative variables, duplicating its column and objective coefficient with opposite signs.
knowledge_statements.title: Split-Variable Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The split-variable representation and its column and objective transformations are correct, but the supplied locator does not inspectably support them.

children.title: Free-to-Split Mapping Consequences
children.top_down_role: Sparsity, degeneracy, reconstruction, plus numerical effects of representation conversion.

assumptions_latex: The substitution is \(x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-\) with \(x_j^+,x_j^-\ge0\).
Feasibility and objective values depend on the pair only through its difference.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each fixed \(x_j\) has representations \((x_j^++t,x_j^-+t)\) for every \(t\ge0\); hence recovery is unique but the split representation is not.

notation.meaning: Original free variable and its nonnegative split components.
Common nonnegative increment applied to both split components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Surjectivity, nonuniqueness, and recovery consequences of free-variable splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-\), every \(x_j\in\mathbb R\) has at least one nonnegative representation, for example \(x_j^+=\max\{x_j,0\}\) and \(x_j^-=\max\{-x_j,0\}\). The representation is nonunique: if \((x_j^+,x_j^-)\) represents \(x_j\), then \((x_j^++t,x_j^-+t)\) does also for every \(t\ge0\). Consequently, the two generated matrix columns are negatives and the split formulation has a null direction \((1,1)\) in these coordinates. Postsolve recovery \(x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-\) is nevertheless unique and preserves feasibility and objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting is surjective but nonunique: increasing both parts equally changes neither the recovered variable, row activities, nor the objective value.
knowledge_statements.title: Free-to-Split Mapping Consequences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated surjectivity, nonuniqueness, null direction, and recovery consequences are coherent, but the supplied locator does not inspectably support these properties.

children.title: Slack-Variable Representations
children.top_down_role: Internal representations associated with inequality rows using nonnegative slack variables.

assumptions_latex: The row is \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\).
A new variable \(s_i\) is constrained by \(s_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\iff \exists s_i\ge0:\ a_i^{\mathsf T}x+s_i=b_i\), with unique \(s_i=b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x\).

notation.meaning: Row coefficient vector and right-hand side.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality representation of a less-than-or-equal row using nonnegative slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a row \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\), introduce a slack variable \(s_i\ge0\) and replace the inequality by \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+s_i=b_i\). For every feasible \(x\), the extension is unique, namely \(s_i=b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge0\). Conversely, every pair \((x,s_i)\) satisfying the equality and nonnegativity condition has \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\). Thus projection onto the original variables gives exactly the original feasible set. The slack has zero objective coefficient unless the model explicitly assigns it a cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A less-than-or-equal row becomes an equality by adding a nonnegative slack equal to the unused right-hand-side capacity.
knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Variable Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The slack-variable equivalence and uniqueness formula are correct, but the cited locator does not inspectably support the representation. The objective-coefficient qualification also needs a source clarifying that equivalence to the original LP requires zero auxiliary cost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inequality-to-equality conversion, the resulting slack-column basis, and the feasibility boundary for simplex initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A x\le b\), introducing \(s\ge0\) gives the equivalent system \(A x+s=b\), with slack columns \(I_m\). If \(b\ge0\), setting the structural variables to zero gives the basic feasible solution \((x,s)=(0,b)\); when the slack-variable costs are zero, these variables contribute zero to the objective. For \(A x\ge b\), introducing \(s\ge0\) gives \(A x-s=b\), with columns \(-I_m\). The corresponding basic assignment at \(x=0\) is \(s=-b\), which is infeasible if any component of \(b\) is positive; when \(b=0\), it is instead a degenerate feasible assignment. Thus surplus-variable columns generally do not provide a feasible simplex start, and artificial columns may be required. Mixed \(\le\), \(\ge\), and equality rows are converted row by row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a nonnegative slack converts a less-than-or-equal row to an equality and supplies identity columns. With a nonnegative right-hand side, setting the original variables to zero gives the slack basic feasible solution s = b; zero slack costs give no objective contribution. Subtracting a nonnegative surplus variable converts a greater-than-or-equal row, but its negative-identity basis gives s = -b at x = 0 and is infeasible whenever some right-hand side is positive. The all-zero right-hand-side case is a degenerate exception. Artificial columns may therefore be needed for initialization.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n},\quad x\in\mathbb{R}^n_+,\quad s\in\mathbb{R}^m_+
b\ge0\ \text{for the stated slack-basis initialization}
c_s=0\ \text{only for the zero objective contribution of slack variables}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A x\le b\iff \exists s\ge0:\ A x+s=b;\qquad A x\ge b\iff \exists s\ge0:\ A x-s=b,\quad s\big|_{x=0}=-b.

source_evidence.locator: The Simplex Computational Procedure / 4. A First Feasible Solution Using Slack Variables / Definition 4-extra-1

source_refs.locator: The Simplex Computational Procedure / 4. A First Feasible Solution Using Slack Variables / Definition 4-extra-1

knowledge_statements.title: Slack-variable conversion and slack-basis initialization

children.title: Surplus-Variable Representations
children.top_down_role: Internal representations associated with inequality rows using surplus variables.

assumptions_latex: The row is \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i\).
A new variable \(r_i\) is constrained by \(r_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i\iff \exists r_i\ge0:\ a_i^{\mathsf T}x-r_i=b_i\), with unique \(r_i=a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\).

notation.meaning: Row coefficient vector and right-hand side.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality representation of a greater-than-or-equal row using nonnegative surplus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a row \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i\), introduce a surplus variable \(r_i\ge0\) and replace the inequality by \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-r_i=b_i\). For every feasible \(x\), the extension is unique, namely \(r_i=a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\ge0\). Conversely, every pair \((x,r_i)\) satisfying the equality and nonnegativity condition has \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i\). Thus projection onto the original variables recovers exactly the original feasible set. Negating the original row converts this construction into the corresponding slack-variable representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A greater-than-or-equal row becomes an equality by subtracting a nonnegative surplus equal to the amount above its lower limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Surplus-Variable Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The surplus-variable representation is mathematically correct and fits the leaf, but the supplied locator does not inspectably support it.

children.title: Ranged-Row Representations
children.top_down_role: Storage, transformation, plus recovery choices for rows bounded on both sides.

assumptions_latex: The ranged row is \(L_i\le a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le U_i\), with finite \(L_i\le U_i\).
A row variable \(s_i\) is introduced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ranged row is equivalent to \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+s_i=U_i\) with \(0\le s_i\le U_i-L_i\).

notation.meaning: Finite lower and upper row bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single bounded-slack representation of a two-sided finite row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A ranged row \(L_i\le a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le U_i\), where \(L_i\) and \(U_i\) are finite and \(L_i\le U_i\), is equivalently represented by \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+s_i=U_i\) and \(0\le s_i\le U_i-L_i\). For each feasible \(x\), the auxiliary value is uniquely \(s_i=U_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x\). Its lower bound enforces the upper row bound, and its upper bound enforces the lower row bound. Alternatively, the ranged row may be stored as two inequalities, but the bounded-slack form uses one equality row and one auxiliary variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent a finite two-sided row by one equality and a slack bounded between zero and the row range.
knowledge_statements.title: Ranged-Row Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-slack representation of a finite ranged row is correct and appropriately classified, but the cited locator does not inspectably support it or the alternative-storage claim.

children.title: Empty-Row Reductions
children.top_down_role: Feasibility classification plus removal handling for rows without structural coefficients.

assumptions_latex: A constraint row has coefficient vector \(a_i=0\) and relation \(0\mathrel{\rho_i}b_i\).
The relation \(\rho_i\) is one of \(\le\), \(=\), or \(\ge\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Delete the row when \(0\mathrel{\rho_i}b_i\) is true; otherwise certify primal infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Zero row coefficient vector, right-hand side, and row relation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Presolve treatment of a structurally empty constraint row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an empty row \(a_i=0\), evaluate the scalar predicate \(0\mathrel{\rho_i}b_i\). If it is true, the row is redundant for every assignment of the variables and may be deleted. If it is false, no assignment can satisfy the row, so presolve terminates with a primal-infeasibility certificate consisting of the empty row, its right-hand side, and its relation. In particular, \(0\le b_i\) requires \(b_i\ge0\), \(0\ge b_i\) requires \(b_i\le0\), and \(0=b_i\) requires \(b_i=0\). A deleted row must be recorded for postsolve diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate an empty row as a constant predicate: delete it if true, and otherwise report primal infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty-Row Reductions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The empty-row reduction is correct, but the supplied locator does not inspectably support the reduction or the characterization of the inconsistent row record as a primal-infeasibility certificate.

children.title: Empty-Column Reductions
children.top_down_role: Objective, bound, unboundedness, plus removal handling for columns without structural coefficients.

assumptions_latex: The LP is a minimization problem and column \(A_{:j}=0\).
The variable domain is the nonempty closed interval \([\ell_j,u_j]\) with extended-real endpoints.
The variable contributes \(c_jx_j\) to the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fix \(x_j=\ell_j\) if \(c_j>0\), fix \(x_j=u_j\) if \(c_j<0\), and choose any feasible value if \(c_j=0\); a required infinite endpoint certifies unboundedness.

notation.meaning: Empty matrix column and its objective coefficient.
Extended-real lower and upper variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Presolve optimization and removal of a variable absent from every row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a minimization LP, suppose \(A_{:j}=0\) and \(\ell_j\le x_j\le u_j\). Since \(x_j\) affects no row, minimize \(c_jx_j\) over its bounds independently. If \(c_j>0\) and \(\ell_j\) is finite, fix \(x_j=\ell_j\); if \(\ell_j=-\infty\), certify objective unboundedness. If \(c_j<0\) and \(u_j\) is finite, fix \(x_j=u_j\); if \(u_j=+\infty\), certify unboundedness. If \(c_j=0\), choose any feasible value. Delete the column, update the objective constant, and store the selected value for postsolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize an empty column solely over its bounds, fixing it at the favorable endpoint or reporting unboundedness when that endpoint is infinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty-Column Reductions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The empty-column case analysis is correct for a minimization LP with a nonempty bound domain, but the cited locator does not inspectably support the endpoint fixing, unboundedness conclusions, or postsolve update.

children.title: Empty-Structure Postsolve Records
children.top_down_role: Reconstruction records needed after empty rows or columns are removed.

knowledge_statements.title: Empty-Structure Postsolve Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records for exact postsolve reversal of empty-row and empty-column presolve steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An empty-row record stores the row index, \(L_i\), \(U_i\), and whether \(L_i\le 0\le U_i\); failure of this condition is an infeasibility certificate. An empty-column record stores the column index and \((\ell_j,u_j,c_j)\). For minimization, postsolve assigns \(x_j=\ell_j\) when \(c_j>0\), assigns \(x_j=u_j\) when \(c_j<0\), and selects any \(x_j\in[\ell_j,u_j]\) when \(c_j=0\). If \(c_j>0\) and \(\ell_j=-\infty\), or if \(c_j<0\) and \(u_j=+\infty\), the record instead reports primal unboundedness below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The record retains the removed index, relevant bounds, cost, and status. It restores an optimal empty-column value or reports the infeasibility or unboundedness detected by an empty structure.
assumptions_latex: The LP is \(\min\{c^\top x:L\le Ax\le U,\;\ell\le x\le u\}\), with extended-real bounds.
An empty row has no nonzero coefficients, and an empty column has no nonzero coefficients.
Every variable interval satisfies \(\ell_j\le u_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stored data reconstruct an optimal removed empty-column component or retain the corresponding empty-structure infeasibility or unboundedness certificate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct feasibility and objective analysis of zero rows and columns

assumptions_latex: The LP is \(\min\{c^\top x:L\le Ax\le U,\;\ell\le x\le u\}\).
For some column \(j\), \(\ell_j=u_j=v\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating \(x_j\) by substitution preserves feasibility and shifts every feasible objective value by \(c_jv\).

notation.meaning: column j of the constraint matrix

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact substitution of a fixed coordinate in a linear program
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination of a variable whose lower and upper bounds coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(x_j=v\), delete column \(j\), and replace the row bounds by \(L'=L-vA_{:j}\) and \(U'=U-vA_{:j}\). Delete the bounds on \(x_j\) and add \(c_jv\) to the objective constant. The reduced problem is \(\min\{c_{-j}^{\top}x_{-j}+c_jv:L'\le A_{:-j}x_{-j}\le U',\;\ell_{-j}\le x_{-j}\le u_{-j}\}\). If a shifted interval is empty, report infeasibility. Otherwise solve the reduced problem and reconstruct the original solution by inserting \(x_j=v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substitute the fixed value into every affected row and the objective, remove the variable, and restore that value during postsolve.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Variable Elimination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-variable substitution algorithm is mathematically consistent and fits the leaf, but the record supplies no inspectable citation for this presolve rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Singleton-Row Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound propagation and removal for a row containing one active variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(\alpha=\min\{L_i/a_{ij},U_i/a_{ij}\}\) and \(\beta=\max\{L_i/a_{ij},U_i/a_{ij}\}\), using well-defined extended-real arithmetic. Set \(\ell'_j=\max\{\ell_j,\alpha\}\) and \(u'_j=\min\{u_j,\beta\}\). If \(\ell'_j>u'_j\), report infeasibility. Otherwise replace the bounds of \(x_j\) by \([\ell'_j,u'_j]\), delete row \(i\), and record the previous bounds for postsolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singleton row yields an interval for its sole variable. Intersect it with the existing interval, report infeasibility if the intersection is empty, and otherwise remove the row.
assumptions_latex: Row \(i\) has exactly one nonzero coefficient \(a_{ij}\ne0\).
The row is \(L_i\le a_{ij}x_j\le U_i\), with \(x_j\in[\ell_j,u_j]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \([\ell_j,u_j]\) by its intersection with the row-implied interval and deleting row \(i\) preserves the feasible set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: division of a singleton linear inequality by a nonzero coefficient

assumptions_latex: Column \(j\) occurs only in equality row \(a_{ij}x_j+\sum_{k\ne j}a_{ik}x_k=b_i\), where \(a_{ij}\ne0\).
The variable satisfies \(\ell_j\le x_j\le u_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Substitution removes row \(i\) and column \(j\) while preserving feasible solutions and objective values under the recorded reconstruction map.

notation.meaning: row activity excluding the singleton column

children.title: Duplicate-Row Reductions
children.top_down_role: Detection, compatibility, retention, plus reconstruction issues for repeated or proportional rows.

assumptions_latex: Rows \(i\) and \(k\) satisfy \(A_{k:}=\gamma A_{i:}\) for some \(\gamma\ne0\).
Their bounds are \(L_i\le A_{i:}x\le U_i\) and \(L_k\le A_{k:}x\le U_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two proportional rows are equivalent to one row whose interval is the intersection of their normalized intervals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact consolidation of proportional constraint rows with possibly different bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Normalize row \(k\) to the activity \(A_{i:}x\). If \(\gamma>0\), set \((\widehat L_k,\widehat U_k)=(L_k/\gamma,U_k/\gamma)\); if \(\gamma<0\), set \((\widehat L_k,\widehat U_k)=(U_k/\gamma,L_k/\gamma)\). Replace row \(i\)'s interval by \([L',U']=[\max\{L_i,\widehat L_k\},\min\{U_i,\widehat U_k\}]\). If \(L'>U'\), the pair certifies infeasibility. Otherwise retain one row with interval \([L',U']\), delete the other, and record the proportionality factor and original intervals for dual postsolve reconstruction.

children.title: Duplicate-Column Reductions
children.top_down_role: Bound-aware treatment of repeated or proportional columns with objective implications.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Column Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient exact aggregation rule for proportional columns and costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce \(z=x_p+\gamma x_q\), with \(\ell_z=\ell_p+\min\{\gamma\ell_q,\gamma u_q\}\) and \(u_z=u_p+\max\{\gamma\ell_q,\gamma u_q\}\). Replace columns \(p,q\) by column \(A_{:p}\), replace their objective terms by \(c_pz\), and impose \(z\in[\ell_z,u_z]\). Store \(\gamma\) and the two original intervals. During postsolve, choose any \((x_p,x_q)\) in the original box satisfying \(x_p+\gamma x_q=z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proportional columns with proportional costs are replaced by one aggregate variable whose interval is the exact image of their original finite box; postsolve decomposes the aggregate value.
assumptions_latex: Columns \(p\) and \(q\) satisfy \(A_{:q}=\gamma A_{:p}\) for some \(\gamma\ne0\).
Their costs satisfy \(c_q=\gamma c_p\), and their bounds are finite intervals \([\ell_p,u_p]\) and \([\ell_q,u_q]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Aggregation into \(z=x_p+\gamma x_q\) preserves the feasible image and every objective value.

children.title: Row–Column Duplicate Interactions
children.top_down_role: Ordering conflicts plus compounded effects when duplicate structures coexist.

knowledge_statements.title: Row–Column Duplicate Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness and order sensitivity when duplicate-row and duplicate-column passes are interleaved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) and \(C\) be exact duplicate-row and duplicate-column reductions with lifting maps \(L_R\) and \(L_C\). Whenever each reduction's eligibility conditions hold when it is applied, both \(C\circ R\) and \(R\circ C\) preserve feasibility status and optimal value. Their postsolve lifts apply stored maps in reverse order: \(L_R\circ L_C\) for \(C\circ R\), and \(L_C\circ L_R\) for \(R\circ C\). A structural reduction can expose additional duplicate patterns, so row-first and column-first pipelines need not execute the same later reductions or produce identical reduced matrices. Duplicate eligibility must therefore be recomputed after structural changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact row and column duplicate reductions compose correctly, with postsolve records reversed. Their order can expose different later duplicate opportunities and therefore need not yield identical reduced matrices.
assumptions_latex: Each applied duplicate-row or duplicate-column reduction preserves feasibility status and optimal value and has a valid lift for reduced feasible solutions.
Eligibility is checked against the current matrix before every reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any finite composition of eligible exact duplicate reductions is valid, although different application orders may expose different subsequent reductions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: closure of exact equivalence transformations under composition

knowledge_statements.title: Dependent-Equation Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact consistency test for a linearly dependent equality row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a dependence certificate \(A_{k:}=\sum_{i\ne k}\lambda_iA_{i:}\), compare \(b_k\) with \(\sum_{i\ne k}\lambda_i b_i\). If they are equal, row \(k\) is redundant and may be deleted, with \(\lambda\) stored for dual reconstruction. If they differ, the certificate establishes infeasibility of the equality subsystem. A tolerance-based numerical rank decision must not be reported as an exact certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dependent equation is removable when its right-hand side obeys the same dependence. A mismatch is an exact infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: The equality subsystem is \(Ax=b\).
For row \(k\), coefficients \(\lambda_i\) satisfy \(A_{k:}=\sum_{i\ne k}\lambda_iA_{i:}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Row \(k\) is removable exactly when \(b_k=\sum_{i\ne k}\lambda_i b_i\); otherwise the equality subsystem is infeasible.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: consistency criterion for a linearly dependent equation

knowledge_statements.title: Dominated-Column Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient dominance reduction for identical columns in nonnegative standard form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x_q=0\) and remove column \(q\). For postsolve, retain \(x_q=0\); any original feasible point can be represented after the reduction by transferring its former value of \(x_q\) to \(x_p\). Under the stated assumptions, this transfer preserves \(Ax=b\), respects nonnegativity and the bounds of \(x_p\), and does not increase the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For identical nonnegative columns, fix the costlier column to zero and transfer its value to the no-more-expensive column that has no finite upper bound.
assumptions_latex: The LP is \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\;x\ge0\}\).
Columns \(p,q\) satisfy \(A_{:p}=A_{:q}\), variable \(x_p\) has no finite upper bound, and \(c_p\le c_q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Imposing \(x_q=0\) and removing column \(q\) leaves the infimum unchanged.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasible mass transfer between identical nonnegative columns

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Constraint Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact redundancy certificate obtained from minimum and maximum row activity over the remaining system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\underline\alpha_i=\inf\{a_i^\top x:x\in P_{-i}\}\) and \(\overline\alpha_i=\sup\{a_i^\top x:x\in P_{-i}\}\), allowing infinite values. Row \(i\) is redundant exactly when \(\underline\alpha_i\ge L_i\) and \(\overline\alpha_i\le U_i\). A certified lower bound \(d_i^-\le\underline\alpha_i\) with \(d_i^-\ge L_i\), together with a certified upper bound \(d_i^+\ge\overline\alpha_i\) with \(d_i^+\le U_i\), is a sufficient checkable redundancy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A row is redundant exactly when its minimum and maximum activity under all other constraints lie within its interval. Certified bounds enclosing those extrema can establish redundancy.
assumptions_latex: The set \(P_{-i}\ne\varnothing\) is defined by all variable bounds and constraints except row \(i\).
The omitted row is \(L_i\le a_i^\top x\le U_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Row \(i\) is redundant if and only if \(\inf_{x\in P_{-i}}a_i^\top x\ge L_i\) and \(\sup_{x\in P_{-i}}a_i^\top x\le U_i\).

notation.meaning: certified lower and upper bounds on the two activity extrema

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact optimization characterization of implication by the remaining constraints

knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Based Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact box-activity propagation for tightening one variable from a ranged linear constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(m_{ij}=\sum_{k\ne j}\min\{a_{ik}\ell_k,a_{ik}u_k\}\) and \(M_{ij}=\sum_{k\ne j}\max\{a_{ik}\ell_k,a_{ik}u_k\}\). Form the necessary interval \(L_i-M_{ij}\le a_{ij}x_j\le U_i-m_{ij}\), divide by \(a_{ij}\) with endpoint order reversed when \(a_{ij}<0\), and intersect the resulting interval with \([\ell_j,u_j]\). Report infeasibility if the intersection is empty; otherwise replace the bound of \(x_j\) by the intersection and record row \(i\) as its justification. The exact update may be repeated until a fixed point is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual minimum and maximum row activities give a necessary interval for one variable. Intersect it with the current interval, reporting infeasibility if the result is empty, and repeat exact updates as desired.
assumptions_latex: A row is \(L_i\le\sum_k a_{ik}x_k\le U_i\), with box bounds \(\ell_k\le x_k\le u_k\).
For the updated variable \(j\), \(a_{ij}\ne0\).
The residual extrema \(m_{ij}\) and \(M_{ij}\), and the endpoint differences used in the update, are well-defined in the adopted extended-real arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Intersecting the current bound of \(x_j\) with \(\{t:L_i-M_{ij}\le a_{ij}t\le U_i-m_{ij}\}\) is a valid bound tightening.

notation.meaning: minimum residual row activity excluding variable j
maximum residual row activity excluding variable j

children.title: Implied-Bound Detection
children.top_down_role: Identification, strength, provenance, plus safe use of bounds inferred from model structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Implied-Bound Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact semantic criterion for detecting whether a variable bound follows from the remaining LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_{-j}^{U}\) retain all constraints and variable bounds except \(x_j\le u_j\), and let \(P_{-j}^{L}\) retain all constraints and variable bounds except \(x_j\ge\ell_j\). Assuming the tested set is nonempty, define \(\overline x_j=\sup\{x_j:x\in P_{-j}^{U}\}\) and \(\underline x_j=\inf\{x_j:x\in P_{-j}^{L}\}\). The upper bound is implied exactly when \(\overline x_j\le u_j\), and the lower bound is implied exactly when \(\underline x_j\ge\ell_j\). An upper bound on \(\overline x_j\) or a lower bound on \(\underline x_j\) gives a sufficient certified test. An infinite extremum disproves implication of the corresponding finite bound; emptiness of a tested set is reported separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Test each variable bound by optimizing that coordinate after removing only that bound. The bound is implied exactly when the resulting extremum cannot cross it.
assumptions_latex: The upper-bound test set \(P_{-j}^{U}\) omits only \(x_j\le u_j\), and the lower-bound test set \(P_{-j}^{L}\) omits only \(x_j\ge\ell_j\).
All other constraints and variable bounds remain enforced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The upper bound is implied exactly when \(\sup_{x\in P_{-j}^{U}}x_j\le u_j\), and the lower bound is implied exactly when \(\inf_{x\in P_{-j}^{L}}x_j\ge\ell_j\), provided the corresponding test set is nonempty.

notation.meaning: feasible regions with the tested upper or lower bound omitted
coordinate extrema in the lower- and upper-bound test sets

children.title: Implied-Free Detection
children.top_down_role: Identification of variables whose explicit limits become unnecessary under remaining constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Implied-Free Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasible-set criterion for removing both explicit bounds of one LP variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ l\le x\le u\}\). For index \(j\), remove only the bounds on \(x_j\) and define \(F^{-j}=\{x:Ax\le b,\ l_i\le x_i\le u_i\text{ for }i\ne j\}\). Variable \(x_j\) is implied free precisely when \[F^{-j}\subseteq\{x:l_j\le x_j\le u_j\}.\] Equivalently, deleting both explicit bounds on \(x_j\) leaves the feasible set unchanged: \(F^{-j}=F\). Sound detection may establish the containment using exact row implications or conservative outward-rounded activity bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable is implied free when all other constraints already enforce both of its explicit bounds, so deleting those bounds does not change feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(l,u\in\overline{\mathbb R}^n\) with \(l\le u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^{-j}=F\), so both explicit bounds on \(x_j\) are redundant.

notation.meaning: Feasible region after removing only the explicit bounds on variable j.

children.title: Implied-Status Ambiguities
children.top_down_role: Numerical or structural cases where implied-bound versus implied-free classification is unreliable.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(l,u\in\overline{\mathbb R}^n\) with \(l\le u\).
All status comparisons use exact arithmetic or certified directed rounding.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: distinction between exact redundancy and incomplete interval propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact implied status and conclusions obtained from incomplete propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F^{-j}=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ l_i\le x_i\le u_i\text{ for every }i\ne j\}\). The lower bound is implied when \(\inf_{x\in F^{-j}}x_j\ge l_j\), and the upper bound is implied when \(\sup_{x\in F^{-j}}x_j\le u_j\). Both predicates may hold simultaneously, including when the remaining constraints fix \(x_j\). Row-wise interval propagation supplies only sufficient tests for these global predicates: failure to derive either inequality does not prove that the corresponding bound is essential. Consequently, implementations must distinguish proven implied-free, proven one-sided implied-bound, and undetermined status, especially when infinite activities or numerical tolerances prevent a certified comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower or upper bound is exactly implied when all points satisfying the other constraints obey it. Both statuses can hold simultaneously, while incomplete interval propagation may prove neither; an inconclusive test is not proof that a bound is necessary.

children.title: Forcing-Constraint Reductions
children.top_down_role: Variable fixation plus row removal opportunities created by forcing constraint activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Forcing-Constraint Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box-activity forcing rule for a single linear inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a row \(a^Tx\le\beta\), compute the minimum box activity \(L=\sum_i\min\{a_il_i,a_iu_i\}\). If \(L>\beta\), declare infeasibility. If \(L=\beta\), the row is forcing: for every \(i\) with \(a_i>0\), fix \(x_i=l_i\), and for every \(i\) with \(a_i<0\), fix \(x_i=u_i\); zero coefficients are unchanged. Apply the symmetric rule to \(a^Tx\ge\alpha\) using the maximum activity \(U=\sum_i\max\{a_il_i,a_iu_i\}\). Record every fixing so a solution can be reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an inequality permits only the activity-minimizing or activity-maximizing corner of the variable box, presolve fixes every participating variable at that corner.
assumptions_latex: Every activity term used in an equality test is finite and evaluated exactly or with certified rounding.
Variables satisfy \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated fixings preserve exactly the feasible points satisfying the forcing row and the box.

notation.meaning: Minimum and maximum row activities over the current variable box.

children.title: Tight-Constraint Reductions
children.top_down_role: Reductions supported by constraints whose attainable activity reaches a limiting bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Tight-Constraint Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-activity bound propagation from a nearly tight inequality row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a^Tx\le\beta\) and index \(j\), compute \(L_{-j}=\sum_{i\ne j}\min\{a_il_i,a_iu_i\}\). If \(a_j>0\), replace \(u_j\) by \(\min\{u_j,(\beta-L_{-j})/a_j\}\); if \(a_j<0\), replace \(l_j\) by \(\max\{l_j,(\beta-L_{-j})/a_j\}\). Empty updated intervals certify infeasibility. Repeat the symmetric calculation for lower-bounded rows using maximum residual activity. Stop when no certified bound improvement occurs, and retain a reversible record of deleted or tightened bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual row activity yields valid bounds on each participating variable; presolve tightens those bounds and detects infeasibility if an interval becomes empty.
assumptions_latex: Residual activities are finite and computed with outward rounding when arithmetic is inexact.
The current bounds satisfy \(l_i\le u_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each updated bound is valid for every point satisfying the original row and current box.

notation.meaning: Minimum activity of the row excluding variable j.

children.title: Forcing–Tight Overlap Cases
children.top_down_role: Classification, ordering, plus reconstruction issues when both reduction patterns apply.

knowledge_statements.title: Forcing–Tight Overlap Cases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relationship between forcing rows and per-variable tight bound propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(a^Tx\le\beta\) with finite minimum activity \(L\). If \(L=\beta\), then for every \(j\) with \(a_j\ne0\), residual-activity propagation returns the activity-minimizing endpoint: \((\beta-L_{-j})/a_j=l_j\) when \(a_j>0\), and \((\beta-L_{-j})/a_j=u_j\) when \(a_j<0\). Thus a forcing-row reduction is simultaneously a collection of tight single-variable implications. An implementation may apply either route, but duplicate fixings must share one reconstruction-consistent explanation and must not be counted as independent reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forcing row makes every nonzero variable implication tight at its activity-minimizing bound, so forcing and ordinary bound-propagation reductions overlap.
assumptions_latex: All relevant bounds and row-activity terms are finite.
Equality \(L=\beta\) is certified.

children.title: Presolve Infeasibility Detection
children.top_down_role: Structural plus bound-based evidence supporting an infeasible presolve status.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Infeasibility Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally checkable infeasibility certificates produced by bound and row propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Presolve may certify infeasibility if it derives either an empty variable interval \(l_j>u_j\), or a row contradiction. For \(a^Tx\le\beta\), the latter is \(L=\sum_i\min\{a_il_i,a_iu_i\}>\beta\); for \(a^Tx\ge\alpha\), it is \(U=\sum_i\max\{a_il_i,a_iu_i\}<\alpha\). Because every box-feasible point has activity in \([L,U]\), the violated comparison is a directly checkable certificate. When reductions preceded detection, the solver must retain mappings showing that the certified bounds and row are valid consequences of the original LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empty variable interval or an impossible row-activity interval certifies infeasibility, provided all propagated bounds remain traceable to the original LP.

Every preceding reduction is feasibility preserving and has a valid reconstruction record.

children.title: Presolve Unboundedness Detection
children.top_down_role: Objective-improving structural evidence supporting an unbounded presolve status.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Unboundedness Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal feasible-ray certificate for unboundedness of a minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization LP \(\inf\{c^Tx:Ax\le b,\ l\le x\le u\}\), presolve certifies unboundedness by producing a feasible point \(\bar x\) and a nonzero direction \(d\) such that \(Ad\le0\), \(c^Td<0\), \(d_i=0\) whenever both \(l_i\) and \(u_i\) are finite, \(d_i\ge0\) whenever \(u_i=+\infty\) and \(l_i\) is finite, and \(d_i\le0\) whenever \(l_i=-\infty\) and \(u_i\) is finite. Then \(\bar x+td\) is feasible for every \(t\ge0\), while its objective tends to \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point plus a bound-compatible improving recession direction is a checkable certificate that a minimization LP is unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) satisfies every original constraint and bound.
The direction and objective comparisons are verified in exact or certified arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{c^Tx:Ax\le b,\ l\le x\le u\}=-\infty\).

notation.meaning: Feasible base point for the ray.

children.title: Infeasible-or-Unbounded Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Cases where transformations do not safely distinguish the two terminal statuses.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-or-Unbounded Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary when presolve lacks either a feasibility or an unboundedness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An improving recession direction \(d\) satisfying \(Ad\le0\) and \(c^Td<0\) does not alone certify unboundedness: a feasible base point must also exist. Conversely, failure to construct such a base point is not an infeasibility certificate. Therefore a presolve pipeline that derives an improving direction but neither reconstructs a feasible point nor derives an explicit contradiction may report only infeasible-or-unbounded. It may report infeasible only with a valid contradiction certificate, and unbounded only with a feasible-point-plus-ray certificate mapped to the original LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An improving direction without a feasible base point distinguishes neither infeasibility nor unboundedness; a definite status requires the corresponding complete certificate.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a linear minimization problem.
No independent feasibility or infeasibility certificate has been established.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The available information supports only the disjunctive status \(\text{infeasible}\lor\text{unbounded}\).
