children.title: Constraint Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Combined-row structures used to support elimination or stronger presolve simplification.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence-preserving aggregation of equality rows and implication-only aggregation of inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equality constraints \(Ex=f\), replacing them by \(MEx=Mf\) preserves their solution set whenever \(M\) is square and nonsingular. More generally, appending \(\lambda^TEx=\lambda^Tf\) for any multiplier \(\lambda\) adds only a redundant equality. For inequalities \(Ax\le b\), every multiplier \(\lambda\ge0\) yields the valid aggregate \(\lambda^TAx\le\lambda^Tb\), but that aggregate generally cannot replace its source rows without enlarging the feasible set. Hence deletion after aggregation requires a separate implication or invertibility certificate; aggregation alone supplies only a valid consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible row operations preserve equalities exactly. Nonnegative combinations of inequalities are valid consequences but ordinarily cannot replace their source constraints.
assumptions_latex: All rows are linear over \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality aggregation is equivalent under nonsingular row transformation; inequality aggregation is implication-preserving under nonnegative multipliers.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary linear row operations and nonnegative inequality aggregation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between invertible equality transformations and implication-only nonnegative inequality aggregation is correct. The representation kind is suitable for this equivalence-focused statement, but an inspectable source is missing.

children.title: Aggregation Fill-Growth Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Sparsity loss, coefficient growth, plus reconstruction costs that limit aggregation.

assumptions_latex: Fill is counted structurally, with exact zero cancellations removed only after coefficient computation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structural fill increase is bounded by \(q(|S|-1)\), and unrestricted repeated elimination may cause densification.

notation.meaning: Support of the equality used for elimination.
Number of other rows containing the eliminated variable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural boundary limiting substitution or row aggregation when nonzeros proliferate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an equality with support \(S\) is used to eliminate \(x_j\), and \(x_j\) occurs in \(q\) other rows. Each affected row can acquire nonzeros only in \(S\setminus\{j\}\), so the total number of newly created matrix entries is at most \(q(|S|-1)\), before cancellations and excluding the replaced occurrences of \(x_j\). This bound is attainable when the affected rows have supports disjoint from \(S\setminus\{j\}\) and no cancellation occurs. Therefore unrestricted substitution can transform a sparse matrix into a dense one; a fill-limited presolver must reject or defer pivots whose predicted or realized fill exceeds its declared threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating a variable occurring in many rows can add up to the pivot-row width minus one in each affected row, potentially destroying sparsity.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation Fill-Growth Boundaries

children.title: Coefficient Elimination
children.top_down_role: Removal of selected coefficients through safe structural transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fourier–Motzkin elimination of one variable from linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To eliminate \(x_j\) from \(Ax\le b\), partition rows into \(P=\{r:a_{rj}>0\}\), \(N=\{s:a_{sj}<0\}\), and \(Z=\{t:a_{tj}=0\}\). Retain every row in \(Z\). For each \((r,s)\in P\times N\), form the nonnegative aggregate \[\frac{1}{a_{rj}}(a_r^Tx\le b_r)+\frac{-1}{a_{sj}}(a_s^Tx\le b_s),\] whose coefficient of \(x_j\) is zero. Delete the original rows in \(P\cup N\). The resulting inequalities describe exactly the projection of the original polyhedron onto the coordinates other than \(j\), although up to \(|P||N|\) generated rows may require redundancy removal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fourier–Motzkin elimination combines every positive-coefficient row with every negative-coefficient row, cancels one variable, and exactly represents the projected polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: The system consists solely of non-strict linear inequalities over real variables.
Arithmetic is exact, or generated inequalities are conservatively rounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced system equals the coordinate projection of \(\{x:Ax\le b\}\) after eliminating \(x_j\).

notation.meaning: Rows with positive, negative, and zero coefficients on the eliminated variable.

source_refs.locator: 2.8. Projections of polyhedra: Fourier-Motzkin elimination* p. 70

source_witnesses.locator: 2.8. Projections of polyhedra: Fourier-Motzkin elimination* p. 70

children.title: Matrix Sparsification
children.top_down_role: Reduction of matrix density while preserving recoverable solver behavior.

assumptions_latex: The LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\).
Every deleted coefficient is certified redundant by an exact implication from retained rows and bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced LP has the same feasible objective values as the original LP, and its solutions can be lifted by the recorded transformations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact presolve sparsification, not numerical dropping of merely small coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the LP \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\), inspect a candidate entry \(a_{ij}\ne0\). Delete or replace that entry only when an exact certificate shows that the modified row, together with retained rows and bounds, defines the same feasible set after a recorded affine reconstruction. Applying certified edits produces \(\widetilde A\) and a map \(L\) such that every reduced feasible point \(\widetilde x\) lifts to an original feasible point \(L(\widetilde x)\) with \(c^{\mathsf T}L(\widetilde x)=\widetilde c^{\mathsf T}\widetilde x+\gamma\), and every original feasible point has a corresponding reduced point. Output the reduced LP and the ordered reconstruction records.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix sparsification removes coefficients only with exact certificates preserving feasibility and objective values, while recording how reduced solutions are reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Sparsification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but no source supports this particular coefficient-edit procedure or its claimed bidirectional reconstruction. The transformed cost, objective offset, reduced-variable space, and exact certificate form are not introduced sufficiently to make the guarantee reliable.

children.title: Sparsification Safety Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Coefficient growth, conditioning, fill redistribution, plus reversibility limits.

assumptions_latex: Presolve must preserve feasibility status and the optimal value, up to a recorded objective constant.
Floating-point tolerances are not treated as exact logical implications.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uncertified coefficient deletion is outside the safe boundary because it can alter feasibility or the optimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact sparsification and tolerance-based model perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: No positive magnitude threshold alone makes coefficient deletion exact. For any \(\varepsilon>0\), consider \(\min\{x:\varepsilon x=1,\ x\ge0\}\). Its unique feasible point and optimum are \(x=1/\varepsilon\). Replacing the coefficient \(\varepsilon\) by zero yields the inconsistent constraint \(0=1\), so feasibility is destroyed despite the coefficient being arbitrarily small. Likewise, small deletions can change an optimum when bounds keep the perturbed model feasible. Therefore a sparsification is safe only when each edit follows from an exact redundancy, bound, or substitution certificate and the associated primal and dual reconstruction maps are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No universal small-coefficient threshold is exact: deleting an arbitrarily small entry can destroy feasibility or change the optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparsification Safety Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly shows that coefficient magnitude alone cannot justify exact deletion, and failure_boundary fits the container. An authoritative presolve source is still needed for the broader claim that the listed certificate and reconstruction conditions characterize safe sparsification.

children.title: Primal Reduction Pairings
children.top_down_role: Related transformations viewed through primal variables, rows, bounds, plus objectives.

assumptions_latex: The primal LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
Each reduction is exact and carries an affine primal reconstruction map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A primal reduction is paired with the transformation of the dual constraint indexed by the same primal component.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise pairings for exact primal presolve reductions in equality form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal-dual pair \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), each primal variable \(x_j\) is paired with the dual equation and slack \(a_j^{\mathsf T}y+s_j=c_j\), while each primal equation is paired with one component of \(y\). Thus fixing or eliminating \(x_j\) requires deleting or transforming its paired dual equation and recording recovery of \(s_j\); deleting an exactly redundant primal equation requires a compatible reconstruction of its dual multiplier. A valid pairing preserves primal feasibility, objective offsets, and complementary products \(x_js_j\) after reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal variables pair with dual slack equations, and primal rows pair with dual multipliers; exact reductions must transform and reconstruct those paired objects consistently.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Reduction Pairings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The component indexing follows standard primal-dual structure, but no evidence supports the asserted presolve operations and reconstruction requirements. Preservation of each complementary product is stronger than ordinary preservation of feasibility and optimality and requires precise hypotheses.

children.title: Dual Reduction Pairings
children.top_down_role: Counterpart transformations viewed through dual variables, constraints, plus reduced costs.

assumptions_latex: The dual LP is \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
Each reduction is exact and carries a dual reconstruction map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A dual reduction is paired with the transformation of the primal component sharing its constraint or multiplier index.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise pairings for exact dual presolve reductions in equality-form primal-dual LPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the pair \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), the dual slack \(s_j\) and its equation are paired with \(x_j\), and the multiplier \(y_i\) is paired with primal row \(i\). Consequently, fixing or eliminating a dual slack transforms the paired primal variable and its column, whereas eliminating a dual multiplier transforms the paired primal row. An exact dual reduction must provide reconstruction yielding \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), preserve the dual objective up to the recorded primal objective offset, and preserve complementary products \(x_js_j\) for reconstructed solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual slacks pair with primal variables, and dual multipliers pair with primal rows; reduction records must reconstruct feasibility, objectives, and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Reduction Pairings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The basic primal-dual indexing is standard, but the claimed consequences for eliminating slacks or multipliers and preserving individual complementary products need a presolve-specific source and more precise transformation hypotheses.

children.title: Primal–Dual Reduction Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence, sequencing implications, plus reconstruction dependencies across paired reductions.

assumptions_latex: The primal and dual are feasible equality-form LPs with finite common optimum.
The reduction has exact primal and dual reconstruction maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced and original primal-dual systems have corresponding feasible solutions, equal duality gaps, and matching optimality certificates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence of primal and dual reductions through solution reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a reduced primal-dual pair admit maps \(x=P(\widetilde x)\) and \((y,s)=D(\widetilde y,\widetilde s)\). It is an exact primal-dual reduction correspondence when these maps send reduced feasible points to original feasible points, every original feasible point relevant to the optimum has a reduced representative, and \(c^{\mathsf T}P(\widetilde x)=\widetilde c^{\mathsf T}\widetilde x+\gamma\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y=\widetilde b^{\mathsf T}\widetilde y+\gamma\). Hence the gaps satisfy \(g(x,y,s)=\widetilde g(\widetilde x,\widetilde y,\widetilde s)\), so zero-gap optimality and primal or dual infeasibility certificates transfer through the recorded correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact paired reductions reconstruct both sides, preserve objective offsets and duality gaps, and transfer optimality or infeasibility certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Reduction Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited general primal-dual section does not establish the stated reconstruction theorem. The assumptions make both original problems feasible, while the conclusion additionally claims transfer of infeasibility certificates; moreover, maps on feasible points do not by themselves define certificate transformations. The exact correspondence hypotheses and supported conclusion require a presolve-specific source.

children.title: Row Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scale selection plus numerical consequences for constraint rows.

assumptions_latex: The LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\).
The row-scaling matrix \(D_r\) is diagonal with strictly positive entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Row scaling preserves the primal feasible set and objective while dual multipliers reconstruct as \(y=D_r\widehat y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal scaling of equality rows and right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D_r=\operatorname{diag}(r_1,\ldots,r_m)\) with \(r_i>0\), row scaling replaces \(Ax=b\) by \((D_rA)x=D_rb\). Because \(D_r\) is invertible, \((D_rA)x=D_rb\) if and only if \(Ax=b\); bounds and the objective remain unchanged. If the scaled dual equations are \((D_rA)^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+s=c\), define \(y=D_r\widehat y\). Then \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), and \((D_rb)^{\mathsf T}\widehat y=b^{\mathsf T}y\). Thus primal points are unchanged, dual multipliers rescale, and primal-dual objective values and complementarity are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying each row and its right-hand side by a positive factor preserves primal feasibility; dual row multipliers transform by the same diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Row Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The row-scaling identities are mathematically correct for the displayed equality constraints, and representation fits the leaf. A scaling-specific source is absent, and the dual-slack discussion implicitly needs a standard-form sign/domain convention not stated for the bounded-variable LP.

children.title: Column Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scale selection plus numerical consequences for structural columns.

assumptions_latex: The LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\).
The column-scaling matrix \(D_c\) is diagonal with strictly positive entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Column scaling is the substitution \(x=D_c\widehat x\), with consistently transformed objective, bounds, and dual slacks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal change of primal-variable coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_c=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) with \(d_j>0\), and substitute \(x=D_c\widehat x\). The scaled LP is \(\min\{(D_cc)^{\mathsf T}\widehat x:(AD_c)\widehat x=b,\ D_c^{-1}\ell\le\widehat x\le D_c^{-1}u\}\). This substitution is a bijection between the two feasible sets and preserves objective values. If \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), define \(\widehat s=D_cs\); then \((AD_c)^{\mathsf T}y+\widehat s=D_cc\). Moreover, \(\widehat x_j\widehat s_j=x_js_j\), so complementarity is invariant under the coordinate change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive column scaling changes variable coordinates and consistently rescales costs, bounds, and dual slacks without changing feasible objective values or complementarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Column Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primal coordinate substitution, costs, and bounds are correct. However, the displayed dual equation with one nonnegative slack corresponds to a standard-form sign restriction and is incomplete for a general two-sided bounded variable unless bound multipliers and their complementarity relations are introduced.

children.title: Objective Scaling
children.top_down_role: Objective-magnitude control plus implications for tolerances and reported values.

assumptions_latex: The LP has objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x+\beta\).
The objective multiplier \(\alpha\) is strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive objective scaling preserves minimizers and multiplies finite objective differences, dual variables, slacks, and the duality gap by \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive scalar scaling of the entire objective, including its constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing \(c^{\mathsf T}x+\beta\) by \(\alpha(c^{\mathsf T}x+\beta)\), where \(\alpha>0\), leaves the feasible set and the set of minimizers unchanged. Every finite objective value and every objective difference is multiplied by \(\alpha\). For the equality-form dual relation \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), the scaled dual variables \(\widehat y=\alpha y\) and \(\widehat s=\alpha s\) satisfy \(A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+\widehat s=\alpha c\). Consequently, the duality gap is multiplied by \(\alpha\), and unscaled objective values and dual certificates are recovered by division by \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying the full objective by a positive scalar preserves minimizers while scaling objective values, dual variables, slacks, and gaps uniformly.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Positive scaling of the full objective preserves minimizers, but the dual-variable and slack assertions presuppose an equality-form primal with specified variable signs and dual domains. Those assumptions and an authoritative scaling source are missing.

children.title: Bound Scaling
children.top_down_role: Consistent transformation plus recovery of variable limits under column scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation of finite or infinite bounds under positive variable scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the positive substitution \(x_j=d_j\widehat x_j\), where \(d_j>0\), the bound interval \(\ell_j\le x_j\le u_j\) becomes \(\ell_j/d_j\le\widehat x_j\le u_j/d_j\). The conventions \((+\infty)/d_j=+\infty\) and \((-\infty)/d_j=-\infty\) preserve absent bounds. Because \(d_j>0\), inequality directions are unchanged and the mapping is bijective. In an LP with constraint matrix \(A\) and objective coefficient \(c_j\), column \(A_{:j}\) becomes \(d_jA_{:j}\) and the cost coefficient becomes \(d_jc_j\). Primal points transfer by \(\widehat x_j=x_j/d_j\) and reconstruct by \(x_j=d_j\widehat x_j\); bounds must be transformed together with this coordinate change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive variable scaling divides the variable's bounds by the same factor and scales its matrix column and cost, preserving bound feasibility bijectively.
assumptions_latex: A variable \(x_j\) satisfies \(\ell_j\le x_j\le u_j\), where each endpoint may be finite or infinite.
The scaling factor satisfies \(0<d_j<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The substitution \(x_j=d_j\widehat x_j\) transforms the bounds to \(\ell_j/d_j\le\widehat x_j\le u_j/d_j\) and gives a bijection between the original and scaled bound intervals.

notation.meaning: Column of the original constraint matrix associated with the variable
Original objective coefficient of the variable

children.title: Norm-Based Scaling
children.top_down_role: Row or column scale choices derived from selected magnitude norms.

assumptions_latex: The selected row or column has nonzero finite \(p\)-norm.
The norm order satisfies \(1\le p\le\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dividing a component by its nonzero norm normalizes that component to unit \(p\)-norm while preserving LP equivalence under consistent scaling.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-pass or iterative row-column normalization by vector norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\) and \(p\in[1,\infty]\), choose a nonzero row \(a_{i:}\), set \(d_i=\lVert a_{i:}\rVert_p\), and divide that row and its right-hand side by \(d_i\). For a nonzero column \(a_{:j}\), set \(e_j=\lVert a_{:j}\rVert_p\) and apply the variable substitution that divides the column norm by \(e_j\), with corresponding cost and bound transformations. Zero rows or columns are excluded and handled by presolve. A pass outputs \(\widehat A=D_rAD_c\) and the accumulated positive diagonal factors; alternating passes may stop when all eligible norms lie within a prescribed tolerance of one or after a fixed pass limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Norm-based scaling normalizes eligible rows and columns using positive norm factors, accumulates the transformations, and leaves zero components to presolve.
knowledge_statements.title: Norm-Based Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate kind, but the row and column factors are not defined consistently with the final form \(\widehat A=D_rAD_c\). In particular, normalizing a column of norm \(e_j\) requires a column multiplier \(1/e_j\). The iterative stopping tolerance also needs a quantified definition and source.

children.title: Geometric-Mean Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scale choices based on balancing coefficient magnitude ranges.

assumptions_latex: The eligible component contains at least one nonzero coefficient.
Minimum and maximum magnitudes are taken only over its nonzero coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaling by the reciprocal geometric mean maps the smallest and largest nonzero magnitudes to reciprocal values with equal logarithmic distance from one.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extremal-magnitude geometric scaling of nonzero row or column coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an eligible row or column with nonzero coefficient magnitudes, let \(m=\min\{|a_k|:a_k\ne0\}\) and \(M=\max\{|a_k|:a_k\ne0\}\). Set \(d=(mM)^{-1/2}\) and multiply the component by \(d\), applying the corresponding right-hand-side or variable, cost, and bound transformations. The extreme scaled magnitudes are \(dm=\sqrt{m/M}\) and \(dM=\sqrt{M/m}\), whose product equals one. Apply row and column passes iteratively if desired, accumulate all positive diagonal factors, and stop at a prescribed equilibration tolerance or iteration limit. Empty components are excluded and sent to presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric-mean scaling centers each eligible component's extreme nonzero magnitudes around one on a logarithmic scale while recording equivalent LP transformations.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric-Mean Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-component geometric-mean formula and its extremal identities are correct, and algorithm fits the leaf. No source supports the LP-wide iterative row-column variant, whose pass order and stopping criterion are left implementation-dependent.

children.title: Scaling-Variant Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Matrix patterns, outlier sensitivity, plus computational costs governing variant choice.

assumptions_latex: All candidate scaling factors are positive and finite.
The implementation supplies thresholds for dynamic range, norm imbalance, and iteration count.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A scaling variant is admissible only when its factors are defined, numerically representable, and consistently applicable to all coupled LP data.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility and diagnostic conditions for choosing between norm and geometric scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each eligible row or column, compute its nonzero-magnitude range \(\rho=M/m\) and selected \(p\)-norm. Geometric-mean scaling is admissible only when \(0<m\le M<\infty\) and \((mM)^{-1/2}\) is representable; it targets components whose extreme magnitudes require logarithmic centering. Norm-based scaling is admissible when the chosen norm is positive and finite; it targets aggregate norm imbalance. A selection rule may choose geometric scaling when \(\rho>\tau\) and norm scaling otherwise, but \(\tau\) is an implementation parameter, not an equivalence theorem. Reject either variant when accumulated factors overflow, underflow, or cannot be applied consistently to right-hand sides, costs, bounds, starts, and reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose only defined, representable scaling factors: geometric scaling addresses extreme dynamic range, norm scaling addresses aggregate imbalance, and implementation thresholds require validation.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Variant Selection Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition fits this selection-regime leaf, and the statement properly labels the threshold as an implementation parameter. The proposed dynamic-range selection heuristic and numerical rejection conditions nevertheless require authoritative and empirical support before their reliability can be assessed.

children.title: Iterative Equilibration
children.top_down_role: Repeated row–column balancing regimes plus their practical control considerations.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating infinity-norm equilibration of a sparse LP constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a matrix \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), initialize \(D_r^{(0)}=I_m\) and \(D_c^{(0)}=I_n\). At iteration \(k\), form \(M^{(k)}=D_r^{(k)}AD_c^{(k)}\). For every nonzero row set \(s_i=(\max_j|M_{ij}^{(k)}|)^{-1/2}\), and for every nonzero column set \(t_j=(\max_i|M_{ij}^{(k)}|)^{-1/2}\). Update \(D_r^{(k+1)}=\operatorname{diag}(s)D_r^{(k)}\) and \(D_c^{(k+1)}=D_c^{(k)}\operatorname{diag}(t)\). Stop when all nonzero row and column maxima lie in \([1-\tau,1+\tau]\), or after \(K\) iterations; output the scaled matrix and both diagonal factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly rescale rows and columns using their largest absolute entries until their magnitudes are approximately one or an iteration limit is reached.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\)
\(0<\tau<1\) and \(K\in\mathbb{N}\)
Zero rows and columns are left unchanged
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat A=D_r^{(K')}AD_c^{(K')}\), where \(K'\le K\), with the stated equilibration test satisfied unless the iteration limit is reached.

notation.meaning: positive diagonal row and column scaling matrices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but the simultaneous square-root infinity-norm update and its stopping behavior identify a specific equilibration variant requiring an authoritative source.

children.title: Curtis–Reid Equilibration
children.top_down_role: Curtis–Reid scaling architecture, implementation concerns, plus suitable matrix regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Curtis–Reid Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logarithmic least-squares formulation of Curtis–Reid row-column scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\{(i,j):A_{ij}\ne0\}\) and \(w_{ij}=\log|A_{ij}|\). Compute \((u,v)\) minimizing \(\sum_{(i,j)\in E}(w_{ij}+u_i+v_j)^2\), subject to one gauge constraint per connected component of the bipartite sparsity graph. Set \(D_r=\operatorname{diag}(e^{u_i})\), \(D_c=\operatorname{diag}(e^{v_j})\), and output \(D_rAD_c\). At a minimizer, the logarithms of the nonzero scaled magnitudes have zero sum over every row and column, modulo dependent equations caused by the gauge freedom.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose logarithmic row and column factors by least squares so scaled nonzero magnitudes are centered within every row and column.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\)
Every retained row and column contains a nonzero entry
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((D_r,D_c)\) minimizes the stated logarithmic equilibration objective, up to componentwise gauge transformations.

notation.meaning: logarithmic row and column scaling variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but a source is required to verify that the stated logarithmic least-squares objective, componentwise gauge constraints, and row/column optimality conditions are precisely the Curtis–Reid method.

children.title: Equilibration Variant Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance quality, runtime, robustness, plus reproducibility differences between variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Equilibration Variant Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant and objective tradeoffs among diagonal matrix-scaling variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive diagonal matrices \(D_r,D_c\), the scaled matrix \(\widehat A=D_rAD_c\) has the same rank and zero pattern as \(A\). Nevertheless, infinity-norm equilibration, logarithmic least-squares equilibration, and condition-number minimization generally solve different optimization problems; hence a scaling optimal for one criterion need not optimize another. Extremely large diagonal ratios can also amplify rounding and distort the relative interpretation of primal and dual residuals, so scaling quality must be assessed jointly with factor range and unscaled residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal scaling preserves rank and sparsity, but different equilibration objectives can select different factors and extreme factors can harm numerical interpretation.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\)
\(D_r\) and \(D_c\) are positive and nonsingular diagonal matrices
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(D_rAD_c)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\) and \(\operatorname{supp}(D_rAD_c)=\operatorname{supp}(A)\), without universal optimality across scaling criteria.

notation.meaning: index set of nonzero entries of A

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Rank and support preservation are correct, but the claims about rounding amplification and residual interpretation are nontrivial numerical tradeoffs with no cited evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Basis Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal scaling of the simplex basis solve and its recovery map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) be a nonsingular simplex basis and let \(D_1,D_2\) be nonsingular diagonal matrices. Define \(\widehat B=D_1BD_2\). The system \(Bx=b\) is equivalent to \(\widehat B\widehat x=D_1b\) under \(x=D_2\widehat x\). Likewise, \(B^{\mathsf T}y=c_B\) is equivalent to \(\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat y=D_2c_B\) under \(y=D_1\widehat y\). Thus scaled primal and transposed basis solves recover exactly the original solutions in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row and column scaling transforms primal and transposed simplex basis solves, with diagonal maps recovering the original solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular
\(D_1,D_2\) are nonsingular diagonal matrices
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=D_2\widehat B^{-1}D_1b=B^{-1}b\) and \(y=D_1\widehat B^{-\mathsf T}D_2c_B=B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role and exact-arithmetic recovery identities are appropriate, but the record provides no source for this implementation-specific simplex scaling statement.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point System Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric diagonal congruence scaling of an interior-point Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times q}\) be a symmetric nonsingular Newton or KKT matrix, and let \(D\) be a positive diagonal matrix. With \(\widehat K=DKD\), the system \(K\Delta z=r\) is equivalent to \(\widehat K\widehat z=Dr\) under \(\Delta z=D\widehat z\). The transformation is a congruence, so \(K\) and \(\widehat K\) have identical inertia. Consequently, symmetric scaling preserves nonsingularity and the numbers of positive and negative eigenvalues while changing coefficient magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal congruence rescales an interior-point Newton system, preserves inertia, and recovers the original search direction by a diagonal map.
assumptions_latex: \(K=K^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times q}\) is nonsingular
\(D\) is positive diagonal
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta z=D(DKD)^{-1}Dr=K^{-1}r\) and \(\operatorname{inertia}(DKD)=\operatorname{inertia}(K)\).

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Diagonal Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal change of variables for primal-dual first-order LP iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the saddle formulation \(\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y} c^{\mathsf T}x+y^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\), choose positive diagonal matrices \(D_x,D_y\), set \(x=D_xu\) and \(y=D_yv\), and use the transformed operator \(\widehat A=D_yAD_x\). Apply the selected first-order method in \((u,v)\)-coordinates with scalar or diagonal step sizes satisfying that method's stability condition for \(\widehat A\). At termination output \(x=D_xu\) and \(y=D_yv\), and evaluate feasibility and optimality residuals in the original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale primal and dual coordinates diagonally, run the first-order method on the transformed operator, then assess the recovered solution without scaling.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\)
\(D_x,D_y\) are positive diagonal matrices
The transformed steps satisfy the chosen method's stability condition
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y)=(D_xu,D_yv)\) represents the original-coordinate iterate corresponding to the preconditioned iterate \((u,v)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the transformed domains and linear terms are not stated, and no particular first-order method or stability condition is identified. A source is needed to determine the intended mathematically complete formulation.

children.title: Aggressive Presolve
children.top_down_role: Broad reduction use, deeper transformation, plus higher simplification ambition.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggressive Presolve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point application of sound LP reductions, including fill-producing substitutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an LP \(P\), initialize \(P_0=P\) and an empty reversible transformation log \(L\). Repeatedly apply any available sound reduction—bound propagation, fixed-variable elimination, singleton substitution, redundant-row deletion, coefficient strengthening, or implied-free substitution—even when it may increase fill, provided it returns a reconstruction map and preserves the declared solution status. Stop when a full pass makes no change or a resource limit is reached. Output the reduced problem \(P'\), log \(L\), and any sound infeasibility or unboundedness certificate discovered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a broad set of valid reductions to a fixed point, accepting possible fill while recording enough information to reconstruct solutions or certificates.
assumptions_latex: Every reduction is equivalence-preserving or has a stated status-preservation guarantee
Every eliminated quantity has a recorded reconstruction rule
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P'\) has the preserved status of \(P\), and solutions or certificates are mapped through \(L\) according to each reduction's guarantee.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the reduction portfolio, status-preservation guarantees, reconstruction requirements, and meaning of aggressive presolve are solver-dependent and unsupported.

children.title: Conservative Presolve
children.top_down_role: Restricted transformations emphasizing stability, structure retention, plus predictable reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.title: Conservative Presolve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted presolve using low-risk, readily reversible LP reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an LP \(P\), initialize \(P_0=P\) and a reconstruction log \(L\). Apply only reductions whose validity is established with prescribed numerical tolerances and whose postsolve map is direct, such as removing explicit zero rows, tightening bounds by certified implications, and eliminating exactly fixed variables. Reject a proposed reduction if it relies on marginal cancellation, creates prohibited fill, or violates a requested preservation constraint. Stop after stabilization or a pass limit, and output the reduced LP and \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use only numerically clear, easily reversible reductions and reject transformations that threaten stability, sparsity, or requested preservation goals.
assumptions_latex: Reduction predicates use fixed feasibility and zero tolerances
Each accepted reduction has a direct postsolve map
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(P'\) contains only reductions accepted by the conservative admissibility tests, with reconstruction data stored in \(L\).

children.title: Presolve Aggressiveness Selection
children.top_down_role: Model characteristics, solver goals, plus risk signals governing regime choice.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Aggressiveness Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy for selecting a presolve regime from risk, structure, and reduction estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each candidate regime \(g\in G\), estimate reduction benefit \(R_g\), fill cost \(F_g\), numerical risk \(N_g\), and preservation penalty \(Q_g\). Given nonnegative weights \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\), choose an admissible regime maximizing \(S_g=\alpha R_g-\beta F_g-\gamma N_g-\delta Q_g\). A regime is admissible only if all mandatory preservation constraints and resource limits hold. If no aggressive regime is admissible or the best score fails a specified threshold, select the conservative regime. Record the selected regime and the diagnostics used by the decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score candidate presolve regimes by expected reduction, fill, numerical risk, and preservation cost, subject to mandatory constraints and a conservative fallback.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite set of available presolve regimes
\(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\ge0\)
Mandatory constraints are evaluated before scoring
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{g\in G_{\mathrm{adm}}}S_g\), with conservative fallback when the acceptance rule fails.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role is plausible, but the weighted score, diagnostics, threshold, and fallback constitute a solver-design policy rather than a standard presolve-selection algorithm and require a specification or source.

children.title: Basis-Preserving Presolve
children.top_down_role: Transformations constrained by basis continuity, warm starts, plus basis reconstruction needs.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Preserving Presolve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Presolve admissibility condition for retaining a recoverable simplex basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A presolve transformation \(T:P\mapsto P'\) is basis-preserving if it supplies maps \(\Phi\) and \(\Psi\) such that every nonsingular basis of \(P'\) accepted by the solver maps through \(\Phi\) to a nonsingular basis of \(P\), and every associated basic primal-dual solution and basis status maps through \(\Psi\) to the corresponding original variables and constraints. The maps must be computable from the transformation log without resolving the original LP; degenerate statuses may follow a declared deterministic convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolve is basis-preserving when every reduced basis and its statuses can be reconstructed as a valid original basis without resolving the LP.
assumptions_latex: \(P'=T(P)\) is obtained by recorded presolve transformations
Both LPs use a declared simplex basis convention
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is basis-preserving exactly when the stated basis and basic-solution reconstruction maps exist and are executable from the log.

children.title: Structure-Preserving Presolve
children.top_down_role: Transformations constrained by recognizable rows, columns, blocks, or application structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Preserving Presolve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Presolve admissibility relative to a declared matrix-structure invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a structural descriptor \(\mathcal S\), such as a block partition, network incidence representation, or specified sparsity adjacency. A presolve transformation \(T:P\mapsto P'\) is \(\mathcal S\)-preserving if the reduced constraint matrix admits an induced descriptor \(\mathcal S'\) obtained from \(\mathcal S\) solely by permitted deletions, contractions, and relabelings, and every remaining coefficient respects \(\mathcal S'\). Moreover, the postsolve map must restore eliminated variables and constraints without requiring transformations forbidden by \(\mathcal S\). The permitted operations must be declared before presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve preserves structure when its reduced model and reconstruction arise only through operations explicitly allowed by a chosen structural descriptor.
assumptions_latex: A structural descriptor \(\mathcal S\) and its permitted operations are fixed
\(T\) records every reduction needed for postsolve
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is \(\mathcal S\)-preserving precisely when both the reduced model and reconstruction satisfy the declared structural rules.

notation.meaning: induced descriptor of the reduced model

children.title: Preservation-Goal Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Cases where basis continuity, structural retention, plus reduction strength cannot all be maintained.

knowledge_statements.title: Preservation-Goal Conflicts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A substitution can improve reduction while destroying a declared block structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider constraints \(x+u=0\) and \(x+v=0\), where the declared decomposition assigns \(u\) and the first row to block one, \(v\) and the second row to block two, and \(x\) is a linking variable. Eliminating \(x\) using the first equation produces \(v-u=0\), which directly couples the two blocks. Thus a valid dimension-reducing substitution may violate block-structure preservation; prohibiting that substitution preserves the decomposition but forfeits the reduction. Consequently, maximal reduction and preservation of a fixed block partition cannot always be achieved simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating a linking variable can merge otherwise separate blocks, so maximal presolve reduction may conflict with preservation of a declared decomposition.
assumptions_latex: The two displayed equations are retained as exact linear equalities
The declared blocks may interact only through designated linking variables
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating \(x\) yields \(v-u=0\), violating the original block-separation rule despite preserving the feasible set after reconstruction.

children.title: Presolve Reduction Ordering
children.top_down_role: Priority, dependency, plus interaction considerations among available reduction families.

assumptions_latex: The presolve state space \(\mathcal S\) contains LP formulations together with a reversible transformation log.
Each enabled reduction \(R_i:\mathcal S\to\mathcal S\) preserves the represented LP solution and certificate information recorded by the log.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: formalization of an ordered presolve-reduction pass
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One finite ordered pass through enabled, reversible LP presolve reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial state \(S^{(0)}\in\mathcal S\), an enabled index set \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and a permutation \(\pi\) of \(I\), apply \(R_{\pi(1)},R_{\pi(2)},\ldots\) sequentially. After each successful reduction, append sufficient inverse data to the transformation log; after an inapplicable reduction, leave the state unchanged. The output after the pass is \[S^{(|I|)}=R_{\pi(|I|)}\bigl(\cdots R_{\pi(1)}(S^{(0)})\cdots\bigr).\] A deterministic ordering policy fixes \(\pi\) as a function of the current state and solver configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolve pass applies enabled reductions in a specified order, records inverse data, and returns the resulting formulation and transformation log.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Reduction Ordering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the ordering, logging, and deterministic-policy claims. The separate conclusion also incorrectly composes m reductions although the statement applies only |I| reductions.

children.title: Presolve Fixed-Point Control
children.top_down_role: Pass repetition, diminishing returns, plus termination behavior for presolve cycles.

assumptions_latex: The presolve state space \(\mathcal S\) includes a reversible transformation log.
A complete sweep operator \(T:\mathcal S\to\mathcal S\) deterministically applies the configured reductions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(S^*\) satisfies \(T(S^*)=S^*\), unless a declared resource limit terminates the process earlier.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fixed-point iteration is the standard formal model for repeated presolve sweeps
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated deterministic sweeps with an explicit quiescence or resource-limit stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(S^{(0)}\in\mathcal S\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \(S^{(k+1)}=T(S^{(k)})\). Stop with output \(S^*=S^{(k)}\) when a full sweep changes neither the active LP formulation nor its transformation log, equivalently when \(T(S^{(k)})=S^{(k)}\). An implementation may instead stop at a declared pass, time, or memory limit; that output is resource-limited and need not be a fixed point. Every accepted sweep must preserve enough inverse information for postsolve reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve repeats complete reduction sweeps until a sweep changes nothing, or reports that a declared resource limit stopped iteration first.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Fixed-Point Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits fixed-point control, but no source supports this implementation model. Moreover, deterministic iteration alone does not guarantee finite arrival at a fixed point; a finite-state, monotonicity, or explicit termination assumption would be needed for an unconditional fixed-point output claim.

children.title: Ordering-Induced Reduction Variability
children.top_down_role: Differences in reduced models, numerical behavior, or runtime caused by reduction order.

assumptions_latex: The same initial state \(S\in\mathcal S\) and enabled reduction family are used under two ordering policies.
Each reduction is individually validity-preserving but reductions need not commute.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ordering variability occurs when \(F_{\pi}(S)\ne F_{\sigma}(S)\), even though both outputs represent equivalent LPs.

notation.meaning: fixed-point outputs under orderings pi and sigma

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: noncommuting rewrite operators can produce distinct normal forms
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variability of reduced formulations, not variability of the original LP's mathematical solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_{\pi}(S)\) denote the quiescent presolve state obtained from \(S\) using ordering policy \(\pi\). Ordering-induced reduction variability is the condition \[F_{\pi}(S)\ne F_{\sigma}(S)\] for two admissible policies \(\pi\) and \(\sigma\), where inequality may concern dimensions, sparsity, coefficients, bounds, or transformation logs. Such variability is possible whenever some applicable reductions fail to commute, meaning \(R_i(R_j(S))\ne R_j(R_i(S))\), or one reduction disables another. Validity preservation requires both terminal states to encode LPs equivalent to the original through their respective logs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different valid reduction orders can yield different reduced formulations because reductions may not commute, while each result remains equivalent to the original LP.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordering-Induced Reduction Variability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role and definition of observed variability fit the leaf, but no source is supplied. Failure of two reductions to commute at an intermediate state does not by itself ensure distinct quiescent outputs, so the stated sufficient condition also requires correction or authoritative qualification.

children.title: Presolve-Ablation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Runs suppressing selected presolve capabilities to isolate transformation effects.

assumptions_latex: A baseline solver configuration fixes all components except the presolve regime.
Every regime is evaluated on the same LP instance and with the same stopping and resource conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The presolve ablation family is \(\{C_{\mathrm{off}},C_{J_1},\ldots,C_{J_q},C_{\mathrm{full}}\}\).

notation.meaning: configuration enabling the full presolve family

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: controlled ablation varies one transformation component while holding the evaluation protocol fixed
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled experimental regimes for isolating presolve's effect on solver behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R=\{R_1,\ldots,R_m\}\) be the available presolve reductions. A presolve-ablation regime is a solver configuration \(C_J\), indexed by \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), that enables exactly \(\{R_j:j\in J\}\) while holding scaling, core algorithm, tolerances, stopping rules, and resource limits fixed. The canonical controls are \(C_{\mathrm{off}}=C_{\varnothing}\) and \(C_{\mathrm{full}}=C_{\{1,\ldots,m\}}\). Intermediate regimes may remove one reduction family or enable a prescribed subset, but their ordering and fixed-point policies must be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolve ablation compares configurations that differ only in which presolve reductions are enabled, under a common algorithm and evaluation protocol.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve-Ablation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the ablation-regime leaf, and the controlled-comparison formulation is plausible, but the exact experimental controls and required declarations have no inspectable citation.

children.title: Scaling-Ablation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Runs suppressing selected scaling capabilities to isolate numerical effects.

assumptions_latex: A baseline solver configuration fixes all components except scaling.
Every regime uses the same LP instance, tolerances, stopping rules, and resource limits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaling ablation compares \(C_I\) across declared diagonal-scaling choices, including \(C_{(I,I)}\).

notation.meaning: positive diagonal row and column scalings

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: controlled ablation varies the scaling transformation while fixing the evaluation protocol
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled regimes for row and column scaling of an LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an LP with matrix \(A\), a diagonal scaling regime selects positive diagonal matrices \(D_r\) and \(D_c\) and solves the consistently transformed formulation whose matrix is \(D_rAD_c\). A scaling-ablation family consists of configurations \(C_{(D_r,D_c)}\) that differ only in this selection. It includes the unscaled control \(C_{(I,I)}\) and each declared scaling rule. Presolve, core algorithm, tolerances, stopping criteria, and resource limits remain fixed, and reported residuals must be mapped to a common coordinate system before comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaling ablation changes only the declared row and column scaling rule and compares results after mapping residuals to common coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Ablation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, but no source supports the protocol. Specifying only the transformed matrix D_r A D_c does not fully define the consistent transformation of the objective, right-hand side, bounds, and solution coordinates.

children.title: Joint Transformation Ablation
children.top_down_role: Combined suppression regimes used to expose interaction effects between presolve plus scaling.

assumptions_latex: Presolve and scaling settings are the only transformation factors varied.
All configurations share the same LP instance, core solver, tolerances, stopping rules, and resource limits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The joint ablation is the factorial family \(\{C_{p,s}:(p,s)\in P\times S\}\).

notation.meaning: configuration with presolve p and scaling s

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a factorial ablation identifies main effects and transformation interactions
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factorial ablation of presolve and scaling, including their interaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a finite set of presolve regimes and \(S\) a finite set of scaling regimes, each containing an off or identity control. A joint transformation ablation is the factorial configuration family \[\mathcal C=\{C_{p,s}:(p,s)\in P\times S\},\] with every nontransformation setting held fixed. For a scalar diagnostic \(M(p,s)\), the interaction contrast relative to controls \(p_0\) and \(s_0\) is \[\Delta_{p,s}=M(p,s)-M(p,s_0)-M(p_0,s)+M(p_0,s_0).\] A nonzero contrast records a joint effect not attributable to the two separate control comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint ablation evaluates every declared presolve-scaling pair; an interaction contrast separates their combined effect from their individual effects.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Transformation Ablation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits joint ablation, but the factorial protocol and diagnostic interpretation lack a source. The interaction contrast is scale-dependent and records additivity failure on the chosen metric scale, not an invariant causal interaction.

assumptions_latex: The transformation log records an inverse primal map for every accepted presolve or scaling step.
A reduced primal vector \(\hat x\) satisfies the reduced formulation to the required tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reconstructed vector is \(x=T_1^x\circ\cdots\circ T_k^x(\hat x)\).

notation.meaning: inverse primal map for transformation i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse-order reconstruction of an original-space primal solution from a reduced solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose forward preprocessing applies transformations \(T_1,T_2,\ldots,T_k\) in that order and records corresponding inverse primal maps \(T_1^x,\ldots,T_k^x\). Initialize \(x^{(k)}=\hat x\). For \(i=k,k-1,\ldots,1\), compute \(x^{(i-1)}=T_i^x(x^{(i)})\), restoring eliminated variables, undoing substitutions, and reversing column scaling as specified by the log. Output \(x=x^{(0)}\). Accept the reconstruction only if original-space bounds and row residuals satisfy the declared feasibility tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Postsolve reconstructs the original primal vector by reversing logged transformations and then checks original bounds and row residuals.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Solution Reconstruction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits primal reconstruction, and the reverse-log order is internally consistent, but no source supports the assumed inverse maps, restoration rules, or acceptance tests.

children.title: Dual-Value Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of reported row dual values through reversed transformations.

assumptions_latex: The forward transformation log supplies an inverse dual map for each row transformation or elimination.
The reduced dual vector \(\hat y\) follows the same constraint-sign convention as the original LP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reconstructed dual vector is \(y=T_1^y\circ\cdots\circ T_k^y(\hat y)\).

notation.meaning: inverse dual map for transformation i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dual postsolve reverses logged row transformations and restores eliminated multipliers
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse-order reconstruction of original constraint multipliers under a fixed sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If forward preprocessing applies \(T_1,T_2,\ldots,T_k\), initialize \(y^{(k)}=\hat y\) and, for \(i=k,k-1,\ldots,1\), set \(y^{(i-1)}=T_i^y(y^{(i)})\). Each inverse map reverses row scaling and aggregation and assigns multipliers for removed constraints according to the recorded reduction identity. Output \(y=y^{(0)}\). The reconstruction is admissible only when the resulting multiplier signs satisfy the original constraint senses and when the associated reduced costs satisfy the original dual stationarity equations within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual postsolve reverses logged row transformations, restores removed multipliers, and validates signs and original-space stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Value Reconstruction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits dual-value reconstruction, but no citation supports the existence of a dual inverse map for every listed transformation. Eliminated-row multipliers may require coupled reconstruction with reduced costs rather than a map depending only on the current dual vector.

children.title: Reduced-Cost Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of reported reduced costs through scaling, substitution, plus eliminated-column mappings.

assumptions_latex: The original LP is written with objective vector \(c\), constraint matrix \(A\), and reconstructed row-dual vector \(y\).
The solver's dual sign convention is fixed so that stationarity uses \(c-A^{\mathsf T}y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original-space reduced-cost vector is \(r=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-space reduced costs reconstructed from dual values under one explicit sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the original-space minimization convention, define the reduced-cost vector by \[r=c-A^{\mathsf T}y.\] After reconstructing \(y\), compute this identity in original coordinates rather than relying solely on transformed reduced costs. Equivalently, if the transformation log provides inverse reduced-cost maps \(T_i^r\), their reverse composition must produce the same vector within the declared numerical tolerance. Components associated with restored variables are included, and their signs must agree with the corresponding original lower-bound, upper-bound, or free-variable dual-feasibility conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Original reduced costs are recomputed as objective coefficients minus transposed constraint coefficients times reconstructed dual values, then checked against bound signs.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Reconstruction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role and identity r=c-A^T y are standard under the declared convention, and the locator is specific. However, the cited primal-dual section does not establish the asserted equivalence with reverse-composed implementation-specific reduced-cost maps, which is material to the reconstruction leaf.

children.title: Dual–Reduced-Cost Consistency
children.top_down_role: Sign, scaling, activity, plus status consistency across reconstructed dual artifacts.

assumptions_latex: The original LP is a minimization problem using the stationarity convention \(r=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\).
The vectors \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(r\in\mathbb R^n\) are reconstructed in original coordinates, where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
Each variable has a declared original-space status in \(\{\mathrm{lower},\mathrm{upper},\mathrm{interior},\mathrm{free},\mathrm{fixed}\}\), consistent with its original bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistency requires \(\|r-(c-A^{\mathsf T}y)\|_{\infty}\le\tau_d\) and the status-dependent reduced-cost conditions at tolerance \(\tau_d\ge 0\).

notation.meaning: original constraint matrix and objective vector
original-space bound status of variable j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical stationarity and bound-status sign consistency for a minimization LP in original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the minimization convention \(r=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\), the reconstructed pair \((y,r)\) is dual-reduced-cost consistent at tolerance \(\tau_d\ge 0\) when \[\|r-(c-A^{\mathsf T}y)\|_{\infty}\le\tau_d.\] For each variable \(j\), its original-space bound status \(s_j\) must also satisfy the corresponding condition: if \(s_j=\mathrm{lower}\), then \(r_j\ge-\tau_d\); if \(s_j=\mathrm{upper}\), then \(r_j\le\tau_d\); and if \(s_j\in\{\mathrm{interior},\mathrm{free}\}\), then \(|r_j|\le\tau_d\). A fixed variable imposes no sign restriction on \(r_j\) because both bound multipliers may be active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstructed dual values and reduced costs are consistent when they satisfy original-space stationarity and, for a minimization problem, the reduced-cost sign or zero condition associated with every variable's original bound status.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual–Reduced-Cost Consistency

children.title: Basis Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of row or column basis statuses after reversible model transformations.

assumptions_latex: The reduced solve returns a valid basis status assignment.
Every presolve transformation records a rule for lifting basis statuses or flags that exact lifting is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful output \(B\) has full rank and induces the reconstructed primal and dual basic solution within tolerance.

Reverse the transformation log and set \(B^{(i-1)}=T_i^B(B^{(i)})\), restoring statuses for eliminated rows, columns, and slacks according to each recorded rule. Output \(B=B^{(0)}\) only if its basic columns have the required cardinality and full rank and if the associated basic primal and dual solutions agree with the reconstructed vectors within tolerance. If a transformation lacks a valid inverse basis rule, report basis reconstruction as unavailable rather than assigning unsupported statuses.

The existence and validity of each basis-status map require an implementation-specific presolve/postsolve source.

children.title: Ray Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Mapping of primal or dual rays from transformed space to submitted-model space.

assumptions_latex: The reduced solver returns a nonzero recession ray \(\hat d\) or certificate direction.
Every forward transformation records a positively homogeneous inverse direction map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reconstructed direction is \(d=T_1^d\circ\cdots\circ T_k^d(\hat d)\) and must satisfy the original homogeneous certificate conditions.

notation.meaning: inverse direction map for transformation i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: certificate directions must be lifted through the homogeneous parts of preprocessing maps
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse reconstruction and validation of an unboundedness or infeasibility direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(d^{(k)}=\hat d\). For \(i=k,k-1,\ldots,1\), compute \(d^{(i-1)}=T_i^d(d^{(i)})\), using the homogeneous part of substitutions and scalings so that constant offsets do not enter the direction. Set \(d=d^{(0)}\) and normalize only by a positive scalar. Accept \(d\) as a ray only if \(d\ne0\) and it satisfies the appropriate original-space homogeneous feasibility, bound-direction, and objective-improvement inequalities within declared tolerances; otherwise report reconstruction failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ray postsolve reverses the homogeneous transformation maps and validates the nonzero direction against the original certificate inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Ray Reconstruction

children.title: Certificate Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of infeasibility or unboundedness evidence across presolve plus scaling transformations.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(R\) uses the complete ordered record of presolve transformations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y,s)\) certifies optimality for the original LP when the displayed original-space conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Postsolve certification for a canonical primal-dual LP pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). Consider the primal LP
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in\mathbb R^n,\ x\ge 0\}\]
and its dual
\[\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ y\in\mathbb R^m,\ s\in\mathbb R^n,\ s\ge 0\}.\]
Given a reduced-solver artifact \(\widetilde w\) and a recorded postsolve map \(R\), let \((x,y,s)=R(\widetilde w)\). This triple is a reconstructed optimality certificate precisely when
\[Ax=b,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\qquad x\ge0,\qquad s\ge0,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y=0.\]
A tolerance-based reconstruction replaces the equality conditions by prescribed residual tests and requires componentwise bounds \(x\ge-\tau\mathbf1\) and \(s\ge-\tau\mathbf1\), where \(\tau\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated finite-dimensional primal-dual LP pair, a reconstructed certificate is valid exactly when the postsolved primal and dual variables satisfy the original feasibility, sign, and duality-gap tests, or their prescribed tolerance-based counterparts.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Reconstruction

children.title: Artifact Reconstruction Failures

knowledge_statements.title: Artifact Reconstruction Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-loss boundary for postsolve artifacts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Artifact reconstruction cannot be guaranteed when presolve discards data needed to distinguish original models. For example, the one-variable feasibility problems \(x=0\) and \(x=1\) both become the same empty reduced problem after fixed-variable elimination. If the eliminated value is not recorded, both runs expose the same reduced artifact \(\widetilde w\). No deterministic map depending only on \(\widetilde w\) can return a point feasible for both original problems. More generally, exact reconstruction fails whenever two original instances induce identical retained reduced data but require disjoint sets of valid original-space artifacts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discarded transformation metadata can make distinct original problems indistinguishable, so no reduced-artifact-only reconstruction can be correct for both.
assumptions_latex: Postsolve receives only the reduced artifact and retained transformation data.
A valid artifact must satisfy the corresponding original-space equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Loss of distinguishing elimination data precludes a universally correct artifact reconstruction map.

notation.meaning: Artifact returned for the reduced problem

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the indistinguishability example correctly identifies an information-loss obstruction. No inspectable source is supplied for the postsolve reconstruction failure claim.

children.title: Postsolve Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Cross-checks among reconstructed primal, dual, basis, objective, plus status information.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
All residuals are evaluated with the original, unscaled LP data.
The tolerances \(\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_g,\tau_c\) are nonnegative and fixed before validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities define postsolve consistency of \((x,y,s)\).

notation.meaning: Primal, dual, gap, and componentwise tolerances

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-space acceptance conditions after postsolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). For the primal-dual LP pair
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in\mathbb R^n,\ x\ge0\},\qquad \max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ y\in\mathbb R^m,\ s\in\mathbb R^n,\ s\ge0\},\]
a postsolved triple \((x,y,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) passes the stated scaled consistency checks at tolerances \(\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_g,\tau_c\ge0\) when
\[\frac{\|Ax-b\|_\infty}{1+\|b\|_\infty}\le\tau_p,\quad \frac{\|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|_\infty}{1+\|c\|_\infty}\le\tau_d,\]
\[x\ge-\tau_c\mathbf1,\quad s\ge-\tau_c\mathbf1,\quad \frac{|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|}{1+|c^{\mathsf T}x|+|b^{\mathsf T}y|}\le\tau_g.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated finite-dimensional primal-dual LP pair, postsolve acceptance under this convention requires small scaled primal, dual, sign, and duality-gap violations in the original model.
knowledge_statements.title: Postsolve Consistency Checks

children.title: Postsolve Mapping Failures
children.top_down_role: Missing, conflicting, irreversible, or numerically unstable transformation mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(n\ge2\), \(x_{-j}\in\mathbb R^{n-1}\), \(a\in\mathbb R^{n-1}\), and \(b,\alpha,x_j\in\mathbb R\).
The eliminated equation and its coefficient \(\alpha\) are retained exactly enough to apply the inverse step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A zero pivot prevents this inverse reconstruction, while a nonzero pivot amplifies numerator perturbations by \(1/|\alpha|\).

notation.meaning: All components of the primal vector except component j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Undefined or unstable inverse transformations during postsolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\ge2\), \(x_{-j}\in\mathbb R^{n-1}\), \(a\in\mathbb R^{n-1}\), and \(b,\alpha,x_j\in\mathbb R\). Suppose presolve eliminates \(x_j\) from
\[\alpha x_j+a^{\mathsf T}x_{-j}=b,\]
so postsolve uses
\[x_j=\frac{b-a^{\mathsf T}x_{-j}}{\alpha}.\]
This inverse mapping is undefined when \(\alpha=0\). When \(\alpha\ne0\), a numerator perturbation \(\delta r\in\mathbb R\) produces \(|\delta x_j|=|\delta r|/|\alpha|\), so small \(|\alpha|\) amplifies reconstruction error. A postsolve implementation reports mapping failure when a required inverse is undefined, required recorded metadata is absent, or a reconstructed original-space residual exceeds the declared acceptance tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated scalar elimination step, a postsolve inverse is undefined when its pivot or required metadata is absent, and a nonzero pivot amplifies numerator error by the reciprocal of its magnitude.
knowledge_statements.title: Postsolve Mapping Failures

children.title: Reconstruction Residual Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Residual patterns used to localize faults introduced during postsolve recovery.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
Residuals use the original, unscaled problem data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(x,y,s)=0\) exactly when \((x,y,s)\) satisfies the primal-dual feasibility, nonnegativity, and zero-gap conditions.

notation.meaning: Componentwise positive part of a vector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled diagnostic vector for reconstructed LP solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \((x,y,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) be a reconstructed primal-dual triple. Define
\[r_p=Ax-b,\qquad r_d=A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c,\qquad r_g=c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y.\]
A scale-aware diagnostic vector is
\[D(x,y,s)=\left(\frac{\|r_p\|_\infty}{1+\|b\|_\infty},\ \frac{\|r_d\|_\infty}{1+\|c\|_\infty},\ \frac{|r_g|}{1+|c^{\mathsf T}x|+|b^{\mathsf T}y|},\ \|(-x)_+\|_\infty,\ \|(-s)_+\|_\infty\right).\]
Reporting the components separately distinguishes primal infeasibility, dual infeasibility, gap error, and sign violations that a single aggregate residual could conceal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For explicitly dimensioned original-space primal-dual variables, the diagnostic vector separately reports scaled primal, dual, gap, and nonnegativity errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction Residual Diagnostics

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(b\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
The selected basis matrix \(B\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed basis systems determine \(x_B\), \(y\), and the nonbasic reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear systems induced by a simplex basis partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(m\), let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and partition
\[A=[B\ N],\qquad x=(x_B,x_N),\qquad c=(c_B,c_N),\]
where \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular. For prescribed \(x_N\), primal feasibility is represented by
\[Bx_B=b-Nx_N,\qquad x_B=B^{-1}(b-Nx_N).\]
The simplex multiplier \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and nonbasic reduced costs satisfy
\[B^{\mathsf T}y=c_B,\qquad \bar c_N=c_N-N^{\mathsf T}y.\]
Thus primal basic values and dual pricing require solves with \(B\) and \(B^{\mathsf T}\), normally through a maintained factorization rather than explicit inversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given explicitly dimensioned LP data and a nonsingular basis partition, primal basic values and dual prices are represented by linear solves with the basis matrix and its transpose.
knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Basis Systems

\(x,s\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(x>0\) and \(s>0\), so \(X\) and \(S\) are positive diagonal matrices.
\(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(r_d,r_c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal-dual Newton equations reduce to the displayed normal equations and recovery formulas, and the normal-equation coefficient is symmetric positive definite.
