assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is a nonsingular simplex basis matrix.
Row and column permutations are allowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(PBQ=LU\), so basis solves reduce to triangular substitutions and permutations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Permuted sparse LU representation used for primal and transposed simplex basis solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse LU basis factorization represents a nonsingular basis \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) as \(PBQ=LU\), where \(P\) and \(Q\) are permutation matrices, \(L\) is nonsingular lower triangular, and \(U\) is nonsingular upper triangular. For \(Bx=b\), compute \(Ly=Pb\), then \(Uz=y\), and return \(x=Qz\). For \(B^{\mathsf T}x=b\), apply the corresponding transposed substitutions in reverse order. Sparse ordering and pivoting determine fill and stability but do not alter these identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A permuted sparse LU factorization turns basis and transposed-basis solves into sparse triangular substitutions and permutations.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse LU Basis Factorization

assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular, and \(B'\) is obtained by replacing column \(r\) of \(B\) with \(a\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
The transformed entering column is \(d=B^{-1}a\), and \(d_r\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B'=BE\), \((B')^{-1}=E^{-1}B^{-1}\), and successive updated solves apply the initial basis solve before the eta inverses in increasing update order.

notation.meaning: identity matrix with column r replaced by d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical eta-matrix product representation for successive simplex basis replacements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B'\) be obtained from a nonsingular matrix \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) by replacing column \(r\) with \(a\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(d=B^{-1}a\). Define the eta matrix \(E\) as the identity matrix with column \(r\) replaced by \(d\). Then \(B'=BE\), and \(B'\) is nonsingular exactly when \(d_r\ne0\). In that case \((B')^{-1}=E^{-1}B^{-1}\). After successive replacements, \(B_k=B_0E_1\cdots E_k\). Thus, to compute \(x=B_k^{-1}b\), first compute \(x_0=B_0^{-1}b\), and then compute \(x_i=E_i^{-1}x_{i-1}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each basis replacement is represented by an eta matrix; an updated solve first uses the initial basis factorization and then applies the stored eta inverses in update order.
knowledge_statements.title: Product-Form Updates

assumptions_latex: A stable factorization \(PBQ=LU\) is available.
One basis column is replaced and the resulting basis remains nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update produces triangular factors for the new basis after elimination of the induced spike.

notation.meaning: new basis after one column replacement
intermediate upper factor containing a spike

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical column-replacement interpretation; implementation variants differ in permutations and elimination storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(PBQ=LU\) and a replacement of one column of \(B\), first transform the entering column by the existing lower factor and insert it into \(U\), obtaining an upper-triangular matrix with one spike, denoted \(\widehat U\). Apply adjacent permutations and numerically stable elementary eliminations to move and eliminate the spike. Accumulate those eliminations into the lower-factor representation and retain the resulting upper triangular factor \(U'\). The algorithm outputs permutations and factors satisfying \(P'B'Q'=L'U'\); a rejected elimination pivot terminates the update and requests refactorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Insert the transformed entering column into the upper factor, then use permutations and eliminations to remove the resulting spike.
knowledge_statements.title: Bartels–Golub Updates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic spike-elimination description is plausible, and algorithm is the correct content kind, but the cited table-of-contents locator does not establish that the stated permutation, elimination, and lower-factor accumulation scheme is specifically the Bartels–Golub update. A specialized source with an algorithm or section devoted to the named update is required.

assumptions_latex: A stable sparse factorization of the current basis is available.
A single-column replacement yields a nonsingular new basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated basis is represented by retained triangular factors plus sparse row transformations restoring triangular form.

notation.meaning: upper factor after column insertion and permutation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical sparse Forrest–Tomlin update; storage and permutation conventions vary among implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given sparse factors of \(B\), transform the entering column through the existing lower-factor representation, replace the leaving column in the upper factor, and permute the modified column to expose a short nontriangular spike in \(\widehat U\). Apply sparse row transformations whose product is \(R\) so that \(R\widehat U=U'\) is upper triangular. Store the transformations without fully merging them into the original factors, thereby representing solves with \(B'\) through the old factors, permutations, \(R\), and \(U'\). If a required pivot fails stability tests, request fresh factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restore triangular form after a column replacement while storing sparse row transformations separately to limit fill and update cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Forrest–Tomlin Updates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The source locator does not verify that this particular separately stored row-transformation representation is the Forrest–Tomlin update, and the equation relating the old factors, permutations, \(R\), and the new basis is not stated. A specialized source confirming the named algorithm and its factor identities is required.

children.title: Basis Refactorization Policies
children.top_down_role: Scheduled or condition-triggered replacement of accumulated basis updates.

assumptions_latex: A basis has a fresh factorization followed by zero or more updates.
Finite thresholds for update count, residual, growth, and work are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Refactorization occurs at the first iteration satisfying the policy predicate \(T_k\).

notation.meaning: number of updates since the last factorization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic policy combining periodic and diagnostic refactorization triggers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After each basis change, update the current factor representation and evaluate \(T_k\), where \(k\) counts updates since the last fresh factorization. The predicate may be \(T_k=(k\ge k_{\max})\lor(r_k>\tau_r)\lor(g_k>\tau_g)\lor(c_k>\tau_c)\), using a solve residual \(r_k\), growth indicator \(g_k\), and estimated update-solve cost \(c_k\). If \(T_k\) is false, retain the updated representation. If \(T_k\) is true, factorize \(B_k\) afresh, discard accumulated updates, reset \(k=0\), and continue only if the new factors pass stability tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse basis updates until a periodic, accuracy, growth, or cost trigger requests a fresh factorization.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis Refactorization Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is a suitable role for a refactorization policy, but the cited section locators do not support this exact composite trigger. The solve residual, growth indicator, and cost estimate are also not mathematically defined, so different implementations could realize materially different policies. A solver specification or numerical linear algebra source is required.

children.title: Basis Update-Limit Policies
children.top_down_role: Caps based on update count, storage, solve cost, or numerical degradation.

assumptions_latex: Each accepted pivot creates one stored basis update.
A positive integer limit \(k_{\max}\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A fresh factorization is mandatory whenever \(k\ge k_{\max}\).

notation.meaning: updates since the last fresh factorization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A hard update-count cap independent of adaptive numerical triggers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\) be the number of accepted basis updates retained since the most recent fresh factorization, and fix \(k_{\max}\in\mathbb{N}\). The update-limit policy permits another updated solve only while \(k<k_{\max}\). When an accepted pivot makes \(k\ge k_{\max}\), the solver must form the current basis explicitly, compute a fresh factorization, discard the accumulated update representation, and reset \(k=0\). Numerical instability may trigger earlier refactorization, so the count limit is a maximum rather than a promised update lifetime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permit at most a fixed number of retained basis updates, while allowing numerical diagnostics to force earlier refactorization.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis Update-Limit Policies

children.title: Adaptive Refactorization Triggers
children.top_down_role: Runtime signals used to revise refactorization timing during simplex execution.

assumptions_latex: Current basis solves provide computable residual, growth, pivot, and cost indicators.
Corresponding intervention thresholds are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Refactorize exactly when \(T_k=1\), subject to any overriding hard update limit.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive intervention based on observed numerical quality and solve cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After update \(k\), compute a scaled solve residual \(r_k\), a factor or update-growth indicator \(g_k\), the smallest scaled update pivot \(p_k\), and an update-solve cost estimate \(c_k\). Define \(T_k=1\) when \(r_k>\tau_r\), \(g_k>\tau_g\), \(p_k<\tau_p\), or \(c_k>\tau_c\); otherwise set \(T_k=0\). A policy using these diagnostics refactorizes the current basis exactly when \(T_k=1\), unless a hard update-count limit has already required refactorization. Thresholds must be calibrated to arithmetic precision and target feasibility accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trigger refactorization when measured residual, growth, pivot quality, or update-solve cost crosses its configured intervention threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Refactorization Triggers

children.title: Delayed-Refactorization Failures
children.top_down_role: Accuracy loss, excessive solve cost, memory growth, or instability from retaining updates too long.

assumptions_latex: Floating-point arithmetic has unit roundoff \(u\).
A basis solve applies \(k\) stored transformations with cumulative amplification \(G_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(\gamma_{ck}G_k\) is not small, the updated solve lacks a useful small-backward-error guarantee and refactorization is required.

notation.meaning: cumulative norm amplification of stored transformations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Roundoff-amplification boundary for excessively long update chains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the standard floating-point model, applying \(k\) stored update transformations introduces an error term whose representative scale is \(\gamma_{ck}G_k\), where \(\gamma_j=ju/(1-ju)\), \(u\) is unit roundoff, \(c\) bounds work per update, and \(G_k\) measures cumulative norm amplification. If refactorization is delayed until \(cku\ge1\), then \(\gamma_{ck}\) is undefined; even before that point, when \(\gamma_{ck}G_k\) is not small, no useful small-backward-error guarantee follows. Thus update count alone is unsafe without residual or growth monitoring.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Long update chains can amplify accumulated rounding error until basis solves lose a useful backward-error guarantee, even before a fixed count limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Delayed-Refactorization Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the appropriate content kind, but the cited reuse section does not support the asserted \(\gamma_{ck}G_k\) scale. The amplification quantity \(G_k\), operation constant \(c\), and connection to backward error require a specialized rounding-error analysis. Without that source, the stated boundary is not reliable.

children.title: Basis Condition Monitoring
children.top_down_role: Condition indicators used to assess sensitivity plus reliability of basis solves.

assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is the current nonsingular basis.
A consistent induced matrix norm and an inverse-norm estimator are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\kappa(B)=\lVert B\rVert\widehat{\lVert B^{-1}\rVert}\) is the monitored condition indicator and triggers intervention when it exceeds \(\tau_\kappa\).

notation.meaning: basis condition number in the selected norm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise condition estimation using existing basis solves, without explicitly forming the inverse.

source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the current nonsingular basis \(B\), select a consistent induced norm and compute or update \(\lVert B\rVert\). Use solves with \(B\) and \(B^{\mathsf T}\) to obtain an inverse-norm estimate \(\widehat{\lVert B^{-1}\rVert}\) without forming \(B^{-1}\). Report \(\widehat\kappa(B)=\lVert B\rVert\widehat{\lVert B^{-1}\rVert}\). If \(\widehat\kappa(B)>\tau_\kappa\), mark the basis as ill-conditioned and request refinement, refactorization, or a basis change. Because the estimate may be a lower bound, residual and factor-growth diagnostics remain independent safeguards.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate the basis condition number from basis and transposed-basis solves, then intervene when the estimate exceeds a configured threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis Condition Monitoring

source_witnesses.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition-number identity is standard, but the cited condition-number section and implementation chapter do not establish the proposed inverse-norm estimator, its lower-bound behavior, or the intervention policy. A numerical linear algebra source specifying condition estimation from solves and its guarantees is required before accepting this monitoring algorithm.

children.title: Factor-Growth Monitoring
children.top_down_role: Growth indicators used to detect numerical amplification during basis factorization or updates.

assumptions_latex: The nonsingular simplex basis matrix is \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\).
Gaussian elimination with specified pivoting produces intermediate matrices \(B^{(k)}\) and factors \(P B Q=L U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The statistic \(\rho_B\) quantifies element growth during basis factorization and can be compared across refactorizations of the same scaled basis system.

notation.meaning: element-growth factor for the basis factorization
largest absolute entry of a matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Element-growth diagnostic for a scaled simplex basis under a fixed pivoting convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the factor-growth statistic by \[\rho_B=\frac{\max_{0\le k\le m}\lVert B^{(k)}\rVert_{\max}}{\lVert B\rVert_{\max}}.\] Here \(B^{(0)}=B\), and \(B^{(k)}\) denotes the active elimination matrix after step \(k\), including the effects of the selected row and column permutations. A monitor records \(\rho_B\), the pivoting rule, and the scaling used for \(B\). Large \(\rho_B\) indicates amplification within elimination; it is a factorization diagnostic rather than an estimate of \(\kappa(B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monitor the largest entry created during elimination relative to the largest original basis entry, while recording scaling and pivoting conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: Factor-Growth Monitoring

children.title: Condition–Growth Disagreement
children.top_down_role: Cases where condition indicators plus growth indicators suggest different stability assessments.

assumptions_latex: A scaled nonsingular basis \(B\) has a condition estimate \(\widehat\kappa(B)>0\) and factor-growth statistic \(\rho_B\ge 1\).
Warning levels \(\tau_\kappa>1\) and \(\tau_\rho>1\) are fixed for one solver configuration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A disagreement is present exactly when one normalized diagnostic exceeds its warning level and the other does not.

notation.meaning: estimated condition number of the scaled basis

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean disagreement predicate; it does not assert that either diagnostic is a complete stability test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the warning indicators \(c_B=\mathbf{1}\{\widehat\kappa(B)>\tau_\kappa\}\) and \(g_B=\mathbf{1}\{\rho_B>\tau_\rho\}\). Condition-growth disagreement is the predicate \[c_B\mathbin{\oplus}g_B=1,\] equivalently \[(\widehat\kappa(B)>\tau_\kappa\ \wedge\ \rho_B\le\tau_\rho)\ \vee\ (\widehat\kappa(B)\le\tau_\kappa\ \wedge\ \rho_B>\tau_\rho).\] The first case flags estimated sensitivity without excessive observed elimination growth; the second flags excessive growth despite an acceptable condition estimate. Scaling, norm, estimator, and pivoting rule are held fixed when applying this predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Condition-growth disagreement occurs when exactly one of the condition estimate and elimination-growth statistic crosses its configured warning threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Condition–Growth Disagreement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The XOR predicate is internally correct and content_kind condition fits the leaf, but no source supports this particular solver-diagnostic classification or its interpretation. An authoritative numerical linear algebra or LP solver implementation source is required.

children.title: Basis-Stability Intervention Thresholds
children.top_down_role: Monitoring levels that motivate refactorization, pivot-policy changes, rescaling, or method recovery.

assumptions_latex: Diagnostics \(d_j(B)\ge 0\) have warning and critical thresholds \(0<w_j<c_j\).
A deterministic intervention order is configured for the simplex implementation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maximum diagnostic severity selects a reproducible intervention class without treating thresholds as universal mathematical constants.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A generic threshold policy for implementation diagnostics, not universal numerical constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each monitored diagnostic define \[s_j=\begin{cases}0,&d_j(B)\le w_j,\\1,&w_j<d_j(B)\le c_j,\\2,&d_j(B)>c_j.\end{cases}\] Set \(s(B)=\max_j s_j\). If \(s(B)=0\), retain the current factors; if \(s(B)=1\), request a fresh factorization with strengthened pivoting or scaling; if \(s(B)=2\), reject the pending basis solve and refactorize before continuing. If the post-refactorization severity remains \(2\), invoke the configured higher-level recovery action. The output is the selected intervention and the diagnostics that attained \(s(B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify each stability diagnostic as normal, warning, or critical, then retain, refactorize, or reject the solve according to the maximum severity.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Stability Intervention Thresholds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is explicit and fits the intervention-threshold leaf, but the prescribed retain, refactorize, reject, and higher-level recovery actions are solver-policy claims without cited support. Their mathematical and operational validity depends on an authoritative implementation source.

assumptions_latex: The Newton equations are \(-D\Delta x+A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y=r_d\) and \(A\Delta x=r_p\), with diagonal \(D\succ0\).
The constraint matrix \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solving the positive-definite normal equations and recovering \(\Delta x\) yields the unique solution of the augmented Newton system.

notation.meaning: Cholesky factor of the normal-equation matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-row-rank primal-dual Newton system reduced to positive-definite normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form \(N=A D^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) and \(g=r_p+A D^{-1}r_d\). Since \(D\succ0\) and \(A\) has full row rank, \(N\succ0\). Compute a Cholesky factorization \(N=L L^{\mathsf T}\), solve \(Lw=g\) and \(L^{\mathsf T}\Delta y=w\), and recover \[\Delta x=D^{-1}(A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y-r_d).\] Stop when the triangular solves and recovery are complete; output \((\Delta x,\Delta y)\). This pair satisfies both original block equations in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate the primal step, solve the positive-definite normal equations by Cholesky, and recover the primal step by diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Cholesky-Based Normal-Equation Solves

assumptions_latex: The augmented Newton matrix is \(K=\begin{bmatrix}-D&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), where \(D\succ0\).
The matrix \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A symmetric-indefinite factorization solves the augmented system without explicitly forming \(A D^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct symmetric-indefinite solution of a primal-dual augmented Newton system.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(r=(r_d,r_p)\), compute a symmetric-pivoted factorization \[P K P^{\mathsf T}=L\mathcal{D}L^{\mathsf T},\] where \(P\) is a permutation, \(L\) is unit lower triangular, and \(\mathcal{D}\) has nonsingular \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) diagonal blocks. Solve successively with \(L\), \(\mathcal{D}\), and \(L^{\mathsf T}\), then undo \(P\) to obtain \((\Delta x,\Delta y)\). The output solves \(K(\Delta x,\Delta y)^{\mathsf T}=r\) in exact arithmetic, while avoiding explicit normal-equation formation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply symmetric pivoting and an indefinite block factorization directly to the augmented Newton matrix, avoiding explicit normal equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric-Indefinite Augmented-System Solves

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

children.title: Primal Regularized Systems
children.top_down_role: Primal-side regularization choices within interior-point linear systems.

assumptions_latex: The unregularized augmented matrix has primal block \(-D\), with diagonal \(D\succ0\).
The primal regularizer is symmetric positive semidefinite: \(R_p\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal regularization replaces \(D\) by \(D+R_p\), increasing primal-block definiteness while perturbing the Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite regularization of the primal diagonal block in an augmented Newton system.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a residual vector \((r_d,r_p)\), the primal-regularized Newton system is \[K_p\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}r_d\\r_p\end{bmatrix},\qquad K_p=\begin{bmatrix}-(D+R_p)&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}.\] Because \(D+R_p\succ0\), elimination of \(\Delta x\) produces the positive-semidefinite Schur complement \(A(D+R_p)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\), which is positive definite when \(A\) has full row rank. Setting \(R_p=0\) recovers the unregularized augmented system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a positive-semidefinite matrix to the primal diagonal block; the resulting Schur complement uses the inverse of the enlarged block.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Regularized Systems

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

children.title: Dual Regularized Systems
children.top_down_role: Dual-side regularization choices within interior-point linear systems.

assumptions_latex: The primal block satisfies \(D\succ0\).
The dual regularizer is symmetric positive semidefinite: \(R_d\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual regularization adds \(R_d\) directly to the normal-equation matrix and perturbs the constraint equation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite regularization of the dual constraint block in an augmented Newton system.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a residual vector \((r_d,r_p)\), define the dual-regularized system by \[K_d\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}r_d\\r_p\end{bmatrix},\qquad K_d=\begin{bmatrix}-D&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&R_d\end{bmatrix}.\] Eliminating \(\Delta x\) yields \[(A D^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}+R_d)\Delta y=r_p+A D^{-1}r_d.\] Thus \(R_d\) acts additively on the normal-equation matrix. If \(R_d\succ0\), that matrix is positive definite even when \(A\) lacks full row rank. Setting \(R_d=0\) recovers the unregularized system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a positive-semidefinite dual block; after elimination it appears additively in the normal-equation matrix and can remove rank deficiency.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Regularized Systems

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

children.title: Cross-System Regularization Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Structural tradeoffs between primal-side, dual-side, or combined regularization.

assumptions_latex: The regularized augmented matrix is \(K_{p,d}=\begin{bmatrix}-(D+R_p)&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&R_d\end{bmatrix}\), with \(D\succ0\), \(R_p\succeq0\), and \(R_d\succeq0\).
Perturbation is measured relative to the unregularized Newton system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal and dual regularization improve different blocks, but both alter the computed Newton direction; their sizes must balance conditioning against perturbation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic conditioning-versus-perturbation tradeoff for combined primal and dual regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Eliminating the primal variable gives \[S_{p,d}=A(D+R_p)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}+R_d.\] Increasing \(R_d\) raises the Schur complement directly, whereas increasing \(R_p\) enlarges the inverted primal block and generally reduces the contribution \(A(D+R_p)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) in the Loewner order. Either change may improve factorization behavior of a deficient or badly scaled system, but it changes \(K_{p,d}\) and therefore the Newton direction. Consequently, regularization acceptance requires both a linear-solve quality test and a bound on the induced residual for the unregularized equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal regularization changes the inverse-weighted Schur term, while dual regularization adds to it directly; both trade numerical stability for Newton-equation perturbation.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-System Regularization Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Schur-complement formula and Loewner-order comparison are mathematically plausible, but the claims about factorization behavior and the required acceptance tests are nontrivial solver-design principles with no citation. A regularization-specific interior-point or numerical linear algebra source is required.

assumptions_latex: The matrix \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular, \(q\in\mathbb{N}\) is positive, and \(b_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\) for \(i=1,\ldots,q\).
A factorization of \(K\), or of one fixed permutation of \(K\), is available and remains unchanged for all right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The factorization is performed once and reused for all \(q\) systems; applying permutations and factors incurs work for each right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact factor reuse when the coefficient matrix, scaling, permutations, and factors are unchanged across several interior-point right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute one factorization of \(K\), such as \(PKQ=LU\) or a symmetric \(L\mathcal{D}L^{\mathsf T}\) factorization. Assemble \(B=[b_1\ \cdots\ b_q]\), apply the stored permutations, and perform the corresponding triangular and block-diagonal substitutions with all columns of \(B\). Undo the permutations to obtain \(X=[x_1\ \cdots\ x_q]\) satisfying \[KX=B.\] Reuse is valid only while \(K\), its scaling, its permutations, and its factors remain unchanged. Changing only a right-hand side does not require refactorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor an unchanged coefficient matrix once, then apply the same stored factors and permutations to every right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Right-Hand-Side Reuse

children.title: Factorization Quality Monitoring
children.top_down_role: Indicators associated with numerical quality of the computed factorization.

assumptions_latex: A scaled coefficient matrix \(K\) is represented computationally by factors satisfying \(P K Q\approx L U\).
The chosen matrix norm is submultiplicative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized factorization residual measures how accurately the stored factors represent the scaled coefficient matrix.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward-error-style diagnostic for stored factors of a scaled linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[R_F=P K Q-LU,\qquad \eta_F=\frac{\lVert R_F\rVert}{\lVert K\rVert+\lVert L\rVert\lVert U\rVert}.\] If the denominator is nonzero, \(0\le\eta_F\), and smaller values indicate that the computed factors more accurately reproduce the scaled coefficient matrix under the recorded permutations. This statistic tests the factors themselves; it does not include errors subsequently introduced by triangular solves, nor does it by itself bound forward error when \(K\) is ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure factorization quality by the normalized residual between the permuted coefficient matrix and the product of its computed factors.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Quality Monitoring

children.title: Solve-Residual Monitoring
children.top_down_role: Residual evidence associated with completed linear solves.

assumptions_latex: A computed vector \(\widehat x\) is intended to solve \(Kx=b\).
The selected vector and induced matrix norms use the same scaling convention as the solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The statistic \(\eta_s\) is a normwise relative backward-error indicator for the computed solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise residual monitoring for one scaled LP linear-system solve.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. LINEAR EQUATION AND INEQUALITY SYSTEMS

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \[r_s=b-K\widehat x,\qquad \eta_s=\frac{\lVert r_s\rVert}{\lVert K\rVert\lVert\widehat x\rVert+\lVert b\rVert},\] with \(\eta_s=0\) when numerator and denominator are both zero. The monitor accepts the solve only if \(\eta_s\le\tau_s\) for its configured tolerance \(\tau_s\). A small \(\eta_s\) means that \(\widehat x\) exactly solves a nearby normwise-perturbed system; it does not ensure small forward error without additional conditioning information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute the normalized residual of each linear solve and compare it with a configured tolerance; small residual alone does not guarantee small forward error.
knowledge_statements.title: Solve-Residual Monitoring

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 4. LINEAR EQUATION AND INEQUALITY SYSTEMS

children.title: Diagnostic Disagreement Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where factorization indicators and solve residuals support different assessments.

assumptions_latex: Factorization quality \(\eta_F\) and solve quality \(\eta_s\) are computed for the same scaled matrix, factors, and norm.
Warning thresholds \(\tau_F>0\) and \(\tau_s>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The four predicates separate jointly acceptable diagnostics, factor-only failure, solve-only failure, and joint failure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Four-way classification of factorization-residual and solve-residual threshold outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the diagnostic regime by \[\begin{array}{c|c|c} & \eta_s\le\tau_s & \eta_s>\tau_s\\ \hline \eta_F\le\tau_F & \text{jointly acceptable} & \text{solve-only failure}\\ \eta_F>\tau_F & \text{factor-only failure} & \text{joint failure}\end{array}\] A solve-only failure is consistent with inaccurate substitutions, residual evaluation, or a mismatched right-hand side despite acceptable factors. A factor-only failure indicates inaccurate factors even if the tested right-hand side happens to have a small residual. Joint failure supplies evidence against both factor representation and the resulting solve. These are classifications, not unique causal diagnoses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify factor and solve residuals jointly into acceptable, factor-only failure, solve-only failure, or joint failure, without treating the class as a unique cause.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagnostic Disagreement Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four Boolean regimes are exhaustive and correctly labeled, and the text appropriately avoids claiming unique causes. However, the causal interpretations and solver-specific threshold classification have no cited source, so the record requires authoritative numerical diagnostics support.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Solve Iterative Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative refinement of a simplex basis solve using a fixed computed factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonsingular basis matrix \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\), right-hand side \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), computed factors defining an approximate solve \(S_B\), tolerance \(\tau>0\), and limit \(J\), initialize \(x_0=S_B(b)\). For \(j=0,\ldots,J-1\), compute \(r_j=b-Bx_j\) in residual precision. If \(\beta_j=\|r_j\|/(\|B\|\|x_j\|+\|b\|)\leq\tau\), return \(x_j\). Otherwise compute \(c_j=S_B(r_j)\) and set \(x_{j+1}=x_j+c_j\). Return the first accepted iterate; if none exists, report refinement failure rather than accepting an uncertified basis solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly recompute the basis residual, solve for a correction with the existing factors, and accept only when the normwise backward error meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular.
\(S_B\) uses a computed factorization of \(B\).
\(\|B\|\|x_j\|+\|b\|>0\) for each tested iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta_j\leq\tau\) certifies the returned basis solution.

notation.meaning: Approximate solve using the stored basis factors.
Recomputed residual at refinement step j.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports basis-factor iterative refinement.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the basis-solve iterative-refinement container, but no source or inspectable locator supports the basis-factor policy. The domain of J is not stated, and the acceptance test certifies the displayed normwise backward-error criterion only, not forward accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier-System Iterative Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-correction refinement for a fixed primal-dual barrier Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Kz=g\) be a nonsingular barrier Newton system, possibly symmetric indefinite, and let \(S_K\) denote a solve with its computed factors. Initialize \(z_0=S_K(g)\). For \(j=0,\ldots,J-1\), recompute \(r_j=g-Kz_j\) from the uneliminated system. Accept \(z_j\) when \(\|r_j\|/(\|K\|\|z_j\|+\|g\|)\leq\tau\). Otherwise solve \(c_j=S_K(r_j)\) and update \(z_{j+1}=z_j+c_j\). If the corrections stagnate, become nonfinite, or fail the test by iteration \(J\), return a linear-solve failure indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refine a barrier Newton direction by recomputing its full-system residual and solving correction equations with the existing barrier-system factors.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is the fixed, nonsingular Newton-system matrix.
\(S_K\) applies a factorization compatible with the structure of \(K\).
\(\tau>0\) and \(J\in\mathbb{N}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|g-Kz_j\|\leq\tau(\|K\|\|z_j\|+\|g\|)\) for an accepted direction.

notation.meaning: Approximate solve using computed Newton-system factors.

review_flags: Exact refinement and acceptance policy may be implementation-specific.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and content kind fit the barrier-system refinement leaf, but the cited general linear-algebra locator does not establish the exact full-system residual, stagnation, nonfinite-output, and iteration-limit policy. A source specifically supporting this barrier-system refinement procedure is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Precision Iterative Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical mixed-precision refinement with low-precision factors and higher-precision residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given nonsingular \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\), low unit roundoff \(u_\ell\), and higher residual unit roundoff \(u_h<u_\ell\), factor \(A\) and solve \(Ax_0=b\) in precision \(u_\ell\), storing \(x_0\) in precision \(u_h\). At iteration \(j\), compute \(r_j=b-Ax_j\) in precision \(u_h\). If its backward error is at most \(\tau\), return \(x_j\); otherwise solve \(Ac_j=r_j\) with the low-precision factors, convert \(c_j\) to precision \(u_h\), and set \(x_{j+1}=x_j+c_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use low precision for factorization and correction solves, but higher precision for residuals and accumulated iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular.
\(u_h<u_\ell\).
Low-precision correction solves remain finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|b-Ax_j\|\leq\tau(\|A\|\|x_j\|+\|b\|)\) for the returned iterate.

notation.meaning: Unit roundoff used for factorization and correction solves.
Smaller unit roundoff used for residuals and updates.
Low-precision correction converted to higher precision.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports mixed-precision iterative refinement.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits mixed-precision iterative refinement, but no source is supplied. The statement does not define the backward-error expression or give the domain of tau, and it supplies no iteration limit or other failure termination rule.

children.title: Inexact Krylov Solves
children.top_down_role: Krylov-based linear solves operated under deliberately inexact accuracy regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Krylov Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-controlled Krylov solution of an LP linear-algebra subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear system \(Kd=g\), nonsingular preconditioner \(M\), forcing tolerance \(0<\eta<1\), and iteration limit \(J\), apply a Krylov method compatible with \(K\) and \(M\), starting from \(d_0\). At iteration \(j\), form \(r_j=g-Kd_j\) and stop successfully at the first index satisfying \(\|M^{-1}r_j\|\leq\eta\|M^{-1}g\|\). Return \(d_j\) and its measured residual. If no such index occurs by \(J\), return an inexact-solve failure indicator; the last iterate is not declared accurate solely because the iteration limit was reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preconditioned Krylov solve is accepted only when its measured preconditioned residual satisfies the prescribed forcing tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) are nonsingular.
The selected Krylov method is compatible with the operator and preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|M^{-1}(g-Kd_j)\|\leq\eta\|M^{-1}g\|\) for a successful return.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports residual-controlled preconditioned Krylov solves.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Residual-controlled iteration is appropriate for the inexact Krylov-solve leaf, but no supporting source is supplied. The norm, the domain of J, and the concrete compatibility requirements depend on the selected Krylov method and preconditioning convention.

children.title: Preconditioner Families
children.top_down_role: Preconditioning structures used to make iterative LP system solves practical.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator representations of left, right, and split preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Kx=b\) and nonsingular approximations \(M_L,M_R\), left preconditioning represents the system as \(M_L^{-1}Kx=M_L^{-1}b\); right preconditioning represents it as \(KM_R^{-1}y=b\) with \(x=M_R^{-1}y\); split preconditioning represents it as \(M_L^{-1}KM_R^{-1}y=M_L^{-1}b\) with \(x=M_R^{-1}y\). Common construction families choose these operators from diagonal scaling, block-diagonal or block-triangular approximations, incomplete factorizations, approximate Schur complements, or multilevel approximations. Every representation preserves the original exact solution when its preconditioning factors are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioners may act on the left, right, or both sides, using scaling, block, incomplete-factorization, Schur-complement, or multilevel approximations.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\).
\(M_L\) and \(M_R\) are nonsingular.
All transformed solves are interpreted in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Kx=b\) is equivalent to each displayed preconditioned system.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the stated preconditioner taxonomy.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind and the left, right, and split transformations fit the leaf and are algebraically consistent under nonsingular preconditioning factors. An inspectable numerical-linear-algebra source is still required for the stated construction-family taxonomy.

children.title: Krylov–Preconditioner Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility considerations linking Krylov families to preconditioner structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Krylov–Preconditioner Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural conditions under which standard preconditioned Krylov methods retain their defining guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Krylov–preconditioner pair is structurally compatible under the following standard conditions. Preconditioned conjugate gradients requires \(K\) symmetric positive definite and \(M\) symmetric positive definite. Preconditioned MINRES requires \(K\) symmetric and \(M\) symmetric positive definite, with preconditioning implemented so that self-adjointness is preserved in the induced inner product. GMRES permits a general nonsymmetric operator and nonsingular left or right preconditioner. If symmetry or positive definiteness required by conjugate gradients or MINRES is lost, their standard orthogonality, minimization, and convergence conclusions do not apply.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CG and MINRES require symmetry-preserving positive-definite preconditioning, while GMRES permits general nonsingular left or right preconditioners.
assumptions_latex: \(K,M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\).
The preconditioner application is fixed during an ordinary Krylov run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((K,M)\) is compatible only when the selected method's stated structural conditions hold.
review_flags: A numerical-linear-algebra source with method-specific hypotheses is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind fits this compatibility leaf, and the distinctions among CG, MINRES, and GMRES are standard. A method-specific authoritative source is required to support the exact symmetry, positive-definiteness, induced-inner-product, and fixed-preconditioner hypotheses.

children.title: Inexact-Solve Accuracy Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Accuracy regimes where iterative linear solves cease to support reliable outer iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Solve Accuracy Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-error limitation implied by residual control for an ill-conditioned linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, let \(d=K^{-1}g\), and let \(\widehat d\) have residual \(r=g-K\widehat d\). For any subordinate norm, \(\|\widehat d-d\|\leq\|K^{-1}\|\|r\|\), hence \(\|\widehat d-d\|/\|d\|\leq\kappa(K)\|r\|/\|g\|\), where \(\kappa(K)=\|K\|\|K^{-1}\|\). Therefore a relative residual threshold \(\eta\) gives only the bound \(\kappa(K)\eta\) on relative forward error. When \(\kappa(K)\eta\) is not small, residual acceptance alone does not certify an accurate direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small residual need not imply a small solution error when the linear system is ill-conditioned; the amplification factor is the condition number.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular.
\(\|\cdot\|\) is a subordinate matrix-vector norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|r\|/\|g\|\leq\eta\Rightarrow\|\widehat d-d\|/\|d\|\leq\kappa(K)\eta\).

notation.meaning: Condition number in the selected subordinate norm.

review_flags: Locator must be checked for the explicit condition-number bound.

children.title: Precision Escalation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Transitions from lower-precision computation to more accurate arithmetic.

knowledge_statements.title: Precision Escalation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone precision escalation governed by a backward-error acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose available arithmetic levels with unit roundoffs \(u_1>u_2>\cdots>u_L\), an acceptance tolerance \(\tau\), and per-level refinement limits \(J_1,\ldots,J_L\). At level \(\ell\), factor or refactor the current matrix, compute a candidate solution, and perform at most \(J_\ell\) refinement steps. Accept the first candidate \(x\) satisfying \(\|b-Ax\|\leq\tau(\|A\|\|x\|+\|b\|)\). If the test fails, arithmetic is nonfinite, or factorization breaks down, advance to \(\ell+1\). Report exhaustion if no level is accepted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Try progressively smaller unit roundoffs, accepting the first solve that satisfies a common backward-error test and reporting failure after the last level.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned solution satisfies \(\|b-Ax\|\leq\tau(\|A\|\|x\|+\|b\|)\).

notation.meaning: Unit roundoff at escalation level l.

review_flags: Precision hierarchy and triggers are implementation policies requiring a dedicated source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the precision-escalation leaf, but the ordered precision levels, per-level refinement limits, escalation events, and common acceptance policy are implementation choices with no supplied source.

children.title: Linear-Solver Fallback Paths
children.top_down_role: Alternative linear-solver families used after a primary solver becomes unreliable.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Solver Fallback Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated traversal of an ordered family of solvers for the same linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Ax=b\), tolerance \(\tau\), and an ordered list of solver configurations \((S_1,\ldots,S_p)\), run \(S_j(A,b)\) sequentially. A configuration may change scaling, ordering, pivoting, factorization, preconditioning, or arithmetic precision, but must represent the same unregularized system unless model alteration is explicitly authorized. After each finite candidate \(x_j\), recompute \(r_j=b-Ax_j\) independently and accept only if \(\|r_j\|\leq\tau(\|A\|\|x_j\|+\|b\|)\). Otherwise continue to \(S_{j+1}\). If every configuration fails, return exhaustion together with the recorded diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Traverse an ordered list of solver configurations, independently validate every candidate, and preserve the original system unless regularization is explicitly authorized.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
\((S_1,\ldots,S_p)\) is finite and ordered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful fallback returns \(x_j\) with \(\|b-Ax_j\|\leq\tau(\|A\|\|x_j\|+\|b\|)\).

notation.meaning: Solver configuration at fallback stage j.

review_flags: The ordered fallback architecture is implementation-specific and lacks a supplied source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the fallback-path container, but the ordered traversal, independent validation rule, and prohibition on changing the unregularized system are implementation-policy claims without an inspectable supporting source.

children.title: Escalation Trigger Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic conditions motivating a change in precision.

knowledge_statements.title: Escalation Trigger Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit diagnostic predicate for advancing to a stronger linear-solver configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For solver stage \(j\), define backward errors \(\beta_k=\|b-Ax_k\|/(\|A\|\|x_k\|+\|b\|)\). Given tolerance \(\tau\), stagnation ratio \(\rho\in(0,1]\), window \(q\), and conditioning cap \(\Gamma\), escalation is triggered when at least one predicate holds: factorization or iteration breaks down; a computed quantity is nonfinite; \(\beta_k>\tau\) after the stage limit; \(\beta_k/\beta_{k-q}\geq\rho\); or an available condition estimate exceeds \(\Gamma\). If none holds and \(\beta_k\leq\tau\), the stage is accepted rather than escalated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Escalate after breakdown, nonfinite arithmetic, excessive backward error, sustained stagnation, or an excessive condition estimate; otherwise accept a tolerance-satisfying solve.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau>0\), \(\rho\in(0,1]\), and \(q\in\mathbb{N}\).
The backward-error denominator is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_k=1\) exactly when at least one stated escalation predicate holds.

notation.meaning: Normwise backward error at iteration k.

review_flags: Threshold choices and the combined trigger predicate are implementation-specific.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the trigger-boundary leaf, but the combined trigger predicate and thresholds are unsupported implementation policy. In addition, T_k appears only in the conclusion and is never defined, and the stagnation ratio requires an explicit condition such as k at least q with a nonzero denominator.

children.title: Fallback Exhaustion Outcomes
children.top_down_role: Outcomes reached when available linear-solver substitutions remain inadequate.

assumptions_latex: \((S_1,\ldots,S_p)\) contains every configured fallback stage.
Each candidate is checked against the same backward-error tolerance \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall j,\ \beta_j>\tau\text{ or stage }j\text{ fails}\Rightarrow\text{numerical recovery failure only}.\)

notation.meaning: Validation backward error for stage j.

review_flags: A solver-status or implementation standard is needed to support the outcome semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Permissible conclusions after every configured linear-solver recovery stage fails validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((S_1,\ldots,S_p)\) be the complete configured fallback list for \(Ax=b\). If every stage either breaks down, produces nonfinite output, or returns \(x_j\) with \(\|b-Ax_j\|>\tau(\|A\|\|x_j\|+\|b\|)\), then the only certified conclusion is that the configured numerical recovery hierarchy failed to produce an accepted solution. This event does not by itself certify that \(A\) is singular, nor that the underlying linear program is infeasible or unbounded. The solver must return numerical failure or indeterminate status with diagnostics, rather than an optimization-status certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhausting all fallback solvers certifies numerical recovery failure only; it does not establish singularity, infeasibility, or unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.title: Fallback Exhaustion Outcomes

children.title: Rank-Deficient Systems
children.top_down_role: Linear systems exhibiting structural or numerical rank loss.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solvability and nonuniqueness of a finite-dimensional rank-deficient linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<\min\{m,n\}\). The system \(Ax=b\) is consistent exactly when \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\). If it is consistent and \(x_0\) is one solution, then every solution is of the form \(x=x_0+z\) with \(z\in\ker(A)\). Consequently, when \(\ker(A)\neq\{0\}\), a consistent system has infinitely many solutions; when \(b\notin\operatorname{range}(A)\), it has no exact solution. A unique solution therefore cannot be inferred from a rank-deficient square coefficient matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-deficient system is solvable exactly when the right-hand side lies in the matrix range; consistent solutions differ by null-space vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\).
\(\operatorname{rank}(A)<\min\{m,n\}\).
\(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\text{ is solvable}\iff b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\), and its solution set is \(x_0+\ker(A)\) when nonempty.

notation.meaning: Any particular solution of the consistent system.

source_refs.locator: Rank of the Matrix \( A \) p. 31

children.title: Nearly Dependent Systems
children.top_down_role: Systems whose rows or columns are numerically close to dependence.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular.
Computations use floating-point arithmetic with unit roundoff \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Small relative perturbations can produce large relative solution changes when \(\kappa_2(A)u\) is not small.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional square systems measured in the spectral norm.

source_refs.locator: Rank of the Matrix \( A \) p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonsingular system \(Ax=b\) is nearly dependent at working precision when its smallest singular value is small relative to its largest, so \(\kappa_2(A)=\sigma_{\max}(A)/\sigma_{\min}(A)\) is large. For perturbations \(A+\Delta A\) and \(b+\Delta b\), the solution sensitivity is amplified by a factor governed by \(\kappa_2(A)\). Consequently, when \(\kappa_2(A)u\) is not much less than \(1\), computed solutions may lose substantial accuracy even though \(A\) has exact full rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-rank system is numerically nearly dependent when its condition number is so large that roundoff or small data perturbations can severely change its solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Nearly Dependent Systems

source_witnesses.locator: Rank of the Matrix \( A \) p. 31

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition-number characterization is standard, but the cited rank discussion does not inspectably support the perturbation-sensitivity and working-precision claims.

children.title: Rank-Loss Detection Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Threshold-sensitive distinctions between effective rank loss and near dependence.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and a detection threshold \(\tau>0\) are given.
A rank-revealing factorization or singular-value estimate is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Numerical rank is threshold-dependent whenever singular values lie near \(\tau\sigma_1(A)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold-based numerical rank, distinct from exact algebraic rank.

source_refs.locator: Rank of the Matrix \( A \) p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q=\min\{m,n\}\) and let \(\sigma_1(A)\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_q(A)\geq0\). The thresholded numerical rank is \[r_\tau(A)=\#\{i:\sigma_i(A)>\tau\sigma_1(A)\}.\] Rank loss is detected when \(r_\tau(A)<q\). This boundary is not intrinsic: if some \(\sigma_i(A)\) is comparable to \(\tau\sigma_1(A)\), perturbations or a different threshold can change the reported rank. Reliable detection therefore requires recording the threshold, scaling convention, and rank-revealing quantity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank loss is detected by comparing singular-value or factorization estimates with a stated relative threshold; values near that threshold make the diagnosis inherently ambiguous.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Loss Detection Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: Rank of the Matrix \( A \) p. 31

children.title: Small-Pivot Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Factorization difficulties associated with weak or unstable pivots.

assumptions_latex: Gaussian elimination is applied to \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) in floating-point arithmetic.
At elimination step \(k\), the selected pivot is \(p_k\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A pivot small relative to its active column permits large multipliers and amplifies rounding error or element growth.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Floating-point Gaussian elimination used within LP linear solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At step \(k\), elimination forms multipliers \(l_{ik}=a^{(k)}_{ik}/p_k\). A small-pivot pathology occurs when \(|p_k|\) is small relative to \(\max_{i\geq k}|a^{(k)}_{ik}|\), making some \(|l_{ik}|\) large. The subsequent update \(a^{(k+1)}_{ij}=a^{(k)}_{ij}-l_{ik}a^{(k)}_{kj}\) can then magnify rounding errors and intermediate entries. A nonzero pivot therefore prevents exact breakdown but does not ensure numerical reliability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero but relatively tiny pivot creates large elimination multipliers, which can magnify intermediate entries and floating-point errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Small-Pivot Pathologies

children.title: Numerical-Growth Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Amplification phenomena that degrade factorization reliability.

assumptions_latex: A floating-point elimination factorization of \(A\neq0\) produces active matrices \(A^{(k)}\).
Unit roundoff is \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Large element growth enlarges the factorization's backward-error scale even when elimination completes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Element growth during floating-point elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the element-growth factor by \[\rho=\frac{\max_{k,i,j}|a^{(k)}_{ij}|}{\max_{i,j}|a_{ij}|}.\] Numerical-growth pathology occurs when \(\rho\gg1\): intermediate elimination entries greatly exceed the scale of the input. Standard floating-point error bounds then scale with a dimension-dependent multiple of \(u\rho\), so a large \(\rho\) can yield a poor backward error despite a completed factorization and moderate input entries. Overflow is an extreme manifestation when an intermediate entry exceeds the representable range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elimination is numerically hazardous when intermediate entries grow far beyond the input scale, enlarging backward error and potentially causing overflow.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Growth Pathologies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For unrestricted elimination, a backward-error bound cannot generally be summarized solely by a dimension-dependent multiple of unit roundoff times the stated element-growth factor; the pivoting and multiplier hypotheses must be sourced and specified.

children.title: Pivot–Growth Coupling
children.top_down_role: Failure regimes where pivot selection and numerical growth reinforce one another.

assumptions_latex: Elimination uses pivot \(p_k\) and multipliers \(l_{ik}=a^{(k)}_{ik}/p_k\).
The pivoting rule does not uniformly bound all multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A relatively small pivot can initiate large multipliers and element growth, while suitable pivoting can suppress this mechanism.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mechanistic coupling between pivot size, multipliers, and element growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(l_{ik}=a^{(k)}_{ik}/p_k\), choosing \(|p_k|\ll\max_{i\geq k}|a^{(k)}_{ik}|\) produces a large multiplier. The update \(a^{(k+1)}_{ij}=a^{(k)}_{ij}-l_{ik}a^{(k)}_{kj}\) can consequently create entries much larger than those in \(A^{(k)}\), increasing \(\rho\). Under partial pivoting, \(|l_{ik}|\leq1\) for the selected column, which controls this local amplification mechanism, although cumulative element growth can still be large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small pivots create large multipliers that can drive element growth; pivoting bounds the local mechanism but cannot rule out cumulative growth.
knowledge_statements.title: Pivot–Growth Coupling

children.title: Factorization Fill Growth
children.top_down_role: Unexpected nonzero growth during sparse factorization.

assumptions_latex: A sparse matrix \(A\) is factored as \(PAQ=LU\), or symmetrically as \(PAP^{\mathsf T}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\).
Structural nonzeros are counted after an ordering is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fill is the set of factor nonzeros absent from the correspondingly permuted input pattern.

notation.meaning: Fill ratio for an LU factorization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural fill after sparse-factorization ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed sparse ordering, factorization fill consists of structural nonzeros created in \(L\) or \(U\) that are absent from the relevant lower or upper pattern of \(PAQ\). A scalar summary is \[\phi=\frac{\operatorname{nnz}(L)+\operatorname{nnz}(U)}{\operatorname{nnz}(A)}.\] Fill growth means that \(\phi\), or the absolute factor nonzero count, becomes large. It increases factor storage and generally increases factorization and triangular-solve work, independently of whether the factors are numerically stable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factorization fill comprises new structural nonzeros in sparse factors; its growth increases factor storage and usually computational work.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Fill Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is plausible and fits the leaf, but the cited generic LU-factorization locator does not inspectably support sparse fill, the fill ratio, or the storage and work consequences.

children.title: Memory Exhaustion Regimes
children.top_down_role: Resource failures caused by factor storage or workspace demand.

assumptions_latex: The factorization requires \(S_F\) bytes of factor and workspace storage.
At most \(M\) bytes are available to the solver process.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The in-core factorization is infeasible whenever \(S_F>M\).

notation.meaning: Bytes per stored numerical entry including associated indexing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: In-core sparse factorization under a fixed memory budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_F\) include numerical factors, indices, elimination-tree data, fronts, and peak temporary workspace. The in-core factorization enters a memory-exhaustion regime when \(S_F>M\), where \(M\) is the available process memory. Even if final-factor storage satisfies \(b(\operatorname{nnz}(L)+\operatorname{nnz}(U))\leq M\), peak workspace can make \(S_F>M\). In this regime the requested factorization cannot complete in core without changing ordering, representation, precision, algorithm, or memory resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Memory exhaustion occurs when factors plus peak workspace exceed available memory, even if the final factors alone would fit.
knowledge_statements.title: Memory Exhaustion Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary is implementation-dependent, and the cited LU section does not inspectably support the asserted storage components, peak-workspace model, or prescribed remedies.

children.title: Fill-Control Failure
children.top_down_role: Cases where ordering or sparsity controls fail to contain memory growth.

assumptions_latex: A fill-control policy accepts only orderings or factor patterns satisfying a budget \(B\).
Every admissible candidate needed for the solve exceeds that budget or destroys required numerical adequacy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fill policy cannot produce a factorization satisfying both the resource and numerical requirements.

notation.meaning: Resource cost under ordering or pattern q

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract boundary for ordering and dropping policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\) range over orderings or permitted factor-pattern choices, let \(F(q)\) be their predicted or observed resource cost, and let \(N(q)\) assert numerical acceptability. Fill control fails at budget \(B\) when \[\nexists q\;\bigl(F(q)\leq B\ \wedge\ N(q)\bigr).\] This includes structural failure, where all viable orderings create excessive fill, and numerical failure, where dropping or restricting fill meets the budget only by producing unstable factors or an unacceptable solve residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fill control fails when no permitted ordering or sparsification choice simultaneously meets the resource budget and numerical-accuracy requirement.
knowledge_statements.title: Fill-Control Failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract policy-relative condition fits the leaf, but no evidence is supplied for the fill-control model or its structural and numerical failure taxonomy.

children.title: Factorization Breakdown Modes
children.top_down_role: Numerical or structural modes that prevent successful factorization.

assumptions_latex: A direct factorization is attempted in finite precision.
Solver pivot, growth, residual, and resource thresholds are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Breakdown occurs when no admissible next factorization operation satisfies the solver's numerical and resource acceptance tests.

notation.meaning: Active pivot candidate set at step k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational breakdown of direct LP linear-system factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At step \(k\), numerical pivot breakdown occurs if \(\nexists p\in P_k\) satisfying the solver's pivot admissibility predicate \(C_k(p)\). Factorization also breaks down if an intermediate value is nonfinite, observed growth exceeds its limit, required storage exceeds \(M\), or the completed factors fail their residual or inertia test. These modes distinguish exact structural singularity from finite-precision rejection: an algebraically possible factorization may still be operationally unacceptable under the declared thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factorization can break down through absent acceptable pivots, nonfinite arithmetic, excessive growth, memory exhaustion, or failure of post-factorization checks.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Breakdown Modes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed breakdown modes combine solver-specific pivot, growth, memory, residual, and inertia tests without an authoritative source defining their scope or acceptance thresholds.

children.title: Factorization Recovery Strategies
children.top_down_role: Solver responses intended to restore a usable factorization.

assumptions_latex: An initial factorization attempt has failed a declared numerical or resource test.
A finite ordered set of recovery configurations \(R=(r_1,\ldots,r_s)\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns the first configuration passing all acceptance tests, or reports recovery failure after exhausting \(R\).

notation.meaning: Acceptance predicate for a computed factorization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic bounded recovery controller for direct factorizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the failed system, acceptance predicate \(T\), and ordered recovery list \(R=(r_1,\ldots,r_s)\). For \(j=1,\ldots,s\), configuration \(r_j\) may rescale or reorder the matrix, strengthen pivoting, add regularization, increase precision, switch factorization form, or relax a resource representation. Compute \(F_j\) and its diagnostic quantities. Stop and output \(F_j\) only if \(T(F_j)\) holds. If every attempt fails or exceeds its resource limit, output a recovery-failure status together with the attempted configurations and diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retry with a bounded sequence of scaling, ordering, pivoting, regularization, precision, or factorization changes, accepting only a factorization that passes diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Recovery Strategies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate knowledge kind, but the recovery operations and their ordered controller are solver-dependent and have no cited support.

children.title: Unrecoverable Factorization Outcomes
children.top_down_role: Terminal cases where available recovery mechanisms remain insufficient.

assumptions_latex: A required linear system and acceptance predicate \(T\) are fixed.
All authorized recovery configurations \(r\in R\) have been attempted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The outcome is unrecoverable within policy exactly when no authorized attempt produces an accepted factorization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy-relative termination, not proof that no mathematical factorization exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A factorization outcome is unrecoverable relative to the authorized recovery set \(R\) when \[\forall r\in R,\quad F(r)\text{ is not produced or }T(F(r))\text{ is false}.\] The terminal diagnostic must distinguish at least structural or numerical singularity, exhausted memory, nonfinite arithmetic, and persistent residual or inertia failure. This condition certifies only that the configured solver has exhausted its allowed remedies; it does not imply that no alternative algorithm, precision, formulation, or hardware resource could solve the system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure is unrecoverable only relative to the solver's authorized remedies; it does not prove that every algorithm or formulation must fail.
knowledge_statements.title: Unrecoverable Factorization Outcomes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The policy-relative condition is clearly delimited and fits the leaf, but its required terminal diagnostic classes and acceptance policy are unsupported.

children.title: Solver Outcome Acceptance-Certification System
children.top_down_role: Accuracy semantics and computational evidence used to accept, qualify, reject, or independently verify solver outcomes.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Tolerances; Types of Solutions; presolved versus input-model feasibility

assumptions_latex: The primal LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ \ell\leq x\leq u\}\).
Absolute and relative tolerances \(\tau_a,\tau_r\geq0\) and positive row scales \(s_i\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A candidate is accepted as primal feasible exactly when every scaled equality and bound violation satisfies the declared mixed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed absolute-relative acceptance test with explicit scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidate \(x\), define \(r_p=Ax-b\), lower-bound violation \(v_j^\ell=(\ell_j-x_j)_+\), and upper-bound violation \(v_j^u=(x_j-u_j)_+\), omitting infinite bounds. Given positive scales \(s_i\) and \(t_j\), accept primal feasibility when \[|(r_p)_i|\leq\tau_a+\tau_r s_i\quad\text{for every }i,\] and \[v_j^\ell\leq\tau_a+\tau_r t_j,\qquad v_j^u\leq\tau_a+\tau_r t_j\quad\text{for every applicable }j.\] The reported status must identify the scaling convention and both tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility requires every equality and bound violation to lie below a declared mixed absolute-relative threshold under stated row and variable scaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Feasibility Tolerances

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mixed absolute-relative test is a possible solver convention, not a universal primal-feasibility criterion. The cited primal-dual framework locator does not inspectably support the particular row and variable scaling formulas.

children.title: Dual Feasibility Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Tolerance regimes governing dual constraint satisfaction.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
The primal-dual form is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge 0\}\).
A nonnegative absolute tolerance \(\tau_d\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_d= A^Ty+s-c\) and \(v_d=\max\{\|r_d\|_\infty,\|(-s)_+\|_\infty\}\). Dual feasibility is accepted at absolute tolerance \(\tau_d\) precisely when \(v_d\le\tau_d\). Equivalently, every equality residual satisfies \(|(r_d)_j|\le\tau_d\), and every dual slack satisfies \(s_j\ge-\tau_d\). For a scaled test, the same predicate applies after replacing \(v_d\) by a declared dimensionless normalization; the normalization must be reported with the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute dual-feasibility test for the equality-form primal-dual LP pair.

source_refs.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a candidate \((y,s)\), define the dual residual \(r_d=A^Ty+s-c\) and the dual-feasibility violation \(v_d=\max\{\|r_d\|_\infty,\|(-s)_+\|_\infty\}\). The candidate satisfies the absolute dual-feasibility tolerance \(\tau_d\ge0\) if and only if \(v_d\le\tau_d\). Thus the test simultaneously controls the dual equality and nonnegativity of the slack. Any relative or scaled variant must state its denominator explicitly, because changing that denominator changes the acceptance predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual feasibility is accepted when both the stationarity residual and every negative dual slack are no larger than the declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Feasibility Tolerances

source_witnesses.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

children.title: Reduced-Cost Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Tolerance regimes governing reduced-cost quality.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
The primal is a minimization problem with variables constrained by \(x\ge0\).
A nonnegative tolerance \(\tau_{rc}\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced-cost vector is \(\bar c=c-A^Ty\). Approximate reduced-cost feasibility holds exactly when \(\|(-\bar c)_+\|_\infty\le\tau_{rc}\), equivalently \(\bar c_j\ge-\tau_{rc}\) for every \(j\). If a separately stored slack \(s\) is used, reduced-cost acceptance alone does not certify \(s=\bar c\); that identity requires an additional consistency test.

notation.meaning: Reduced-cost vector induced by the dual multiplier.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost sign test for nonnegative variables in a minimization LP.

source_refs.source_title: Network Optimization: Continuous and Discrete Models

source_refs.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization form with \(x\ge0\), the reduced costs induced by \(y\) are \(\bar c=c-A^Ty\). The candidate passes the absolute reduced-cost tolerance \(\tau_{rc}\ge0\) if and only if \(\|(-\bar c)_+\|_\infty\le\tau_{rc}\), or equivalently \(\bar c_j\ge-\tau_{rc}\) for all \(j\). This convention reverses for an oppositely signed primal or dual formulation, so the model form is part of the diagnostic specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced costs pass when none is more negative than the declared tolerance under the stated minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Tolerances
