children.title: Dual–Reduced-Cost Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency checks connecting dual feasibility assessments to reduced-cost assessments.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(c,s\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
Reduced costs use the convention \(\bar c=c-A^Ty\).
A nonnegative consistency tolerance \(\tau_{cons}\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual slack and reduced cost are tolerance-consistent precisely when \(\|s-\bar c\|_\infty=\|A^Ty+s-c\|_\infty\le\tau_{cons}\). Therefore separate sign tests on \(s\) and \(\bar c\) are interchangeable only up to this discrepancy: \(\|(-s)_+\|_\infty\le\|(-\bar c)_+\|_\infty+\tau_{cons}\), and symmetrically with \(s\) and \(\bar c\) exchanged.

notation.meaning: Reduced-cost vector computed from the multiplier.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency identity between stored dual slacks and recomputed reduced costs.

source_refs.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar c=c-A^Ty\) be the reduced costs recomputed from \(y\), and let \(s\) be the stored dual slack. Since \(s-\bar c=A^Ty+s-c\), the consistency discrepancy equals the dual equality residual. Hence \(s\) and \(\bar c\) are consistent at tolerance \(\tau_{cons}\ge0\) exactly when \(\|s-\bar c\|_\infty\le\tau_{cons}\). Moreover, their negative-part violations can differ by at most \(\tau_{cons}\), so passing one sign test need not imply passing the other when distinct tolerances are used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stored dual slacks and recomputed reduced costs agree exactly up to the dual stationarity residual; inconsistent tolerance decisions expose a diagnostic mismatch.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual–Reduced-Cost Consistency

source_witnesses.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

children.title: Complementarity Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Acceptance regimes for complementarity quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Tolerances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute componentwise and aggregate complementarity tests for nonnegative primal-slack pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonnegative \(x\) and \(s\), define the componentwise complementarity violation \(v_c=\|x\odot s\|_\infty\) and aggregate complementarity \(g_c=x^Ts\). A componentwise tolerance accepts the pair when \(v_c\le\tau_c\); an aggregate tolerance accepts it when \(g_c\le\tau_c^{\Sigma}\). Because all products are nonnegative, \(v_c\le g_c\le n v_c\). Thus the diagnostic must identify which measure and threshold it uses; equal numerical thresholds do not define identical acceptance regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementarity may be tested by the largest primal-slack product or by their sum; these differently aggregated tests require explicitly distinguished tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(x,s\in\mathbb{R}^n_+\) are primal variables and dual slacks for the canonical primal-dual LP pair.
Nonnegative tolerances \(\tau_c\) and \(\tau_c^{\Sigma}\) are prescribed for the componentwise and aggregate tests, respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Componentwise complementarity is accepted when \(v_c=\|x\odot s\|_\infty\le\tau_c\). Aggregate complementarity is accepted when \(g_c=x^Ts\le\tau_c^{\Sigma}\). For nonnegative \(x\) and \(s\), \(v_c\le g_c\le n v_c\); consequently, componentwise and aggregate tolerances are equivalent only after accounting for their different aggregation and the factor \(n\).

notation.meaning: Hadamard product of primal variables and dual slacks.

children.title: Objective-Gap Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Acceptance regimes for primal–dual objective-gap quality.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
Candidate points satisfy primal and dual feasibility exactly.
A nonnegative objective-gap tolerance \(\tau_g\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The absolute gap criterion is \(0\le g=c^Tx-b^Ty=x^Ts\le\tau_g\). A relative criterion may instead require \(g/(1+|c^Tx|+|b^Ty|)\le\tau_g^{rel}\). The denominator and whether feasibility is exact or approximate must be declared; otherwise the reported tolerance does not uniquely determine acceptance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute and relative objective-gap tests under exact primal-dual feasibility.

source_refs.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For exactly feasible \((x,y,s)\), weak duality gives \(g=c^Tx-b^Ty\ge0\), and the primal-dual identities give \(g=x^Ts\). The absolute objective-gap test accepts when \(g\le\tau_g\). One dimensionless relative test accepts when \(g/(1+|c^Tx|+|b^Ty|)\le\tau_g^{rel}\). The chosen denominator is part of the criterion: alternative normalizations generally produce different decisions near the threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exactly feasible primal-dual pair passes when its nonnegative objective gap, absolute or explicitly normalized, is below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Gap Tolerances

source_witnesses.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

children.title: Complementarity–Gap Disagreement
children.top_down_role: Cases where complementarity and objective-gap measures imply different solution quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity–Gap Disagreement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual identity explaining disagreement between complementarity and objective-gap diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For arbitrary candidates, let \(r_p=Ax-b\) and \(r_d=A^Ty+s-c\). Direct substitution yields \(c^Tx-b^Ty=x^Ts-x^Tr_d+y^Tr_p\). Thus the objective gap and aggregate complementarity disagree by \(y^Tr_p-x^Tr_d\), which vanishes under exact primal and dual feasibility but need not be small merely because each residual is below an absolute tolerance. Quantitatively, the disagreement is at most \(\|x\|_1\|r_d\|_\infty+\|y\|_1\|r_p\|_\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective gap equals aggregate complementarity only under cancellation of the residual terms; large candidate norms can amplify small feasibility residuals into visible disagreement.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b,y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c,x,s\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
The primal and dual residuals are \(r_p=Ax-b\) and \(r_d=A^Ty+s-c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact identity is \(c^Tx-b^Ty=x^Ts-x^Tr_d+y^Tr_p\). Hence complementarity and objective gap agree only when \(y^Tr_p-x^Tr_d=0\), in particular under exact primal-dual feasibility. Their disagreement is bounded by \(|(c^Tx-b^Ty)-x^Ts|\le\|x\|_1\|r_d\|_\infty+\|y\|_1\|r_p\|_\infty\).

source_refs.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

source_witnesses.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

assumptions_latex: A diagnostic residual or discrepancy is represented by \(r\in\mathbb{R}^k\).
A norm \(\|\cdot\|\) and an absolute tolerance \(\tau_{abs}\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The absolute-error regime accepts exactly the set \(\mathcal A_{abs}=\{r\in\mathbb{R}^k:\|r\|\le\tau_{abs}\}\). This predicate is independent of any reference magnitude but is not invariant under a rescaling \(r\mapsto\alpha r\): for \(\alpha>0\), acceptance becomes \(\|r\|\le\tau_{abs}/\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-based absolute residual acceptance without magnitude normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a residual \(r\in\mathbb{R}^k\), a fixed norm \(\|\cdot\|\), and \(\tau_{abs}\ge0\), the absolute-error regime declares the diagnostic acceptable exactly when \(\|r\|\le\tau_{abs}\). Its acceptance region is \(\mathcal A_{abs}=\{r:\|r\|\le\tau_{abs}\}\). No problem-data or reference magnitude appears in this predicate. Consequently, changing units or scaling the underlying equation changes the decision unless the tolerance is scaled by the same factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An absolute-error regime accepts a residual solely by comparing its norm with a fixed tolerance, making the decision sensitive to units and scaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute-Error Regimes

assumptions_latex: A measured quantity is \(q\) and its reference value is \(q_{ref}\), both in a normed vector space.
A floor \(\sigma>0\) and relative tolerance \(\tau_{rel}\ge0\) are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relative error is \(e_{rel}=\|q-q_{ref}\|/\max\{\sigma,\|q_{ref}\|\}\), and the regime accepts exactly when \(e_{rel}\le\tau_{rel}\). For any \(\alpha>0\), simultaneous scaling of \(q\), \(q_{ref}\), and \(\sigma\) by \(\alpha\) leaves \(e_{rel}\) unchanged. The positive floor prevents division by zero but determines behavior near a zero reference.

notation.meaning: Reference quantity against which discrepancy is measured.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Floored normwise relative-error regime with explicit zero-reference handling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a measured quantity \(q\), reference \(q_{ref}\), norm \(\|\cdot\|\), and floor \(\sigma>0\), define \(e_{rel}=\|q-q_{ref}\|/\max\{\sigma,\|q_{ref}\|\}\). The relative-error regime accepts exactly when \(e_{rel}\le\tau_{rel}\). If \(q\), \(q_{ref}\), and \(\sigma\) are multiplied by the same positive scalar, the ratio is unchanged. The floor is essential when \(q_{ref}=0\), and its declared value is part of the acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative regime divides discrepancy by a floored reference magnitude, gaining common-scale invariance while requiring an explicit rule near zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Error Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The floored denominator is a specific diagnostic convention, but the cited termination section has not been shown to support this exact formula, its common-scale invariance, or the role of the floor. A source with an inspectable relative-residual definition is required.

children.title: Scaled Error Regimes
children.top_down_role: Accuracy assessments expressed relative to solver or model scaling.

assumptions_latex: A residual is \(r\in\mathbb{R}^k\).
A nonsingular diagonal scaling matrix \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times k}\) is fixed.
A tolerance \(\tau_s\ge0\) and norm \(\|\cdot\|\) are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled error is \(e_s=\|Dr\|\), and the regime accepts precisely when \(e_s\le\tau_s\). For diagonal \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)\) and the infinity norm, this is equivalent to \(|r_i|\le\tau_s/|d_i|\) for every \(i\). Thus scaling implements component-dependent absolute tolerances in the original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual acceptance after a fixed nonsingular diagonal coordinate scaling.

source_refs.locator: 8.6 Affine Scaling, Primal-Dual Path Following, and Predictor-Corrector Variants of Interior Point Methods p. 428

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r\in\mathbb{R}^k\) be a residual and \(D\) a fixed nonsingular diagonal matrix. A scaled-error regime measures \(e_s=\|Dr\|\) and accepts when \(e_s\le\tau_s\). With \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)\) and \(\|\cdot\|_\infty\), acceptance is equivalent to \(|r_i|\le\tau_s/|d_i|\) for all \(i\). Hence the scaling matrix determines the relative weighting of residual components and must accompany any reported scaled tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled-error regime applies a fixed coordinate scaling before measuring the residual, thereby imposing component-specific tolerances in original units.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Error Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 8.6 Affine Scaling, Primal-Dual Path Following, and Predictor-Corrector Variants of Interior Point Methods p. 428

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical definition is coherent, but a section on affine-scaling algorithms does not by itself support the asserted solver-diagnostic regime \(\|Dr\|\le\tau_s\). An inspectable source on scaled residual tests or solver stopping criteria is required.

children.title: Normalized Error Regimes
children.top_down_role: Accuracy assessments expressed through dimensionless normalization.

assumptions_latex: A residual is \(r\in\mathbb{R}^k\).
A positive scale functional \(S\) is evaluated on declared problem data \(z\), with \(S(z)>0\).
A normalized tolerance \(\tau_n\ge0\) and norm \(\|\cdot\|\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized error is \(e_n=\|r\|/S(z)\), and acceptance is exactly \(e_n\le\tau_n\). If \(r\mapsto\alpha r\) and \(S(z)\mapsto\alpha S(z)\) for \(\alpha>0\), then \(e_n\) is invariant. Different positive choices of \(S\) generally define different acceptance regions, so the normalization functional is part of the diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionless residual acceptance using an explicit positive problem-data normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r\in\mathbb{R}^k\) be a residual and let \(S(z)>0\) be a declared scalar scale computed from problem data or reference quantities \(z\). A normalized-error regime defines \(e_n=\|r\|/S(z)\) and accepts exactly when \(e_n\le\tau_n\). If both the residual and scale transform by the same positive factor, \(e_n\) is unchanged. Because alternative choices of \(S\) need not be proportional, the formula for \(S\) is an indispensable part of the tolerance specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized regime divides a residual norm by an explicit positive problem scale, producing a dimensionless but normalization-dependent acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Error Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic functional \(S(z)\) defines a coherent normalization family, but the cited primal-dual framework locator has not been shown to support this exact diagnostic definition or its acceptance interpretation. A source specifying normalized residual tests is required.

children.title: Scaling–Normalization Disagreement
children.top_down_role: Cases where scaled and normalized assessments yield materially different quality judgments.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling–Normalization Disagreement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for equivalence of coordinate-scaled and scalar-normalized residual tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scaled test accepts \(r\) when \(\|Dr\|\le\tau_s\), while a scalar-normalized test accepts when \(\|r\|/S\le\tau_n\). For \(S>0\), \(\tau_s>0\), and \(\tau_n>0\), their acceptance regions are identical for every \(r\) only if \(\|Dr\|=(\tau_s/(S\tau_n))\|r\|\) for every \(r\). Under the same infinity norm, a nonuniform diagonal \(D\) violates this condition. For example, residuals concentrated in differently weighted coordinates can pass one test and fail the other despite equal unscaled norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive thresholds, coordinate scaling and scalar normalization give identical decisions only under a proportional norm transformation; nonuniform component weights create genuine disagreement.
assumptions_latex: A residual is \(r\in\mathbb{R}^k\), with nonsingular diagonal scaling \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times k}\).
A positive scalar normalization \(S>0\) and strictly positive tolerances \(\tau_s>0\) and \(\tau_n>0\) are prescribed.
The same norm \(\|\cdot\|\) is used in both tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaled acceptance is \(\|Dr\|\le\tau_s\), whereas normalized acceptance is \(\|r\|/S\le\tau_n\). These acceptance regions coincide for all \(r\) only when \(\|Dr\|=(\tau_s/(S\tau_n))\|r\|\) for all \(r\). For the same underlying norm, this requires \(D\) to act as a scalar norm similarity; a genuinely nonuniform diagonal scaling permits disagreement.

children.title: Optimality Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination based on evidence supporting the requested optimality quality.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual LP pair is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
Declared primal, dual, complementarity, and gap tolerances are nonnegative.
The solver has produced a candidate \((x,y,s)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with status approximately optimal is permitted only when all declared tests pass: \(v_p\le\tau_p\), \(v_d\le\tau_d\), \(v_c\le\tau_c\), and \(v_g\le\tau_g\). The output must include the candidate and measured values. Exact optimality follows only when all four tolerances are zero; positive tolerances certify membership in the declared acceptance region, not exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint residual-based termination rule for an approximately optimal canonical LP solution.

source_refs.locator: 7 Superlinear Convergence and Finite Termination p. 127

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((x,y,s)\), compute \(v_p=\max\{\|Ax-b\|_\infty,\|(-x)_+\|_\infty\}\), \(v_d=\max\{\|A^Ty+s-c\|_\infty,\|(-s)_+\|_\infty\}\), \(v_c=\|x\odot s\|_\infty\), and \(v_g=|c^Tx-b^Ty|\). An optimality termination rule accepts only if \(v_p\le\tau_p\), \(v_d\le\tau_d\), \(v_c\le\tau_c\), and \(v_g\le\tau_g\). The solver returns the candidate, status, measures, tolerances, and scaling conventions. With positive tolerances, the status means approximately optimal under these tests rather than exactly optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality termination requires every declared primal, dual, complementarity, and gap test to pass, with the measured residuals and conventions reported.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Termination

source_witnesses.locator: 7 Superlinear Convergence and Finite Termination p. 127

children.title: Feasibility Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination based on evidence supporting the requested feasibility quality.

assumptions_latex: The original-form primal LP is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\).
The reported iterate is \(x^k\), with feasibility tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_x\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination certifies only tolerance-level primal feasibility, not optimality or exact feasibility.

notation.meaning: Primal equality residual at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-tolerance primal-feasibility stopping rule for an equality-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A feasibility termination regime accepts \(x^k\) when
\[
\|Ax^k-b\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_p
\quad\text{and}\quad
\|(-x^k)_+\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_x.
\]
If relative scaling is used, the denominators and zero-data convention must be fixed before the test is evaluated. Passing this predicate establishes approximate primal feasibility in the original model; it does not by itself establish dual feasibility, a small duality gap, or optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop for feasibility when equality violation and bound violation meet declared tolerances; this status alone makes no optimality claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Termination

children.title: Joint Acceptance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Termination regimes requiring compatible optimality and feasibility assessments.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
The tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_x,\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_g\ge0\) and gap normalization are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Passing every test certifies a jointly acceptable approximate primal-dual solution under the declared tolerances.

notation.meaning: Positive normalization used for the gap.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjunctive acceptance of primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and a normalized objective gap.

source_refs.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A joint acceptance regime terminates successfully exactly when
\[
\|r_p\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_p,\quad
\|(-x)_+\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_x,\quad
\|r_d\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_d,\quad
\|(-s)_+\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_s,
\quad
\frac{|g|}{\sigma_g}\le\varepsilon_g,
\]
where \(\sigma_g>0\) is the declared normalization. The status is joint only if all predicates are evaluated on the same recovered primal-dual point and in the same model representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint acceptance requires simultaneous primal feasibility, dual feasibility, bound feasibility, and a sufficiently small normalized objective gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Acceptance Regimes

children.title: Approximate-Solution Termination
children.top_down_role: Early acceptance of a solution meeting relaxed quality requirements.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual LP pair has finite data and admits comparison through primal and dual residuals and an objective gap.
Positive scaling factors \(\sigma_p,\sigma_d,\sigma_g\) and tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g\ge0\) are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted triple is an approximate solution relative to the stated residual, cone, and gap conventions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-and-gap definition of an approximate solution for a primal-dual equality-form LP.

source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

source_refs.locator: 4.3.4 Approximate solutions of \( \left( P\right) \) and \( \left( D\right) \) p. 82
source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Approximate-solution termination accepts \((x,y,s)\) when
\[
\frac{\|r_p\|_\infty}{\sigma_p}\le\varepsilon_p,
\qquad
\frac{\|r_d\|_\infty}{\sigma_d}\le\varepsilon_d,
\qquad
x\ge-\varepsilon_p\mathbf 1,
\qquad
s\ge-\varepsilon_d\mathbf 1,
\qquad
\frac{|g|}{\sigma_g}\le\varepsilon_g.
\]
The returned status must retain the tolerances and positive scaling factors used, because the word “approximate” has no model-independent numerical meaning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate solution meets declared scaled primal, dual, cone, and objective-gap tolerances, all of which accompany the status.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Solution Termination

children.title: Screening Termination
children.top_down_role: Early exit intended to classify, filter, or deprioritize a solve.

assumptions_latex: For each index \(j\), a screening test returns either a certified decision or an undecided result.
Every certified decision is justified by a valid bound whose error allowance is included in its decision margin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination yields a screened partition, not necessarily a solved LP; unresolved indices remain explicitly undecided.

notation.meaning: Indices certified for elimination or fixing.
Indices not certified by the screen.
Certified screening margin for index j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic safe-screening stopping rule; the navigation does not identify a particular LP screening method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(S=\varnothing\) and \(U=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). At each screening pass, compute certified margins \(m_j\) for \(j\in U\); transfer \(j\) to \(S\) only when the method-specific safe predicate \(m_j>0\) holds after accounting for numerical error. Terminate when \(U=\varnothing\), when a full pass changes neither \(S\) nor the available bounds, or when a declared screening budget is exhausted. Return \((S,U)\), the margins, and the bound certificates; membership in \(U\) is not a classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop screening at complete classification, a certified fixed point, or a budget limit, and return both screened and undecided indices.
knowledge_statements.title: Screening Termination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed generic safe-screening margins, fixed-point condition, or returned certificates. Because these details depend on the screening family, the algorithmic statement cannot be validated as written.

children.title: Screening Misclassification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where limited solve evidence is insufficient for reliable screening.

assumptions_latex: A screening decision uses an exact decision quantity \(q_j\) and a computed value \(\widehat q_j\).
A valid error bound \(|\widehat q_j-q_j|\le\delta_j\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only values outside the uncertainty band admit a sign-safe classification; values inside it must remain undecided.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical uncertainty boundary for threshold-based screening decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a zero-threshold sign screen, the safe regions are
\[
\widehat q_j-\delta_j>0
\quad\text{or}\quad
\widehat q_j+\delta_j<0.
\]
The misclassification boundary is the uncertainty band \(|\widehat q_j|\le\delta_j\). Within this band, admissible exact values include zero and may include both signs, so a forced positive or negative classification is not certified. More generally, for threshold \(\tau_j\), replace \(\widehat q_j\) by \(\widehat q_j-\tau_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A screening sign is certifiable only when its computed margin exceeds its error bound; otherwise either classification may be wrong.
knowledge_statements.title: Screening Misclassification Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elementary uncertainty-band calculation is coherent, but no source connects this sign-screen model to the intended LP screening container or establishes the applicable classification semantics.

children.title: Stagnation Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination after meaningful progress has effectively ceased.

assumptions_latex: A nonnegative monitored merit sequence \((\phi_k)\) and window length \(w\in\mathbb N\) are fixed.
Absolute and relative progress thresholds \(\tau_a,\tau_r\ge0\) are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule diagnoses numerical or algorithmic stagnation; it does not certify infeasibility, unboundedness, or optimality.

notation.meaning: Monitored merit value at iteration k.
Best decrease over the monitoring window.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed no-progress diagnostic based on a declared scalar merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Stagnation termination occurs at iteration \(k\ge w\) when
\[
\Delta_k\le \tau_a+\tau_r\max\{1,\phi_{k-w}\}
\]
and no successful termination certificate has been obtained. The implementation must record \(\phi_k\), \(w\), and both thresholds. If several residuals are monitored separately, the predicate must state whether stagnation requires every component or only an aggregate merit to satisfy the inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Declare stagnation when the best merit improvement over a fixed window is below absolute-plus-relative progress thresholds.
knowledge_statements.title: Stagnation Termination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed window statistic and absolute-plus-relative threshold are solver-policy choices with no cited support. A source must establish the intended merit function and stagnation rule.

children.title: Slow-Progress Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination after progress remains persistent but operationally inadequate.

assumptions_latex: A nonnegative merit sequence \((\phi_k)\), window \(w\in\mathbb N\), and required progress rate \(\rho_{\min}>0\) are fixed.
The current iterate has not met any successful acceptance predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The status reports sustained progress below policy, while distinguishing it from zero-resolution stagnation.

notation.meaning: Average decrease over a monitoring window.
Positive resolution threshold separating slowdown from stagnation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window progress-rate diagnostic separated from stagnation by a positive resolution threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Slow-progress termination occurs at iteration \(k\ge w\) when
\[
\rho_0<\rho_k<\rho_{\min},
\]
where \(0\le\rho_0<\rho_{\min}\) is the declared stagnation-resolution boundary. The inequality must persist for the declared number of windows or iterations. This status asserts measurable but insufficient improvement under the selected merit function; it is not an optimality or infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Declare slow progress when measurable improvement persists but its finite-window rate remains below the required rate.
knowledge_statements.title: Slow-Progress Termination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No evidence supports the rate thresholds or the distinction between slowdown and stagnation. The required persistence duration is also invoked without being introduced as a parameter.

children.title: Stagnation–Slowdown Classification
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic distinctions between stalled progress and unusually slow progress.

assumptions_latex: A windowed improvement statistic \(\Delta_k\ge0\) is computed from a declared merit sequence.
Thresholds satisfy \(0\le\eta_0<\eta_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The three classes are disjoint and exhaustive for \(\Delta_k\ge0\), conditional on the chosen merit and thresholds.

notation.meaning: Observed improvement over the diagnostic window.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold partition distinguishing stagnation, slowdown, and adequate progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Classify the monitored window by
\[
\begin{cases}
\text{stagnation},&0\le\Delta_k\le\eta_0,\\
\text{slowdown},&\eta_0<\Delta_k<\eta_1,\\
\text{adequate progress},&\Delta_k\ge\eta_1.
\end{cases}
\]
Classification is meaningful only after the merit function, window, scaling, and thresholds have been recorded. It is a diagnostic partition of observed progress and does not replace independent tests for optimality, feasibility, infeasibility, or unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two declared thresholds partition nonnegative windowed improvement into stagnation, slowdown, and adequate progress.
knowledge_statements.title: Stagnation–Slowdown Classification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The threshold partition is internally exhaustive and disjoint, but it is an uncited, policy-defined classification rather than an established LP-solver taxonomy.

children.title: Resource-Limited Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination caused by time, memory, iteration, or comparable resource limits.

assumptions_latex: At least one monotone resource counter \(R_i(k)\) and finite limit \(L_i\) is declared.
Successful mathematical termination predicates are checked before or together with the resource predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The status identifies exhaustion of a declared computational resource and makes no mathematical solution claim by itself.

notation.meaning: Consumption of resource i by iteration k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination caused by an iteration, time, memory, or evaluation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Resource-limited termination occurs at the first iteration \(k\) for which
\[
\exists i\in\mathcal R:\ R_i(k)\ge L_i,
\]
unless a successful certificate has already been accepted under the implementation's declared precedence rule. The output must identify the exhausted resource, its limit and measured consumption, and any available incumbent or certificate artifact. Reaching the limit alone does not certify optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when a declared resource limit is reached, recording the exhausted resource without implying a mathematical solver conclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Limited Termination

children.title: Interrupted Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination caused by user, system, orchestration, or external interruption.

assumptions_latex: An external cancellation or shutdown signal is observable by the solver.
The solver has a well-defined last completed consistency point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned status records external interruption separately from resource exhaustion and mathematical termination.

notation.meaning: Iteration of the last completed consistency point.
Partial solver state at the consistency point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Externally initiated termination with recovery from the last consistent solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Interrupted termination occurs when \(I=1\) before a successful or failure certificate is accepted. The solver returns the state \(z^{k_c}\) from the last completed consistency point, together with the interruption cause and \(k_c\). Any iterate produced after \(k_c\) is excluded unless its invariants are revalidated. The interrupted status itself carries no assertion about feasibility, optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On external interruption, return the last validated state and cause, without assigning an unsupported mathematical solution status.
knowledge_statements.title: Interrupted Termination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The last-consistency-point recovery and post-checkpoint exclusion rules are implementation-protocol claims without evidence. Their correctness depends on solver-specific interruption and checkpoint semantics.

children.title: Partial-Artifact Disposition
children.top_down_role: Status and usability of solution artifacts retained after premature termination.

assumptions_latex: Termination occurs before a complete solver outcome is certified.
Each retained artifact can be independently recomputed or checked against declared tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only artifacts passing their own validation predicates may be exposed as usable partial results.

notation.meaning: Set of artifacts available at termination.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation and labeling rule for incumbents, bounds, rays, bases, and checkpoints after incomplete termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given available artifacts \(\mathcal A\), define
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{keep}}=\{a\in\mathcal A:V_a(a)=\mathrm{true}\}.
\]
Each retained artifact must carry its type, model representation, validation tolerance, and provenance. An unchecked iterate may be labeled a candidate only; a bound requires a valid dual certificate, a ray requires its defining feasibility and sign checks, and a basis or checkpoint requires structural consistency. Failure of one artifact's predicate does not invalidate independently checked artifacts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain only independently validated partial artifacts, labeling each by type, model representation, tolerance, and provenance.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Artifact Disposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record describes an artifact-validation and disposition procedure, not a certificate itself. It is also too broad to state that every bound requires a dual certificate, since usable bound provenance depends on bound direction and artifact type.

assumptions_latex: The solver returns a postsolved candidate \((x,y,s)\) for the original primal-dual LP.
Original unscaled data \((A,b,c)\) are available independently of presolve and scaling transformations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance uses residuals recomputed from original data, revealing errors hidden by scaled or transformed internal residuals.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent residual recomputation after undoing presolve and scaling.

source_refs.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input original data \((A,b,c)\), a recovered candidate \((x,y,s)\), and validation tolerances. Discard cached internal residuals and compute
\[
r_p^{\mathrm{orig}}=Ax-b,
\qquad
r_d^{\mathrm{orig}}=A^Ty+s-c,
\qquad
g^{\mathrm{orig}}=c^Tx-b^Ty
\]
directly from the original unscaled coefficients. Also recompute violations of \(x\ge0\) and \(s\ge0\). Apply the declared original-model acceptance tests to these quantities and return both the residuals and pass-or-fail decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute primal, dual, cone, and gap residuals directly from original unscaled data before accepting the postsolved result.
knowledge_statements.title: Unscaled Residual Recomputation

source_witnesses.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

children.title: Objective Recomputation
children.top_down_role: Independent recomputation of reported objective values in the original model.

assumptions_latex: The original primal LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\), with stored original-model data \(A,b,c\).
A postsolved candidate \(\hat x\in\mathbb R^n\) is expressed in the original variable coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The independently recomputed primal objective is \(\hat p:=\sum_{j=1}^n c_j\hat x_j=c^{\mathsf T}\hat x\). It is computed directly from the original coefficients and postsolved variables, without using a solver-reported objective, presolved coefficients, or accumulated objective offsets. If any component required by this sum is unavailable or nonfinite, objective validation is indeterminate rather than successful.

notation.meaning: postsolved primal candidate in original coordinates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical equality-form minimization LP; recomputation uses original, unscaled data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the original primal LP \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and a postsolved candidate \(\hat x\), define the recomputed objective by
\[
\hat p=c^{\mathsf T}\hat x=\sum_{j=1}^{n}c_j\hat x_j.
\]
The computation uses the original objective coefficients and original-coordinate variables, independently of the solver-reported objective and presolve bookkeeping. A finite value is returned only when every required coefficient and variable value is available and finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute the candidate objective directly from original coefficients and postsolved variables; do not reuse the solver-reported value or presolve objective bookkeeping.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Recomputation

children.title: Bound Recomputation
children.top_down_role: Independent recomputation of reported primal or dual bounds.

assumptions_latex: The dual of \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) is \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
The postsolved candidate \(\hat y\in\mathbb R^m\) is expressed in the original constraint coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The independently recomputed dual bound is \(\hat d:=b^{\mathsf T}\hat y\). When \(A^{\mathsf T}\hat y+\hat s=c\) and \(\hat s\ge0\), weak duality makes \(\hat d\) a valid lower bound on every primal feasible objective. Without verified dual feasibility, \(b^{\mathsf T}\hat y\) is only a candidate bound value.

notation.meaning: independently recomputed dual objective or bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual lower-bound recomputation for a canonical minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the dual candidate \((\hat y,\hat s)\), recompute the candidate lower bound from original data as
\[
\hat d=b^{\mathsf T}\hat y.
\]
If \(A^{\mathsf T}\hat y+\hat s=c\) and \(\hat s\ge0\), then weak duality gives \(\hat d\le c^{\mathsf T}x\) for every primal feasible \(x\). Thus \(\hat d\) is accepted as a certified bound only after dual feasibility has been checked in the original model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute the dual objective from original right-hand sides and postsolved multipliers; treat it as a certified bound only after checking dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Recomputation

children.title: Objective–Bound Consistency
children.top_down_role: Cross-checks between recomputed objectives, bounds, and claimed status.

assumptions_latex: The independently recomputed values are \(\hat p=c^{\mathsf T}\hat x\) and \(\hat d=b^{\mathsf T}\hat y\).
A prescribed absolute tolerance \(\tau_a\ge0\) and relative tolerance \(\tau_r\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Objective-bound consistency holds when \(\hat p+\tau_a+\tau_r\max\{1,|\hat p|,|\hat d|\}\ge\hat d\) and \(|\hat p-\hat d|\le\tau_a+\tau_r\max\{1,|\hat p|,|\hat d|\}\). The first test detects a dual bound exceeding the primal value beyond tolerance; the second is required when optimality is claimed.

notation.meaning: recomputed primal and dual objective values

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical consistency test; feasibility residuals must be checked separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set
\[
\Delta=\tau_a+\tau_r\max\{1,|\hat p|,|\hat d|\}.
\]
The recomputed pair is weak-duality consistent when \(\hat d-\hat p\le\Delta\). If the solver claims optimality, objective-bound consistency additionally requires \(|\hat p-\hat d|\le\Delta\). Passing these scalar comparisons does not replace primal- and dual-feasibility checks; it only validates the relationship between the independently recomputed objective and bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recomputed dual bound must not exceed the recomputed primal value beyond tolerance, and an optimality claim additionally requires a small objective gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective–Bound Consistency

assumptions_latex: The original primal-dual pair is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
The postsolve map returns \((\hat x,\hat y,\hat s)\) in original-model coordinates.
Validation tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The postsolved tuple is consistent when \(\|A\hat x-b\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\hat x\ge-\varepsilon_p\mathbf1\), \(\|A^{\mathsf T}\hat y+\hat s-c\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_d\), \(\hat s\ge-\varepsilon_d\mathbf1\), and \(|c^{\mathsf T}\hat x-b^{\mathsf T}\hat y|\le\varepsilon_g\). All quantities are recomputed using original, unscaled data.

notation.meaning: postsolved primal, dual, and dual-slack candidates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-coordinate residual and gap check after reversing presolve transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A postsolved tuple \((\hat x,\hat y,\hat s)\) passes primal-dual consistency checking when
\[
\|A\hat x-b\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_p,\quad \hat x\ge-\varepsilon_p\mathbf1,
\]
\[
\|A^{\mathsf T}\hat y+\hat s-c\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_d,\quad \hat s\ge-\varepsilon_d\mathbf1,
\]
and \(|c^{\mathsf T}\hat x-b^{\mathsf T}\hat y|\le\varepsilon_g\). Each residual and objective is recomputed from original, unscaled model data after all postsolve transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a postsolved primal-dual tuple only when original-model primal residuals, dual residuals, sign violations, and the recomputed duality gap meet their tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Postsolve Primal–Dual Consistency Checking

children.title: Independent Validation
children.top_down_role: Validation performed outside the solver path that produced the reported result.

assumptions_latex: A solver supplies a claimed status and associated original-coordinate candidate data.
A validator independently parses the original model and does not reuse the solver's presolve state, factorizations, residuals, or reported objective values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independent validation accepts the claim only if its own computations establish the corresponding predicates: primal and dual feasibility with a sufficiently small gap for optimality, a Farkas inequality for infeasibility, or a feasible improving ray for unboundedness. Failure to establish the predicate yields an unvalidated claim, not the opposite mathematical status.

notation.meaning: original LP data supplied separately to the validator
solver claim and accompanying candidate witness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical acceptance rule for a validator isolated from solver-internal computations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given original LP data \((A,b,c)\), a claimed status \(\sigma\), and witness \(w\), an independent validator recomputes every predicate defining \(\sigma\) from \((A,b,c,w)\). It accepts only when those predicates hold under the declared arithmetic and tolerances. The validator must not rely on solver-produced residuals, presolve state, bases, factorizations, or objective values. If validation fails, the conclusion is only that \((\sigma,w)\) was not validated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separate validator must derive the status predicate from the original model and witness without trusting solver-internal residuals, transformations, or objective values.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Validation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited simplex-termination section may support status witnesses but does not adequately support the asserted architectural independence boundary or the prohibition on reusing solver artifacts. A validation or solver-verification source is required.

children.title: Exact Validation
children.top_down_role: Validation using exact or certifying arithmetic.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rational verification of finite LP witnesses; witness construction is outside scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For rational original data \((A,b,c)\) and a rational witness \(w\), exact validation evaluates the defining certificate equations and inequalities in \(\mathbb Q\), with no rounding tolerance. Acceptance means that every required equality is exactly zero and every required strict or nonstrict inequality has the stated sign. An accepted primal-dual optimality pair, Farkas vector, or improving feasible ray therefore certifies the claimed status of the encoded rational LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For rational LP data and rational witnesses, check all certificate equations and inequalities in exact arithmetic, without numerical tolerances.
assumptions_latex: All entries of \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb Q^n\) are rational.
Candidate witnesses are represented rationally and every comparison is evaluated in exact rational arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact validation accepts precisely when the relevant equalities and strict or nonstrict inequalities hold over \(\mathbb Q\). It uses no feasibility tolerance. Thus an accepted optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness witness establishes the corresponding mathematical claim for the encoded rational LP.

notation.meaning: rational certificate submitted for exact checking

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods and Rational Arithmetic p. 52

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods and Rational Arithmetic p. 52

children.title: Validator Disagreement
children.top_down_role: Cases where independent floating-point and exact assessments do not support the same outcome.

assumptions_latex: Two validators assess the same original LP, claimed status, and witness under explicitly recorded arithmetic and tolerance policies.
Their decisions or recomputed diagnostic quantities differ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A disagreement prevents unconditional acceptance until reconciled. The diagnostic record must distinguish differing arithmetic or tolerance policies from differing model interpretations and implementation errors. Neither validator's result alone implies that the other is wrong, and numerical rejection alone does not prove the opposite LP status.

notation.meaning: acceptance decisions of the two validators
validator configurations, including arithmetic and tolerances

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance boundary when independent validation channels return incompatible results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If two validators applied to the same original model and witness return \(D_1\ne D_2\), the solver claim remains unconditionally acceptable only after the discrepancy is reconciled. Reconciliation must compare their model encodings, status predicates, arithmetic, scaling conventions, and tolerances \(P_1,P_2\). A rejection under one numerical policy proves only failure of that policy's acceptance test; it does not by itself establish the opposite LP status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflicting validator results suspend unconditional acceptance until differences in model interpretation, arithmetic, predicates, and tolerances are identified and reconciled.
knowledge_statements.title: Validator Disagreement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary is plausible, but no source supports the mandatory suspension-and-reconciliation policy or its listed diagnostic categories. An inspectable validation-policy source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality certificate for the canonical equality-form primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A tuple \((x,y,s)\) is a primal-dual optimality certificate when
\[
Ax=b,\quad x\ge0,\quad A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\quad s\ge0,
\]
and
\[
c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y.
\]
These conditions certify optimality of both feasible solutions. Under primal and dual feasibility, the objective equality is equivalent to \(x^{\mathsf T}s=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and zero duality gap form a directly checkable certificate that both supplied solutions are optimal.
assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A tuple \((x,y,s)\) satisfying \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(s\ge0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y\) certifies that \(x\) and \((y,s)\) are primal and dual optimal. Equivalently, under feasibility, the final equality may be replaced by \(x^{\mathsf T}s=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate for equality constraints with nonnegative primal variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the system \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), a Farkas infeasibility certificate is a vector \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) such that
\[
A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0.
\]
These inequalities are directly verifiable from the original data and certify that the system has no feasible \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier whose transformed coefficients are nonnegative but whose right-hand-side product is negative certifies primal infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The primal feasibility system is \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), with \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A vector \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) certifies that no \(x\ge0\) satisfies \(Ax=b\). For rational input and rational \(y\), these relations can be checked exactly.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Unboundedness Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unboundedness-below certificate for a canonical minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A primal unboundedness certificate consists of \((\bar x,d)\) satisfying
\[
A\bar x=b,\quad \bar x\ge0,\quad Ad=0,\quad d\ge0,\quad c^{\mathsf T}d<0.
\]
These conditions certify that \(\bar x+td\) is primal feasible for every \(t\ge0\) and that its objective tends to \(-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\). Thus the LP is feasible and unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point plus a nonnegative nullspace direction with negative objective slope certifies that the minimization LP is unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: The primal LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A pair \((\bar x,d)\) with \(A\bar x=b\), \(\bar x\ge0\), \(Ad=0\), \(d\ge0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\) certifies primal unboundedness below. Every \(\bar x+td\), \(t\ge0\), is feasible and its objective tends to \(-\infty\).

children.title: Approximate Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates whose numerical evidence is accepted within stated tolerances.

assumptions_latex: The canonical primal-dual LP pair and candidate \((x,y,s)\) are given in floating-point form.
Nonnegative tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g\) and the norm and scaling conventions are declared in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tuple is an approximate optimality certificate when its primal residual and negativity, dual residual and negativity, and objective gap satisfy the stated tolerances. It certifies only tolerance-relative acceptance under the declared numerical model, not exact feasibility or exact optimality.

notation.meaning: candidate primal, dual, and dual-slack vectors

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-relative numerical optimality certificate, not an exact mathematical certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For declared tolerances, \((x,y,s)\) is an approximate optimality certificate when
\[
\|Ax-b\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_p,\quad \|x^-\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_p,
\]
\[
\|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_d,\quad \|s^-\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_d,
\]
and \(|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|\le\varepsilon_g\). The norm, data scaling, and tolerances are part of the certificate semantics. Passing establishes numerical acceptability under those conventions, not exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate certificate meets declared primal, dual, sign, and objective-gap tolerances; it supports numerical acceptance but not exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Certificates

children.title: Weak Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates that support only a qualified or limited conclusion.

assumptions_latex: A claimed LP status is accompanied by a witness that verifies only a proper subset of the defining certificate predicates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Such a witness is weak: it can support diagnostics but cannot establish the claimed status. Concretely, primal feasibility alone does not certify optimality, and a direction satisfying \(Ad=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\) does not certify unboundedness unless an appropriate feasible base point and recession-cone sign conditions are also verified.

notation.meaning: set of all predicates required by the claimed certificate family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between partial diagnostic evidence and a status-establishing certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be the complete set of predicates defining a status certificate. A witness satisfying only a proper subset of \(\mathcal P\) is weak and does not certify that status. For example, \(Ax=b\) and \(x\ge0\) alone do not establish optimality. Likewise, \(Ad=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\) do not establish primal unboundedness unless \(d\ge0\) and a feasible base point \(\bar x\ge0\) with \(A\bar x=b\) are also verified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A witness checking only some required predicates is diagnostic evidence, not a certificate; omitted feasibility, sign, or gap conditions can invalidate the claimed status.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Certificates

children.title: Certificate Trust Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions limiting the interpretation or portability of nondefinitive certificates.

assumptions_latex: The reported model is the minimization LP \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\).
A checker accepts primal feasibility when \(\|Ax-b\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_p\), where \(\varepsilon_p>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A tolerance-accepted certificate need not certify the corresponding exact LP statement.

notation.meaning: primal constraint matrix and right-hand side

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between tolerance-based computational acceptance and exact mathematical certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=0\), choose \(b\ne0\) with \(\|b\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_p\), and take any \(x\ge0\). Then \(\|Ax-b\|_\infty=\|b\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_p\), so the checker accepts \(x\) as approximately primal feasible. Nevertheless, \(Ax=b\) is impossible because \(Ax=0\ne b\). Thus a low-strength certificate bounded only by nonzero residual tolerances establishes membership in a declared acceptance region, not exact feasibility, optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Passing nonzero residual tolerances certifies only the declared numerical acceptance test; even an accepted primal point can correspond to an exactly infeasible LP.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Trust Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly separates tolerance acceptance from exact feasibility, but no citation supports the solver-policy interpretation. The final sentence extends one primal-feasibility counterexample to optimality, infeasibility, and unboundedness without defining the corresponding certificate tests, and the statement contains proof-style derivation.

assumptions_latex: A homogeneous self-dual embedding is constructed for a primal-dual conic representation of the LP.
The embedding variables include nonnegative scalars \(\tau\) and \(\kappa\), and its residual equations are satisfied exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The embedding solution yields either a normalized primal-dual solution or an alternative-system certificate, according to its terminal scalar pattern.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate-extraction property; embedding equations may use an equivalent sign convention.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Embedding into a self-dual LO-problem p. 22
source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization
Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an exact nonzero solution of a homogeneous self-dual LP embedding, the mutually exclusive informative cases are interpreted as follows. If \(\tau>0\), normalization by \(\tau\) produces variables satisfying the original primal-dual equations; if additionally the normalized complementarity gap is zero, they certify optimality. If \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\), appropriate normalized components satisfy an alternative system and certify primal infeasibility or dual infeasibility, the latter corresponding to primal unboundedness only when primal feasibility is also established. The zero solution and numerically unresolved scalar patterns are not outcome certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An informative self-dual embedding solution normalizes either to a primal-dual solution or to an infeasibility alternative; zero or unresolved scalar patterns certify nothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Self-Dual Embedding Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5 Embedding into a self-dual LO-problem p. 22
source_witnesses.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization
Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited sections are relevant, but the embedding equations and sign convention are not stated. Consequently, phrases such as “appropriate normalized components” do not define an independently checkable certificate, and the claimed interpretation of the tau-kappa patterns cannot be verified against the local table-of-contents extract.

children.title: Optimal Statuses
children.top_down_role: Statuses claiming satisfaction of the solver's optimality criteria.

assumptions_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The status optimal is justified by exact primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and zero duality gap.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimal status for a standard-form primal-dual LP pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A solver may assign the exact status optimal when it supplies \((x,y,s)\) satisfying \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), \(A^Ty+s=c\), \(s\ge0\), and \(c^Tx=b^Ty\). Equivalently under these feasibility equations, \(x^Ts=0\). These conditions are independently checkable and imply that \(x\) minimizes the primal objective and \((y,s)\) maximizes the dual objective, with common value \(c^Tx=b^Ty\). A merely small residual or gap supports only a tolerance-qualified status, not this exact status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal status requires checkable primal and dual feasibility together with zero duality gap; merely small residuals justify only an approximate status.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Statuses

children.title: Feasible Statuses
children.top_down_role: Statuses claiming feasibility without a full optimality conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal-feasibility status, without an objective-quality guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the LP \(\min\{c^T x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\), a solver may assign the exact status feasible to a reported point \(x\) when \(Ax=b\) and \(x\ge 0\), equivalently when \(x\in P:=\{z:Az=b,\ z\ge 0\}\). This certificate establishes that \(P\ne\varnothing\). It does not by itself establish that \(x\) is optimal, that an optimal solution exists, or that the objective is bounded below on \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible status means the reported point satisfies every primal constraint exactly; by itself it says neither that the point is optimal nor that the objective has a finite attained minimum.
assumptions_latex: Consider the LP \(\min\{c^T x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The status feasible certifies membership in the primal feasible set but makes no optimality, attainment, or boundedness assertion.

children.title: Approximate Statuses
children.top_down_role: Statuses qualifying solution claims by relaxed numerical accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-qualified primal-dual solution status with explicitly declared residual scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(r_p=Ax-b\), \(r_d=A^T y+s-c\), and \(g=c^T x-b^T y\). With fixed positive scale factors \(\sigma_p,\sigma_d,\sigma_g\), an approximately feasible status for \(x\) requires \(x\ge 0\) and \(\|r_p\|/\sigma_p\le\varepsilon_p\). An approximately optimal status for \((x,y,s)\) requires \(x\ge 0\), \(s\ge 0\), \(\|r_p\|/\sigma_p\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\|r_d\|/\sigma_d\le\varepsilon_d\), and \(|g|/\sigma_g\le\varepsilon_g\). The status must retain the tolerances, norm, and scaling convention because these predicates do not assert exact equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate feasibility records a declared scaled primal-residual bound, while approximate optimality additionally records dual-feasibility and gap bounds; neither status asserts exact feasibility or optimality.
assumptions_latex: Consider the standard-form pair \(\min\{c^T x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\) and \(\max\{b^T y:A^T y+s=c,\ s\ge 0\}\).
Nonnegative tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g\), a norm, and positive scale factors \(\sigma_p,\sigma_d,\sigma_g\) are fixed before checking the result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Approximate status certifies only the displayed tolerance-qualified predicates.

children.title: Status Guarantee Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Relative strength and permitted interpretation of optimal, feasible, or approximate labels.

knowledge_statements.title: Status Guarantee Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical implication hierarchy among exact and tolerance-qualified solution-quality statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a reported tuple \((x,y,s)\), let \(S_{\mathrm{opt}}\) mean \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge 0\), \(A^T y+s=c\), \(s\ge 0\), and \(c^T x=b^T y\). Let \(S_{\mathrm{feas}}\) mean \(Ax=b\) and \(x\ge 0\), and let \(S_{\mathrm{afeas}}(\varepsilon_p)\) mean \(x\ge 0\) and \(\|Ax-b\|/\sigma_p\le\varepsilon_p\), where \(\sigma_p>0\) and \(\varepsilon_p\ge 0\). Then \(S_{\mathrm{opt}}\Rightarrow S_{\mathrm{feas}}\Rightarrow S_{\mathrm{afeas}}(\varepsilon_p)\). The reverse implications fail in general, so promotion to a stronger status requires checking its additional conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the displayed predicates, exact optimality implies exact feasibility, and exact feasibility implies tolerance-qualified feasibility; promotion in the reverse direction requires additional checks.
assumptions_latex: All predicates refer to the same standard-form LP, reported tuple, norm, and residual scaling.
The approximately feasible predicate uses a nonnegative tolerance \(\varepsilon_p\) and a positive scale factor \(\sigma_p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The guarantee implications are \(S_{\mathrm{opt}}\Rightarrow S_{\mathrm{feas}}\Rightarrow S_{\mathrm{afeas}}(\varepsilon_p)\), while their converses do not hold in general.

children.title: Infeasible Statuses
children.top_down_role: Statuses claiming that no acceptable primal solution exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact infeasibility status using the equality-form Farkas alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the feasibility system \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge 0\), the exact status infeasible is certified by a vector \(y\) satisfying \(A^T y\ge 0\) and \(b^T y<0\). A failed search for a feasible point, an iteration limit, or a tolerance-violating approximate multiplier is not an exact infeasibility certificate and requires a weaker status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact infeasibility is certified by a Farkas multiplier satisfying the displayed inequalities; failure to find a feasible point is not sufficient.
assumptions_latex: Consider the primal feasibility system \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A vector \(y\) with \(A^T y\ge 0\) and \(b^T y<0\) certifies exact primal infeasibility.

children.title: Unbounded Statuses
children.top_down_role: Statuses claiming an improving direction without a finite objective limit.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal-unbounded status for a minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization LP \(\min\{c^T x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\), the exact status unbounded below is certified by vectors \(x_0\) and \(d\) satisfying \(Ax_0=b\), \(x_0\ge 0\), \(Ad=0\), \(d\ge 0\), and \(c^T d<0\). A descent recession direction without a feasible base point certifies dual infeasibility but does not by itself certify primal unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal unboundedness is certified by a feasible base point together with a nonnegative feasible recession direction of strictly negative cost.
assumptions_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^T x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible point together with a feasible recession direction of negative cost certifies that the primal optimal value is \(-\infty\).

children.title: Outcome Evidence Requirements
children.top_down_role: Evidence expectations distinguishing infeasibility claims from unboundedness claims.

assumptions_latex: The LP is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), with all certificate quantities expressed in the original model coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each definitive outcome requires independently checkable evidence specific to that outcome.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum exact evidence predicates for optimal, infeasible, and unbounded outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Accept optimal only when \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), \(A^Ty+s=c\), \(s\ge0\), and \(c^Tx=b^Ty\). Accept infeasible only when \(A^Ty_I\ge0\) and \(b^Ty_I<0\). Accept unbounded below only when \(Ax_0=b\), \(x_0\ge0\), \(Ad=0\), \(d\ge0\), and \(c^Td<0\). If presolve or scaling was used, these predicates must be checked after mapping evidence back to the original model. Absent the corresponding predicate, the definitive status is unsupported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal, infeasible, and unbounded outcomes require distinct checkable certificates, evaluated in the original model after undoing transformations.
knowledge_statements.title: Outcome Evidence Requirements

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The three exact certificate predicates are mathematically correct, but the cited primal-dual-framework locator is indirect for the Farkas and recession certificates and does not inspectably support the implementation-specific requirement to undo presolve and scaling transformations.

assumptions_latex: The solver has not produced either a valid Farkas infeasibility certificate or a feasible-point-plus-descent-ray certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The disjunctive status infeasible-or-unbounded cannot be refined to either definitive status from the available evidence.

notation.meaning: proposition that the primal feasible set is empty
proposition that the feasible objective is unbounded below

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary of a disjunctive solver outcome produced without separable certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An infeasible-or-unbounded status asserts at most the disjunction \(I\lor U\). Since \(I\lor U\) entails neither \(I\) nor \(U\), it must not be reported as either exact infeasibility or exact unboundedness. Refinement to \(I\) requires a valid alternative-system certificate such as \(A^Ty\ge0\), \(b^Ty<0\); refinement to \(U\) requires primal feasibility together with a recession direction \(d\ge0\), \(Ad=0\), \(c^Td<0\). Until one predicate is verified, the ambiguity is part of the mathematical status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infeasible-or-unbounded is a disjunction, not either definitive conclusion; refinement requires the corresponding independently checkable certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-or-Unbounded Ambiguity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical distinction between a disjunction and either definitive outcome is correct, but the named solver status and its reduction semantics require a solver or status-standard source. The statement also includes proof-style logical justification.

children.title: Unknown Statuses
children.top_down_role: Statuses reporting insufficient evidence for a more specific conclusion.

assumptions_latex: A fixed certificate checker defines predicates for every definitive and tolerance-qualified solver outcome.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unknown status makes no assertion about feasibility, boundedness, or optimality of the LP.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evidence-relative unknown status, separated from any property of the mathematical LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign unknown when the available evidence \(E\) satisfies no accepted predicate in \(\mathcal C\), and no more specific failure attribution has been established. Formally, the checker has established only \(\bigwedge_{C\in\mathcal C}\neg C(E)\), not infeasibility, unboundedness, feasibility, or optimality of the underlying LP. Consequently, unknown is a statement about insufficiency of accepted evidence at termination; it must not be interpreted as a mathematical disjunction of particular LP outcomes unless that disjunction is separately certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unknown means no accepted outcome certificate is available and no specific failure is established; it says nothing definitive about the LP itself.
knowledge_statements.title: Unknown Statuses

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Unknown-status semantics require a solver-status standard or implementation source. Moreover, failure to accept any predicate does not automatically mean that the checker has established every predicate's logical negation unless exhaustive, decidable evaluation is explicitly assumed.

children.title: Imprecise Statuses
children.top_down_role: Statuses reporting a qualified conclusion with degraded numerical confidence.

assumptions_latex: Target tolerances \(\varepsilon\) and relaxed tolerances \(\widehat\varepsilon\) satisfy \(0\\le\varepsilon_i<\widehat\varepsilon_i\) componentwise.
A residual vector \(R(E)\) and its componentwise acceptance bounds are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Imprecise status records evidence accepted only under relaxed tolerances, not under the target tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-relative imprecise status for evidence that nearly supports a stronger outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given evidence \(E\), assign an imprecise version of an outcome when \(R_i(E)\le\widehat\varepsilon_i\) for every checked component \(i\), but \(R_j(E)>\varepsilon_j\) for at least one component \(j\). The status must identify the intended outcome predicate and the relaxed bounds actually met. It neither establishes the exact predicate \(R(E)=0\) nor the target-tolerance predicate \(R_i(E)\le\varepsilon_i\) for all \(i\). If no relaxed predicate is met, unknown or a specific failure status is required instead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Imprecise means evidence passes declared relaxed bounds but fails at least one target bound; it must identify both the intended outcome and achieved tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Imprecise Statuses

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relaxed-tolerance construction is coherent as a possible checker policy, but “imprecise” is implementation-dependent and has no supporting source. The assumption contains malformed LaTeX, \(0\\le\varepsilon_i\), which must be repaired to \(0\le\varepsilon_i\) before acceptance.

children.title: Numerical-Error Statuses
children.top_down_role: Statuses attributing failure to numerical instability or unreliable computation.

assumptions_latex: The solver is applied to a finite-dimensional LP with finite input data.
Acceptance requires finite iterates and computable residual or certificate quantities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathsf{status}=\mathsf{numerical\_error}\), and no claim of optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness is certified.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes computational breakdown from mathematically certified LP outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A numerical-error status applies when a required floating-point computation fails or ceases to support residual-based acceptance: for example, a factorization or linear solve fails, an iterate or diagnostic contains \(\mathrm{NaN}\) or \(\pm\infty\), or computed \(r_p\), \(r_d\), or \(g\) cannot be evaluated reliably. This status records failure of the computational process, not a property of the exact LP. Consequently it must not be interpreted as evidence that the primal or dual problem is infeasible, unbounded, or optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical error means computation broke down or diagnostics became unreliable; it makes no mathematical claim about the exact LP.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Error Statuses

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and mathematical caution fit the leaf, but the cited implementation chapter does not establish this particular numerical-error taxonomy or its solver-independent semantics. A solver specification or targeted numerical-status reference is required.

children.title: Uncertainty Attribution Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Boundaries separating lack of evidence, low precision, and numerical failure.

assumptions_latex: A solver has recorded diagnostics sufficient to test specified attribution predicates.
Outcome classes include numerical failure, tolerance ambiguity, and unresolved cause.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If no unique supported predicate \(P_k(D)\) holds, the outcome remains \(\mathsf{unknown}\) rather than receiving an unsupported attribution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: diagnostic attribution must not exceed the information supplied by recorded tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits causal interpretation of indeterminate LP solver outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An indeterminate outcome may be attributed to class \(k\) only when the recorded diagnostics \(D\) establish the declared predicate \(P_k(D)\). A numerical-error attribution requires evidence of computational breakdown; a tolerance attribution requires finite diagnostics lying in a declared ambiguity band; and model-side uncertainty requires evidence not explained by either condition. If several predicates remain possible, or none is established, the admissible conclusion is \(\mathsf{status}=\mathsf{unknown}\). Absence of a certificate alone does not identify which failure mechanism occurred.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver may name a cause only when diagnostics support it; otherwise the outcome must remain unknown.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty Attribution Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the attribution-boundary leaf and is internally coherent, but no inspectable source supports the proposed predicates or the rule that unresolved attribution must receive the stated unknown status.

assumptions_latex: The constraint index set \(M\) is finite.
For \(I\subseteq M\), \(F_I\) denotes the points satisfying exactly the constraints indexed by \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\) is an IIS exactly when \(F_I=\varnothing\) and \(F_{I\setminus\{i\}}\neq\varnothing\) for every \(i\in I\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-system definition of an irreducible infeasible subsystem
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses inclusion-minimal infeasibility, not minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite family of linear equalities and inequalities indexed by \(M\), a subset \(I\subseteq M\) is an irreducible infeasible subsystem if its feasible set is empty, \(F_I=\varnothing\), while deleting any single member restores feasibility: \(F_{I\setminus\{i\}}\neq\varnothing\) for every \(i\in I\). Irreducibility is inclusion-minimality. It does not assert that \(I\) has the smallest cardinality among all infeasible subsystems, and distinct irreducible infeasible subsystems may coexist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An IIS is an infeasible constraint subset that becomes feasible whenever any one of its constraints is removed.
knowledge_statements.title: Irreducible Infeasible Subsystems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is the standard inclusion-minimal definition of an IIS, correctly distinguished from minimum cardinality, but the record supplies no citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Constraint Conflict Attribution
children.top_down_role: Attribution of infeasibility evidence to model constraints.

assumptions_latex: Model restrictions are partitioned into row constraints \(H_i\) and bound literals \(L_j\).
The selected conflict is required to be inclusion-minimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A constraint conflict has the form \((I,\varnothing)\), with \(\bigcap_{i\in I}H_i=\varnothing\) and every proper selected subfamily feasible.
