children.title: Degenerate Models
children.top_down_role: Method-selection considerations for models with extensive primal or dual degeneracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal degeneracy of a basic feasible solution in standard-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \\(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\\) with \\(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\\). For a basis \\(B\\) of \\(m\\) linearly independent columns, the associated basic solution satisfies \\(x_B=A_B^{-1}b\\) and \\(x_N=0\\). A feasible basic solution is degenerate when \\(x_j=0\\) for at least one \\(j\in B\\). The LP model is called degenerate when it possesses a degenerate basic feasible solution; relative to an optimization objective, an optimal model is degenerately solved when an optimal basic feasible solution has this property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basic feasible solution is degenerate when at least one basic variable is zero; a model is degenerate when such a solution exists.
assumptions_latex: \\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\\)
\\(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(x\\) is degenerate relative to \\(B\\) exactly when \\(x_B\ge0\\) and some component of \\(x_B\\) equals zero.

children.title: Vertex-Structured Models
children.top_down_role: Method-selection considerations when vertex or basis structure is central.

knowledge_statements.title: Vertex-Structured Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP models whose required output is an extreme-point solution with an identifiable active structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Gx\le h,\ Ex=f\}\\). A feasible point \\(x\\) is a vertex when the only \\(d\in\mathbb R^n\\) satisfying \\(Ed=0\\) and \\(G_i d=0\\) for every active index \\(i\in I(x)=\{i:G_i x=h_i\}\\) is \\(d=0\\). Equivalently, the rows of \\(E\\) together with the active rows \\(G_{I(x)}\\) span \\(\mathbb R^n\\). An LP is vertex-structured for artifact selection when its required solution must include such a vertex and enough linearly independent active constraints to reconstruct that rank condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vertex-structured LP requires an extreme-point solution and active constraints whose normals span the variable space.
assumptions_latex: \\(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n},\ E\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\\)
\\(P\ne\varnothing\\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(x\\) is a vertex exactly when its equality and active-constraint normals have rank \\(n\\).

notation.meaning: Indices of inequalities active at x.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard active-constraint characterization of a polyhedral vertex
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The active-normal rank characterization of a polyhedral vertex is correct, and the artifact-selection specialization fits the local context, but no inspectable source is provided.

children.title: Degeneracy–Vertex Interaction
children.top_down_role: Selection consequences when degeneracy complicates vertex-oriented solution requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy–Vertex Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of degeneracy on basis representations of an LP vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \\(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\\) with \\(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\\), every basic feasible solution is a vertex. If a basic feasible solution \\(x\\) is nondegenerate, exactly \\(m\\) components are positive and their columns form its unique feasible basis. If \\(x\\) is degenerate, fewer than \\(m\\) components are positive, so distinct bases may represent the same vertex. Consequently, a simplex pivot may change the basis while leaving \\(x\\) unchanged and producing zero objective improvement; without an anti-cycling rule, repeated degenerate pivots can revisit earlier bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degeneracy allows multiple bases at one vertex, enabling zero-length simplex pivots and possible cycling despite unchanged primal solutions.
assumptions_latex: \\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\\)
\\(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A degenerate vertex can admit multiple basis representations and zero-displacement pivots.

knowledge_statements.title: Large Sparse Well-Scaled Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative structural regime for sparse, scaled LP method selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an LP data matrix \\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\\), fix declared thresholds \\(N_0\\), \\(\rho_0\\), and \\(\gamma\ge1\\). The model is large and sparse when \\(m+n\ge N_0\\) and \\(\operatorname{nnz}(A)/(mn)\le\rho_0\\). It is well-scaled relative to positive diagonal matrices \\(D_r,D_c\\) when every nonzero entry of \\(\widehat A=D_rAD_c\\) satisfies \\(\gamma^{-1}\le|\widehat A_{ij}|\le\gamma\\), and the correspondingly scaled nonzero components of \\(b\\) and \\(c\\) obey the same declared magnitude range. Classification must report the thresholds and scaling matrices because the regime is not invariant under arbitrary row or column rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This regime requires declared size and density thresholds plus a diagonal scaling that bounds all relevant nonzero data magnitudes.
assumptions_latex: \\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\\)
\\(D_r,D_c\\) are positive diagonal matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model belongs to the regime exactly when the declared size, sparsity, and scaled-magnitude tests hold.

notation.meaning: Number of nonzero entries of A.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit parameterized implementation regime rather than a universal threshold
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The parameterized regime is internally reproducible, but its scaling convention and use as an LP method-selection classification have no inspectable source.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Models
children.top_down_role: Method-selection considerations for models with high numerical sensitivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition-number criterion for numerically sensitive LP linear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(M\\) be the nonsingular basis matrix or regularized KKT matrix used by a specified LP algorithm, and let \\(\|\cdot\|\\) be the declared operator norm. For a threshold \\(\kappa_0>1\\), the model is ill-conditioned relative to that algorithmic system when \\(\kappa(M)=\|M\|\,\|M^{-1}\|\ge\kappa_0\\). Under perturbations \\(M\delta z=r\\), large \\(\kappa(M)\\) permits relative solution error to be much larger than relative data or residual error. The classification must identify \\(M\\), the norm, scaling, regularization, and threshold; ill-conditioning is not an intrinsic label without these choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LP is algorithmically ill-conditioned when its chosen basis or KKT system has a condition number above a declared threshold.
assumptions_latex: \\(M\\) is nonsingular.
\\(\|\cdot\|\\) is a declared subordinate matrix norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(\kappa(M)\ge\kappa_0\\) places the selected LP linear system in the declared ill-conditioned regime.

notation.meaning: Basis or regularized KKT matrix being assessed.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm-relative condition-number criterion is reasonable and appropriately declares the matrix, norm, scaling, regularization, and threshold, but neither the criterion nor the perturbation interpretation has an inspectable source.

children.title: Nearly Dependent Models
children.top_down_role: Method-selection considerations for models containing near-linear dependence.

knowledge_statements.title: Nearly Dependent Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise criterion for near linear dependence among rows of an LP constraint subsystem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\) be a selected nonzero scaled row submatrix of an LP constraint matrix, and define its relative row-dependence measure by \(\delta_{\mathrm{row}}(R)=\min_{\|u\|_2=1}\|R^{\mathsf T}u\|_2/\|R\|_2\), where \(u\in\mathbb R^r\). For a declared tolerance \(\tau>0\), the rows are nearly linearly dependent when \(\delta_{\mathrm{row}}(R)\le\tau\). When \(r\le n\), this measure equals \(\sigma_{\min}(R)/\sigma_{\max}(R)\); when \(r>n\), the rows are necessarily linearly dependent and \(\delta_{\mathrm{row}}(R)=0\). The model is nearly dependent when a declared relevant subsystem satisfies this test. The report must identify the subsystem, scaling, norm, and tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model is nearly dependent when a declared scaled constraint subsystem has a unit combination of its rows whose norm is small relative to the subsystem norm; the subsystem, scaling, norm, and tolerance must be reported.
assumptions_latex: \(R\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\) is nonzero.
\(\tau>0\) is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Near row dependence holds when \(\delta_{\mathrm{row}}(R)\le\tau\).

notation.meaning: Minimum relative norm of a unit linear combination of the rows of R.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normwise characterization of approximate row dependence

children.title: Conditioning–Dependence Interaction
children.top_down_role: Selection regimes where ill-conditioning and near dependence jointly increase solver risk.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning–Dependence Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative link between near dependence and spectral ill-conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(M\\) be a nonsingular square scaled matrix selected from an LP basis or linear-system formulation. In the Euclidean norm, \\(\kappa_2(M)=\sigma_{\max}(M)/\sigma_{\min}(M)\\). Hence, if \\(\sigma_{\min}(M)\le\tau\sigma_{\max}(M)\\) for \\(0<\tau<1\\), then \\(\kappa_2(M)\ge1/\tau\\). Thus near linear dependence of the rows or columns of the actual solved matrix forces ill-conditioning. Near dependence in an unused subsystem need not condition the algorithmic system, while equilibration or regularization can change the relevant matrix and therefore the observed condition number.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near dependence forces a large spectral condition number when it occurs in the matrix actually solved; scaling and regularization can alter the diagnosis.
assumptions_latex: \\(M\\) is a nonsingular square real matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(\sigma_{\min}(M)\le\tau\sigma_{\max}(M)\\) implies \\(\kappa_2(M)\ge1/\tau\\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: singular-value formula for the spectral condition number
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral condition-number identity and implication are correct for a nonsingular square matrix, and the property kind fits the interaction leaf, but no inspectable source is cited.

children.title: Network-Structured Models
children.top_down_role: Method-selection considerations for models dominated by network structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Structured Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Network-matrix structure relevant to specialized LP algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A bounded-form LP is network-structured when it can be written as 
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Bx=b,\;\ell\le x\le u\},\]
where \(B\) is a node-arc incidence matrix, possibly with one row deleted from each connected component. Thus every column of \(B\) contains at most one \(+1\), at most one \(-1\), and zeros elsewhere. The variables represent arc flows, \(Bx=b\) imposes node balances, and the bounds impose arc capacities or lower-flow requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A network-structured LP has node-balance constraints defined by an incidence matrix and individual lower and upper bounds on arc flows.
assumptions_latex: The model is a finite-dimensional linear program.
The directed graph and its node-arc incidence orientation are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint matrix admits a network-flow representation with node balances and arc bounds.

notation.meaning: Vector of node supplies and demands.

source_refs.source_title: Network Optimization: Continuous and Discrete Models

source_witnesses.source_title: Network Optimization: Continuous and Discrete Models

children.title: Angular-Structured Models
children.top_down_role: Method-selection considerations for block-angular or related structured matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Angular-Structured Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-angular structure supporting decomposition and structured factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An LP is block-angular when, after row and column permutations, it has variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_q\) and the form
\[\min\sum_{i=1}^q c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_i x_i=b_i\;(i=1,\ldots,q),\quad \sum_{i=1}^q L_i x_i=d,\quad \ell_i\le x_i\le u_i.\]
The matrices \(A_i\) define mutually disjoint local constraint blocks, while the comparatively small collection of linking rows \(L_i\) couples the blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-angular LP consists of independent local constraint blocks joined by a shared set of linking constraints.
assumptions_latex: The LP has finitely many variable blocks.
Rows and columns may be permuted without changing the model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint matrix separates into diagonal local blocks plus common linking rows.

notation.meaning: Contribution of block \(i\) to the linking constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-angular formulation is standard and the definition kind fits the leaf, but no citation or inspectable locator supports the stated structural characterization.

children.title: Decomposable Models
children.top_down_role: Method-selection considerations for models admitting useful decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposable Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable LP structure with limited cross-block coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An LP is decomposable with respect to blocks \(1,
\ldots,q\) when it admits the representation
\[\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^q c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i:x_i\in P_i\;(i=1,\ldots,q),\;\sum_{i=1}^q T_i x_i=d\right\},\]
where each \(P_i\) is a polyhedron described using only \(x_i\). Removing the coupling equation produces \(q\) independent LPs; equivalently, all interactions between distinct blocks pass through the displayed coupling equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decomposable LP has separable objectives and local feasible sets, with all cross-block interaction confined to explicit coupling constraints.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
The number of blocks is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deleting the coupling constraint separates the model into independent block LPs.

notation.meaning: Block contribution to the coupling equations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is a coherent definition of a decomposable LP, but the claim that all cross-block interaction is confined to the coupling equation has no cited source.

children.title: Hybrid Structural Regimes
children.top_down_role: Models exhibiting multiple structural forms without a single dominant specialization.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Structural Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Models combining several exploitable LP structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A hybrid-structured LP is a decomposable model
\[\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^q c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i:x_i\in P_i,\;\sum_{i=1}^q T_i x_i=d\right\}\]
in which the local polyhedra do not all share one representation: for example, some \(P_i\) have network-incidence constraints while others have general sparse constraints. Its structural regime is specified by the partition, each block's local matrix class, and the linking system; no single specialized matrix class describes the entire constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid regime combines differently structured local LP blocks through explicit linking constraints, so solver architecture must preserve more than one exploitable structure.
assumptions_latex: Each local set \(P_i\) has an explicitly identified matrix class.
The linking equations are distinguished from local constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model has multiple local structural classes coupled by a common linear system.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed hybrid classification is plausible and locally relevant, but it is not standardized by the record and lacks an authoritative source defining the partition, local classes, and linking system as a regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Affordable High-Accuracy Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource predicate favoring factorization-based accurate solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be the sparse linear system arising in each major solver iteration, \(M\) the available memory, and \(F\) the permitted arithmetic budget. The factorization-affordable high-accuracy regime holds when a numerically stable factorization \(K=LDL^{\mathsf T}\) or \(K=LU\), including ordering and workspace, satisfies
\[\operatorname{mem}(L,U,D)\le M,\qquad \operatorname{flop}_{\rm fact}(K)+r\operatorname{flop}_{\rm solve}(K)\le F,\]
and iterative refinement can meet the requested scaled residual tolerance \(\varepsilon\). Here \(r\) is the expected number of right-hand sides using the factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This regime holds when sparse factors fit in memory, their construction and reuse fit the compute budget, and refinement reaches the required residual tolerance.
assumptions_latex: A stable sparse factorization strategy and ordering have been selected.
Accuracy is measured by a specified scaled residual tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system factors are affordable and support the requested numerical accuracy.

notation.meaning: Linear system matrix used by the solver.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the appropriate knowledge kind, but affordability, stability, factor storage, and refinement success depend on the solver and platform. No source supports this particular conjunction or cost model.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Constrained Matrix-Free Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory predicate requiring operator-only linear algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be available memory and \(W_{m vec}\) the storage required by the solver's vectors and preconditioner. A matrix-free regime holds when the model supplies products \(v\mapsto Av\) and \(w\mapsto A^{\mathsf T}w\),
\[W_{m vec}\le M<\min\{\operatorname{mem}(A),\operatorname{mem}(L,U,D)\},\]
and an operator-based iteration with the admitted preconditioner can reach the prescribed tolerance \(\varepsilon\). The inequality rules out storing the explicit matrix or its factors while retaining the working vectors required for iterative computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This regime applies when vectors and a preconditioner fit in memory, but neither the explicit matrix nor its factors do, and operator products suffice.
assumptions_latex: Products by \(A\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\) are computable without materializing \(A\).
Convergence is assessed at a specified tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A matrix-free iterative implementation is memory-feasible whereas explicit storage or factorization is not.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the resource-regime leaf, but the storage inequality and asserted feasibility of the operator iteration require a sourced memory model, preconditioner specification, and convergence basis.

knowledge_statements.title: Multicore Parallel Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work-span condition for beneficial shared-memory parallelism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a solver kernel with total work \(W\), critical-path span \(S\), serial overhead \(H_p\), and \(p\) available CPU cores, the multicore parallel regime holds when
\[T_p\le H_p+\max\{W/p,S\}<T_1\]
and the kernel's shared working set fits available memory. The inequality requires parallel execution to reduce predicted wall time after synchronization, scheduling, and bandwidth effects represented by \(H_p\); the span prevents claiming speedup beyond the kernel's dependency structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This regime holds when parallel work distribution beats single-core time after overhead and dependency limits, while the shared working set remains memory-feasible.
assumptions_latex: The same numerical stopping rule is used for \(T_p\) and \(T_1\).
The work-span estimates include all dominant solver kernels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Execution on \(p\) CPU cores has lower predicted wall time than single-core execution.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but the proposed work-span runtime inequality is a platform-dependent model. The meaning and accounting of the overhead term require authoritative support and calibration.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerator-Resident Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residency and transfer predicate for accelerator execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W_d\) be the solver state required during repeated iterations, \(M_d\) accelerator memory, \(Q\) bytes transferred across the host-device link, \(B_h\) its sustained bandwidth, and \(T_d\) device computation time. The accelerator-resident regime holds when
\[W_d\le M_d,\qquad T_d+Q/B_h<T_h,\]
where \(T_h\) is the corresponding host runtime under the same stopping rule. Persistent residency requires that iteration data remain on the accelerator, with \(Q\) restricted to initialization, termination, and unavoidable synchronization transfers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This regime holds when iterative solver state fits on the accelerator and device compute plus unavoidable transfers is faster than equivalent host execution.
assumptions_latex: Host and accelerator runs use equivalent arithmetic and stopping criteria.
Runtime estimates include conversion and synchronization costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent accelerator execution is memory-feasible and has lower predicted runtime than host execution.

notation.meaning: Device working-set size and available device memory.
Transferred bytes and sustained host-device bandwidth.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is locally appropriate, but the two-term transfer model and persistent-residency criterion are implementation- and platform-dependent and have no supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cold Single-Solve Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method selection when no prior solve state is reusable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For one LP instance and candidate methods \(m\in\mathcal M\), suppose no basis, factorization, iterate, scaling, or symbolic analysis from a related solve is available. Define total predicted cost by
\[C_m=C_m^{\rm setup}+C_m^{\rm solve}+C_m^{\rm certify}.\]
Under a common accuracy and certificate requirement, cold single-solve selection chooses an admissible method in \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{m\in\mathcal M}C_m\). Setup cost is charged once and cannot be amortized over later instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one unrelated LP, select the admissible method minimizing setup, solve, and certification cost together; no preprocessing or warm-start cost is amortized.
assumptions_latex: Exactly one instance is to be solved.
Every candidate method must satisfy the same accuracy and certification requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Method selection minimizes unamortized total predicted cost over admissible methods.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A method-selection principle fits this leaf, but the proposed cost decomposition and argmin rule are an uncited implementation-dependent decision model rather than a sourced mathematical principle.

children.title: Objective Reoptimization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Solver-selection regimes for sequences that modify objective coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Reoptimization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplex-basis certificate under objective-only perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\;x\ge0\}\) with a nonsingular basis matrix \(A_B\) and basic solution \(x_B=A_B^{-1}b\ge0\). If only the objective changes to \(c'\), the same basic solution remains primal feasible. Define
\[y'=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c'_B,\qquad \bar c'_N=c'_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y'.\]
The retained basis is optimal for the perturbed LP if and only if \(\bar c'_N\ge0\). Thus nonnegative updated reduced costs constitute a directly checkable reoptimization certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After an objective-only change, the old basis stays primal feasible and remains optimal exactly when every updated nonbasic reduced cost is nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: The LP is in equality standard form with minimization convention.
The retained basis \(A_B\) is nonsingular and initially primal feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained basis is optimal under \(c'\) if and only if \(c'_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}A_B^{-\mathsf T}c'_B\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Dual vector induced by the perturbed basic costs.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The retained-basis certificate is mathematically precise for equality-standard-form minimization and the certificate kind is appropriate, but no source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Right-Hand-Side Reoptimization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Solver-selection regimes for sequences that modify constraint right-hand sides.

knowledge_statements.title: Right-Hand-Side Reoptimization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplex-basis certificate under right-hand-side perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\;x\ge0\}\) with an optimal nonsingular basis \(A_B\). If only the right-hand side changes to \(b'\), the reduced costs remain unchanged, so the retained basis remains dual feasible. Its new basic vector is
\[x'_B=A_B^{-1}b',\qquad x'_N=0.\]
The retained basis is optimal for the perturbed LP if and only if \(x'_B\ge0\). Hence the sign test on \(A_B^{-1}b'\) is a verifiable certificate for basis-preserving reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a right-hand-side-only change, reduced costs are unchanged; the old basis remains optimal exactly when its updated basic variables are nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: The LP is in equality standard form with minimization convention.
The retained basis is nonsingular and initially optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained basis is optimal under \(b'\) if and only if \(A_B^{-1}b'\ge0\).

source_refs.locator: 5.2. Global dependence on the right-hand side vector p. 212

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2. Global dependence on the right-hand side vector p. 212

children.title: Joint Perturbation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes involving simultaneous objective and right-hand-side changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Perturbation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-optimality certificate under simultaneous objective and right-hand-side changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min\{{c'}^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b',\;x\ge0\}\) and retain a nonsingular basis \(A_B\) from a related LP. Define
\[x'_B=A_B^{-1}b',\qquad y'=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c'_B,\qquad \bar c'_N=c'_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y'.\]
The retained basis is optimal for the jointly perturbed LP if and only if \(x'_B\ge0\) and \(\bar c'_N\ge0\). The two inequalities respectively certify primal and dual feasibility; failure of either test requires basis repair or a fresh solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With simultaneous objective and right-hand-side changes, the old basis remains optimal exactly when updated basic variables and updated reduced costs are both nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: The LP is in equality standard form with minimization convention.
The retained basis matrix \(A_B\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained basis is optimal if and only if \(A_B^{-1}b'\ge0\) and \(c'_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}A_B^{-\mathsf T}c'_B\ge0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simultaneous primal- and dual-feasibility tests form a mathematically coherent retained-basis certificate, but no authoritative citation or locator supports the statement.

assumptions_latex: \(P(\theta)=\min\{c(\theta)^\top x:A(\theta)x=b(\theta),\ x\ge 0\}\) is solved for an ordered parameter sequence \(\theta_0,\ldots,\theta_T\).
Successive LPs preserve dimensions and admit transferable bases or primal-dual iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Select a continuation or warm-start method and reuse the preceding solution state at each parameter value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-selection condition for an ordered family of structurally related LPs.

source_refs.locator: 3. The Parametric Self-Dual Simplex Method p. 116

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the ordered family \(P(\theta_t)\), define the solve sequence to be in the parametric regime when the data variation \(\|A(\theta_t)-A(\theta_{t-1})\|+\|b(\theta_t)-b(\theta_{t-1})\|+\|c(\theta_t)-c(\theta_{t-1})\|\) is sufficiently small that a basis or primal-dual state from \(P(\theta_{t-1})\) remains a valid initialization for \(P(\theta_t)\). The associated selection rule chooses a continuation or warm-start-capable solver and processes \(t=0,\ldots,T\) in parameter order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parametric regime solves nearby members of an ordered LP family by transferring the previous basis or primal-dual state and following the parameter order.
knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Solve Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 3. The Parametric Self-Dual Simplex Method p. 116

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited parametric-simplex section does not clearly support the proposed norm-based small-variation criterion or the generic solver-selection rule. The meaning of a state remaining a valid initialization also requires specification.

assumptions_latex: Each \(P_t\) is an LP relaxation produced by a common decomposition, cutting-plane, or branch-and-bound process.
A solver state can be transferred between consecutive relaxations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Prefer a reoptimization method when state-transfer cost plus warm-start work is smaller than repeated cold-solve work.

notation.meaning: solver state returned for relaxation t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection criterion for repeatedly modified LP relaxations within a larger optimization procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \((P_t)_{t=0}^T\) is in the relaxation-sequence regime when each \(P_{t+1}\) is obtained from \(P_t\) by adding, deleting, or modifying a limited set of rows, columns, or bounds, and later solves depend on earlier results. Given state \(s_t\), select reoptimization when the estimated work satisfies \(W(\operatorname{transfer}(s_t,P_{t+1}))+W(\operatorname{warmsolve}(P_{t+1}))<W(\operatorname{coldsolve}(P_{t+1}))\); otherwise restart. The output at each iteration is a validated solution or status for the current relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation sequence repeatedly changes one LP inside a larger algorithm; reuse solver state exactly when estimated transfer and warm-start work beat a cold solve.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Sequence Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the relaxation-sequence container, but no source supports the proposed transfer-versus-cold-solve inequality or establishes how its work estimates are defined and compared.

assumptions_latex: The LP is represented in equality form \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
A nonsingular basis \(B\) yields a primal-feasible basic solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal simplex is selected when primal feasibility is available and basis-quality and accuracy requirements favor vertex iterates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational condition for choosing primal simplex from an available primal-feasible basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select primal simplex when an initial or warm-start basis \(B\) satisfies \(x_B=B^{-1}b\ge0\), while dual feasibility \(\bar c_N\ge0\) is not yet established, and explicit basic solutions or high-accuracy crossover-free vertex output is required. Primal simplex preserves primal feasibility, chooses an entering nonbasic variable with an improving reduced cost, and pivots until \(\bar c_N\ge0\), or returns an unboundedness or numerical-failure status. This is a selection condition, not a claim of uniformly superior runtime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose primal simplex when a reliable primal-feasible basis is available, reduced costs still violate dual feasibility, and explicit vertex solutions are valuable.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Simplex Selection Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simplex feasibility statements are standard and the condition fits the leaf, but the operational selection criteria, accuracy claims, and stated terminal outcomes have no cited support.

assumptions_latex: The LP is represented as \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
A nonsingular basis \(B\) yields dual-feasible reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual simplex is selected when dual feasibility is available and modifications primarily disturb primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational condition for choosing dual simplex from an available dual-feasible basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select dual simplex when an initial or inherited basis \(B\) satisfies \(\bar c_N\ge0\), while some component of \(x_B=B^{-1}b\) is negative, particularly after changes to bounds or right-hand sides. Dual simplex preserves dual feasibility, selects a primal-infeasible basic variable to leave, and pivots until \(x_B\ge0\), or returns an infeasibility or numerical-failure status. The rule presumes that retaining the dual-feasible basis is cheaper than constructing a new primal-feasible start.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose dual simplex when a trustworthy basis remains dual feasible but becomes primal infeasible, especially after bound or right-hand-side changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Simplex Selection Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual-simplex invariant is standard and the content kind fits, but the selection recommendation and comparative restart-cost premise require an authoritative source.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual LP pair admits a strictly feasible or infeasible-start primal-dual formulation.
Sparse linear-system solves for Newton directions are computationally viable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Select a primal-dual interior-point method when scalable sparse iterations and nonvertex intermediate solutions are acceptable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational selection condition for primal-dual interior-point solution of a large sparse LP.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43
8.6 Affine Scaling, Primal-Dual Path Following, and Predictor-Corrector Variants of Interior Point Methods p. 428

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select a primal-dual interior-point method when the LP is large and sparse, sparse factorization of the Newton system is viable, and a basic solution is not required immediately. Starting from positive \(x\) and \(s\), the method approximately solves primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and perturbed complementarity \(Ax=b\), \(A^\top y+s=c\), and \(XSe=\mu e\), while driving \(\mu\downarrow0\). If a basic optimal solution is required, the selection must include crossover and its anticipated cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an interior-point method for large sparse LPs when Newton systems are manageable and a nonbasic solution is acceptable, adding crossover when a basis is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Selection Regime

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43
8.6 Affine Scaling, Primal-Dual Path Following, and Predictor-Corrector Variants of Interior Point Methods p. 428

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited sections support primal-dual interior-point equations, but they do not clearly support the complete solver-selection and crossover policy. The symbols X, S, e, and mu used in the statement are not introduced.

assumptions_latex: The LP has a first-order saddle formulation \(\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y} L(x,y)\).
Matrix-vector products and projections or proximal maps are cheaper than factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Select a first-order method when moderate residual accuracy suffices and memory or factorization cost dominates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection condition for matrix-free or low-memory first-order LP algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select a first-order method when iterations can be implemented using matrix-vector products with \(A\) and \(A^\top\), projections or proximal maps on \(X\) and \(Y\), and no direct factorization, and when the requested termination tolerance \(\varepsilon\) permits many inexpensive iterations. The solver must stop only after its prescribed primal residual, dual residual, and normalized duality gap are at most \(\varepsilon\). Do not select this regime solely from problem size when high-accuracy basis recovery is mandatory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a first-order solver when matrix-vector operations are cheap, memory or factorization is limiting, moderate certified accuracy suffices, and basis recovery is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Selection Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is appropriately scoped, but no source supports the LP-specific selection rule or the requirement that three differently scaled diagnostics all be bounded by the same epsilon.

assumptions_latex: The LP belongs to a recognized structural class \(\mathcal C\).
A specialized algorithm for \(\mathcal C\) preserves the original feasibility and objective semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Select the specialized solver only after structural recognition and compatibility checks succeed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection condition for structure-exploiting LP solvers after explicit model recognition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an LP \(P\), select the specialized solver \(S_{\mathcal C}\) only if a recognition procedure certifies \(P\in\mathcal C\), the transformation into the solver's representation is equivalence preserving, and \(S_{\mathcal C}\) satisfies requirements \(R\) for accuracy, certificates, warm starts, and output form. Compare its estimated total work, including transformation and recovery, with eligible general-purpose methods. If recognition or equivalence validation fails, the policy must fall back to a general LP solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a specialized solver only when model structure is certified, transformations preserve equivalence, required outputs are supported, and total estimated work beats general methods.
knowledge_statements.title: Specialized Solver Selection Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits specialized-solver selection, but the recognition, equivalence-validation, eligibility, and total-work comparison policy is uncited and too consequential to treat as source-independent.

assumptions_latex: A finite eligible solver set \(\mathcal S\) and model feature map \(\phi\) are fixed.
Each solver has a deterministic static score function \(g_s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Return an eligible solver minimizing its feature-based predicted cost, with deterministic tie-breaking.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic pre-solve selection using only features computed before optimization begins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an LP \(P\), requirements \(R\), and solver set \(\mathcal S\). Compute static features \(\phi(P)\), including dimensions, sparsity, coefficient scales, structural tags, and requested output type. Form the eligible set \(E(P,R)=\{s\in\mathcal S:s\text{ supports }R\}\). If \(E(P,R)=\varnothing\), return unsupported. Otherwise output \(s^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in E(P,R)}g_s(\phi(P))\), resolving ties by a fixed order. No runtime observation from solving \(P\) may enter \(\phi(P)\) or the decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute pre-solve model features, discard solvers that cannot meet requirements, and deterministically choose the eligible solver with the smallest predicted cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Static Model-Feature Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the automatic-selection leaf, but the feature set and scoring policy lack evidence. The statement also includes requested output type in phi(P) even though requirements R are a separate input, so the feature-map arguments are ambiguous.

assumptions_latex: A dataset \(D=\{(\phi(P_i),m_{is})\}\) records comparable outcomes for solver configurations \(s\in\mathcal S\).
Training and evaluation instances are separated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fit a portfolio policy on historical outcomes and select the eligible solver minimizing predicted penalized cost.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Offline portfolio selection learned from historical LP performance observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given historical data \(D\), choose a loss \(\ell\) that assigns a finite penalty to timeouts and invalid outcomes. Fit predictors \(\widehat m_s\) using only training instances by minimizing a regularized empirical loss over \(D\). For a new LP \(P\), compute \(\phi(P)\), remove configurations incompatible with requested requirements, and output \(s^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_s\widehat m_s(\phi(P))\). Record the model version, feature computation, eligibility filter, and tie rule so that the selection is reproducible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Learn solver costs from separated historical data, penalize failures consistently, filter incompatible solvers, and choose the eligible configuration with minimum predicted cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Historical Portfolio Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits historical portfolio selection, but no source supports its learning protocol, timeout penalties, prediction objective, or treatment of censored and invalid outcomes.

assumptions_latex: A finite solver set \(\mathcal S\), total budget \(B\), and checkpoint schedule \(0<\tau_1<\cdots<\tau_K\le B\) are fixed.
Runtime diagnostics are comparable across eligible solvers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Allocate or switch solver effort at checkpoints while preserving total budget and validating the final result.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online solver selection driven by diagnostics observed during the current LP solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an LP, eligible solvers \(\mathcal S\), and budget \(B\). Initialize a solver using a fixed prior policy. At checkpoint \(\tau_k\), observe diagnostic state \(z_k\), including elapsed work, residuals, objective gap, numerical warnings, and progress rates. Continue, switch, or allocate additional effort according to a fixed decision map \(\pi(z_k,B-\tau_k)\). Transfer state only through a validated handoff representation. Stop on a validated terminal status or exhausted budget, and return the best validated result together with consumed resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observe progress at fixed checkpoints, then continue, switch, or reallocate effort under a total budget; validate transferred state and the final result.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Runtime Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits adaptive runtime selection, but the checkpoint policy, diagnostic normalization, state-transfer conditions, and meaning of the shared resource budget require authoritative support and fuller specification.

children.title: LP Solver Coordination-Handoff Interface
children.top_down_role: Coordination of LP engines after selection, including portfolios, fallback routes, crossover, warm starts, and reusable solver state.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: 20.5.2 Notes on Warm Start; 20.7 Optimal Basis Identification
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Concurrent LP optimizer and crossover controls

assumptions_latex: A simplex configuration \(S\) and interior-point configuration \(I\) solve the same LP under a shared budget \(B\).
Each configuration reports independently checkable terminal data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accept the first result passing common validation; otherwise continue until another validated result or budget exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent race between simplex and interior-point configurations with validation before handoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Launch \(S\) and \(I\) concurrently on identical LP data with prescribed resource shares whose aggregate use does not exceed \(B\). When either configuration reports a terminal status, validate primal feasibility, dual feasibility, objective consistency, and any infeasibility or unboundedness certificate under common tolerances. Declare the first validated report the winner, cancel the other configuration, and hand off the validated solution, basis, or certificate. If a report fails validation, retain its diagnostics and continue the remaining configuration until validation or budget exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run simplex and interior-point configurations concurrently, accept only the first commonly validated result, and account for aggregate resources before canceling the loser.
knowledge_statements.title: Simplex–Interior-Point Races

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches the race container, but the first-validated-winner policy, common validation semantics, cancellation behavior, and aggregate resource accounting are unsupported by a source.

assumptions_latex: A finite configuration set \(\mathcal C=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}\) and aggregate budget \(B\) are fixed.
All configurations solve equivalent LP representations and use common validation tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Return the earliest commonly validated terminal result under the aggregate budget, or a budget-exhausted status.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent race among multiple solver algorithms, parameterizations, or numerical configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose nonnegative resource allocations \(r_1,\ldots,r_m\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^m r_i\le B\), and launch every configuration with \(r_i>0\). Process terminal reports in arrival order using one validator for primal and dual residuals, objective consistency, and certificates. Return the first report that passes validation and cancel or checkpoint all remaining configurations. If no report validates, reallocate only unused budget according to a predetermined rule; return budget exhausted when the aggregate consumption reaches \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Race several solver configurations under one aggregate budget, validate reports uniformly in arrival order, reallocate only unused resources, and return the first valid result.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Configuration Races

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits multi-configuration races, but no source supports the proposed orchestration. It also does not precisely distinguish allocated quotas r_i from actual aggregate resource consumption during concurrent execution.

children.title: Winner Validation
children.top_down_role: Checks applied to the provisional winner before its result is accepted.

assumptions_latex: The submitted LP is in standard form \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\), with dual variables \((y,s)\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\).
Validation tolerances \(\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_g\ge 0\) and a deterministic scaling convention are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The candidate is accepted as the winner exactly when \(r_p\le\tau_p\), \(r_d\le\tau_d\), \(r_g\le\tau_g\), and its claimed termination status agrees with these tests.

notation.meaning: scaled dual feasibility and sign residual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation predicate for a finite candidate returned by a concurrent LP solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a candidate tuple \((x,y,s,\sigma)\), independently recompute the scaled residuals \(r_p\), \(r_d\), and \(r_g\) from the original, unpresolved LP data. Accept an optimal-status candidate only if \(r_p\le\tau_p\), \(r_d\le\tau_d\), and \(r_g\le\tau_g\). An infeasible or unbounded status is accepted only with a separately checkable certificate for that status. A candidate failing any required test is rejected regardless of which concurrent worker finished first.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A race winner is accepted only after independent checks of primal feasibility, dual feasibility, duality gap, nonnegativity, and any claimed exceptional-status certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Winner Validation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits Winner Validation, but the residual scaling, acceptance tolerances, and status-agreement rule are implementation-specific and uncited. The exceptional-status certificate tests are also not defined precisely enough to assess the claimed acceptance equivalence.

children.title: Solution Handoff
children.top_down_role: Transfer of an accepted solution, status, or reusable state to downstream processing.

assumptions_latex: A candidate has passed winner validation against the original LP.
Presolve and scaling transformations have recorded inverse maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The handed-off result \(H\) contains the reconstructed solution, status, objective value, residuals, provenance, and any certificate needed to recheck the status.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical payload of a validated solver-to-caller handoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A solution handoff is the record \(H=(\sigma,x,y,s,z,r,\pi)\), where \((x,y,s)\) are expressed in the original model coordinates, \(z=c^{\mathsf T}x\), \(r\) contains independently recomputed residuals, and \(\pi\) identifies the winning method and applied transformations. For an optimal status, the record includes primal and dual solutions; for infeasible or unbounded status, it substitutes the corresponding verifiable certificate. No presolved-only vector is exposed as an original-model solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The handoff reconstructs original-model variables and carries status, objective, residuals, provenance, and the certificate appropriate to that status.
knowledge_statements.title: Solution Handoff

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is an appropriate kind for this leaf, but the required fields and status-dependent substitutions define an implementation contract without authoritative support.

children.title: Rejected-Winner Fallback
children.top_down_role: Fallback routing when the apparent race winner fails validation.

assumptions_latex: Concurrent workers have an ordered set of completed or resumable candidates.
The first completed candidate has failed validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The route returns the first later candidate that validates, or an unresolved failure status when no admissible candidate remains.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fallback after a nominal concurrent winner fails independent validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the rejected set as \(R=\varnothing\). For each completed candidate \(q_i\) in fallback order \(\prec\), evaluate \(V(q_i)\). If \(V(q_i)=1\), stop remaining workers and hand off \(q_i\). If \(V(q_i)=0\), add \(i\) to \(R\) and continue or resume the next admissible worker. If no candidate remains, return an unresolved numerical-failure status together with \(R\) and the failed validation diagnostics; never hand off a rejected candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After rejecting the first finisher, validate later or resumed candidates in priority order; return the first valid one or an unresolved diagnostic result.
knowledge_statements.title: Rejected-Winner Fallback

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the fallback leaf, but its priority, resume, cancellation, and terminal-status policies are implementation choices with no cited source.

assumptions_latex: Workers \(i=1,\ldots,k\) share finite processor, memory-bandwidth, and memory-capacity budgets.
Each worker has isolated logical solver state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A concurrent schedule is resource-admissible only if \(\sum_i u_{ij}(t)\le C_j\) for every resource \(j\) and time \(t\); violations can invalidate race-time comparisons or terminate workers.

notation.meaning: worker i demand for resource j at time t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic capacity boundary for concurrent LP portfolio execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each shared resource \(j\), feasibility of a concurrent execution requires \(\sum_{i=1}^{k}u_{ij}(t)\le C_j\) at every time \(t\). If memory demand exceeds \(C_j\), allocation failure may prevent a worker from returning any mathematical result. If processor or bandwidth demand saturates capacity without allocation failure, observed completion times include contention and therefore need not equal isolated solver times. Consequently, race ordering is not an intrinsic ordering of the underlying LP methods unless resource allocations are controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver race is resource-admissible only within shared capacity limits; contention can change finish order, while memory exhaustion can eliminate workers entirely.
knowledge_statements.title: Concurrent Resource Contention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the pointwise additive-capacity condition is a particular deterministic resource model. Processor and bandwidth oversubscription can be scheduled or queued, so the claimed necessity requires an explicit model and source.

assumptions_latex: A sequential portfolio supplies solver configurations \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\).
Each solver reports a classified numerical outcome and preserves the original LP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The route stops at the first validated result and otherwise returns numerical failure after exhausting all configurations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential rerouting after breakdown, instability, or failed numerical validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run \(S_1\) on the LP. After configuration \(S_i\) returns \(q_i\), accept and stop if \(V(q_i)=1\). If its outcome lies in the retryable numerical set \(\mathcal N\), record the diagnostics and invoke \(S_{i+1}\) using a numerically distinct configuration, such as alternative scaling, ordering, algorithm, or precision. Do not reinterpret numerical failure as mathematical infeasibility. If \(i=m\) and no result validates, return numerical failure with the accumulated diagnostic sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retry a numerically failed solve with ordered, numerically distinct configurations; accept only a validated result and never relabel numerical failure as infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Failure Fallback Routes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the route leaf, but the retryable set, configuration ordering, and terminal numerical-failure policy are uncited and materially determine the procedure.

assumptions_latex: A sequential portfolio has configurations with declared time, iteration, and memory budgets.
Resource-limit outcomes are distinguishable from mathematical solver statuses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The route returns the first validated result, or resource exhaustion with a complete budget ledger if no eligible configuration succeeds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential routing after time, iteration, allocation, or memory exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each configuration \(S_i\) a budget \(B_i\) with aggregate consumption constrained by \(\sum_i U_i\le B\). If \(S_i\) reaches its time or iteration limit, release its resources and start the next eligible configuration. After an allocation or memory failure, start another configuration only when its predicted peak demand fits the released capacity. Stop at the first validated result. If no eligible configuration remains, return resource exhaustion rather than a primal or dual mathematical status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On budget or allocation failure, release resources and try an eligible lower-demand or newly budgeted configuration; otherwise report resource exhaustion, not an LP status.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Failure Fallback Routes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The routing policy is uncited, and the meanings and units of B_i, U_i, and B are not defined sufficiently to justify the aggregate inequality. The conclusion promises a complete budget ledger that the statement does not explicitly construct.

assumptions_latex: A solver reports a provisional status from \(\{\mathrm{optimal},\mathrm{infeasible},\mathrm{unbounded}\}\).
An independent configuration or certificate checker is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A provisional status is confirmed only by an accepted certificate or an independently agreeing validated solve; disagreement produces an unresolved status.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent confirmation of terminal LP statuses in a sequential portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given provisional status \(\sigma\), first check a status-specific certificate \(w_\sigma\) against the original LP. If the certificate is accepted, confirm \(\sigma\). Otherwise run an independent configuration and validate its result \(\widehat\sigma\). Confirm only when \(\widehat\sigma=\sigma\); if the statuses disagree or the second solve also lacks a valid certificate, return unresolved status with both diagnostic records. Confirmation must not rely solely on repeating the original status flag.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Confirm a claimed optimal, infeasible, or unbounded status using its certificate or an independent validated solve; disagreement remains unresolved.
knowledge_statements.title: Status-Confirmation Routes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a routing algorithm, not a certificate: w_sigma is merely an input checked by the procedure. The proposed confirmation policy also lacks an authoritative source, so its mathematical and operational requirements cannot yet be fixed reliably.

knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy-Escalation Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Escalation from ordinary solving to tighter tolerances or higher precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\ell=1,\ldots,m\), solve or refine with configuration \(S_\ell\), recompute \(r^{(\ell)}\) in the original coordinates, and stop if \(r_p^{(\ell)}\le\tau_p\), \(r_d^{(\ell)}\le\tau_d\), and \(r_g^{(\ell)}\le\tau_g\). Otherwise escalate to tighter stopping tolerances, stronger refinement, or higher-precision arithmetic. If level \(m\) fails, return accuracy unattained with the best residual record; do not report a lower-accuracy candidate as satisfying the requested tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tighten solver stopping tolerances, strengthen refinement, or raise arithmetic precision until the original-model residuals meet the fixed requested tolerances; otherwise report that the requested accuracy was unattained.
assumptions_latex: Configurations \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\) use increasingly stringent tolerances or arithmetic.
Requested acceptance tolerances \((\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_g)\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The route returns the first candidate satisfying all requested tolerances, or accuracy unattained after the highest available level.

assumptions_latex: The primal LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), and an interior-point iterate is near optimal.
A nonsingular candidate basis can be selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs a basic feasible solution with no worse objective when its feasibility-restoring pivots terminate successfully.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-feasibility-first crossover from an interior solution to a basic solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select \(m\) linearly independent columns indexed by \(B\), preferentially from large or weakly active components of the interior iterate, and set \(x_N=0\), \(x_B=A_B^{-1}b\). While some basic component is negative, perform a primal-feasibility-restoring basis exchange chosen by a fixed anti-cycling rule. Once \(x_B\ge0\), apply objective-improving primal-simplex pivots until all reduced costs satisfy the optimality tolerance. Output the resulting basis and basic feasible solution; report crossover failure if no stable admissible pivot exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a basis from the interior solution, restore primal feasibility by pivots, then use primal-simplex pivots to obtain an optimal basic solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Crossover

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but this exact basis-selection and feasibility-restoration procedure is uncited. The claimed no-worse objective is not defined relative to a reference solution and does not follow merely from successful feasibility-restoring pivots.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair satisfies \(Ax=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), and \(x,s\ge0\) approximately.
A nonsingular candidate basis can be selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs a dual-feasible basis and reaches a primal-feasible optimal basic solution when its dual-simplex pivots terminate successfully.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-feasibility-first crossover from an interior solution to a basic solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select a nonsingular basis \(B\) for which the computed nonbasic reduced costs \(\bar c_N\) satisfy \(\bar c_N\ge0\) within tolerance. Form \(x_N=0\) and \(x_B=A_B^{-1}b\). While a basic component is negative, perform a dual-simplex pivot that preserves nonnegative reduced costs, using a fixed anti-cycling rule. When \(x_B\ge0\), the basis is primal and dual feasible and is handed off as optimal. Report crossover failure if dual feasibility cannot be maintained by a stable admissible pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a dual-feasible basis from the interior iterate and apply dual-simplex pivots until its basic primal solution becomes feasible and optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Crossover

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional dual-simplex logic is plausible and the algorithm kind fits, but the exact crossover construction, tolerances, stable-pivot requirement, and failure boundary require an authoritative source.

assumptions_latex: The matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\).
The LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basis \(B\) is optimal if \(x_B\ge0\) and \(\bar c_N\ge0\); the associated primal and dual basic solutions then have equal objective values.

notation.meaning: basis indices with nonsingular basis matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality test for a basis of a standard-form minimization LP.

source_refs.locator: 11-1. Complementary Primal and Dual Bases p. 241

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an index set \(B\) with nonsingular \(A_B\), define \(x_N=0\), \(x_B=A_B^{-1}b\), \(y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\), and \(\bar c_N=c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y\). The basis is primal feasible exactly when \(x_B\ge0\), and dual feasible exactly when \(\bar c_N\ge0\). If both inequalities hold, then \(c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y\), so the primal and dual basic solutions are optimal. Strict positivity is not required, hence an optimal basis may be degenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular basis is optimal when its basic variables and nonbasic reduced costs are nonnegative; primal and dual objective values then coincide.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Basis Identification

source_witnesses.locator: 11-1. Complementary Primal and Dual Bases p. 241

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Procedure OB-P for primal optimal-basis recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal basis-adjustment stage using a primal optimal solution, the optimal partition, and an initial basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^*\in\Omega_P\), the partition \(\mathcal B\cup\mathcal N\), and an initial basis \(\mathcal M\), while there exists \(j\in\mathcal B\setminus\mathcal M\) with \(x_j^*>0\), either move \(x_j^*\) to zero while adjusting \(x_{\mathcal M}^*\) to keep \(x^*\) optimal, or pivot \(j\) into \(\mathcal M\); then adjust \(x^*\) and \(\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a primal optimal solution, the optimal partition, and an initial basis, repeatedly select a positive component indexed by B but absent from the basis. Either move that component to zero while preserving primal optimality or pivot its index into the basis, and then update the solution and basis.
assumptions_latex: x^*\in\Omega_P
\mathcal B\cup\mathcal N\text{ is the given partition}
\mathcal M\text{ is an initial basis}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: j\in\mathcal B\setminus\mathcal M,\ x_j^*>0\ \Longrightarrow\ \bigl(x_j^*\leftarrow0\text{ with }x^*\text{ remaining optimal}\bigr)\ \lor\ \bigl(j\text{ is pivoted into }\mathcal M\bigr),\text{ followed by updates of }x^*\text{ and }\mathcal M.

source_evidence.locator: Chapter 7 Superlinear Convergence and Finite Termination / 7.80. Recovering an Optimal Basis / Algorithm 7.80-extra-1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Procedure OB-D for dual optimal-basis recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual basis-adjustment stage using the basis produced by Procedure OB-P.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((\lambda^*,s^*)\in\Omega_D\), the partition \(\mathcal B\cup\mathcal N\), and the basis \(\mathcal M\) produced by Procedure OB-P, while there exists \(j\in\mathcal N\cap\mathcal M\) with \(s_j^*>0\), either move \(s_j^*\) to zero while adjusting \(s_i^*\) for \(i\in\mathcal N\setminus\mathcal M\) and \(\lambda^*\) to keep the dual solution optimal, or pivot \(j\) out of \(\mathcal M\); then adjust \((\lambda^*,s^*)\) and \(\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a dual optimal solution, the optimal partition, and the basis returned by OB-P, repeatedly select a positive dual slack whose index lies in both N and the basis. Either move that slack to zero while preserving dual optimality or pivot its index out of the basis, and then update the dual solution and basis.
assumptions_latex: (\lambda^*,s^*)\in\Omega_D
\mathcal B\cup\mathcal N\text{ is the given partition}
\mathcal M\text{ is the basis produced by Procedure OB-P}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: j\in\mathcal N\cap\mathcal M,\ s_j^*>0\ \Longrightarrow\ \bigl(s_j^*\leftarrow0\text{ with }(\lambda^*,s^*)\text{ remaining optimal}\bigr)\ \lor\ \bigl(j\text{ is pivoted out of }\mathcal M\bigr),\text{ followed by updates of }(\lambda^*,s^*)\text{ and }\mathcal M.
