children.title: Crossover Stalling
children.top_down_role: Progress-loss regimes during crossover despite continued solver activity.

assumptions_latex: A crossover procedure uses simplex-type basis exchanges.
The current basic feasible solution is degenerate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Repeated zero-length admissible pivots can leave the objective unchanged and prevent finite progress unless an anti-cycling or termination safeguard is imposed.

notation.meaning: basic feasible solution at pivot k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy-induced stalling boundary for simplex-based crossover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Crossover stalls when it generates an unbounded sequence of basis exchanges for which \(\theta_k=0\) or is below the progress tolerance and \(z_{k+1}=z_k\), without reaching the required feasibility and optimality tests. Degeneracy permits distinct bases to represent the same vertex, so admissible pivots may make no primal or objective progress and may cycle. A finite anti-cycling pivot rule, repeated-basis detection, or an iteration limit with diagnostic failure is therefore required to bound this failure mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degeneracy can produce zero-step pivots among different bases representing one vertex, causing no objective progress or cycling unless safeguards intervene.
knowledge_statements.title: Crossover Stalling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, and degeneracy-related zero-step cycling is standard, but the proposed definition of stalling as an unbounded sequence and the asserted safeguard requirements need a specific simplex degeneracy or anti-cycling source.

children.title: Crossover Instability
children.top_down_role: Numerical reliability failures arising during crossover.

knowledge_statements.title: Crossover Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ill-conditioning boundary for recovering a simplex basis from an interior-point solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider basic recovery for the standard-form system \(Bx_B=b\). For \(B_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon)\), \(0<\varepsilon<1\), and \(\delta b_\varepsilon=(0,\varepsilon^2)^\top\), the recovered basic solution changes by \(B_\varepsilon^{-1}\delta b_\varepsilon=(0,\varepsilon)^\top\). Hence \(\|B_\varepsilon^{-1}\delta b_\varepsilon\|_2/\|\delta b_\varepsilon\|_2=1/\varepsilon\to\infty\). More generally, perturbations can be amplified by \(\|B^{-1}\|\); therefore crossover has no uniform forward-stability guarantee over candidate bases with \(\sigma_{\min}(B)\to0\), even when the incoming primal residual tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearly singular crossover bases can amplify arbitrarily small handoff residuals into much larger changes in the recovered basic solution.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon<1\)
\(B_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|B_\varepsilon^{-1}\delta b_\varepsilon\|_2/\|\delta b_\varepsilon\|_2\to\infty\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: smallest singular value of the basis matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The instability example is mathematically coherent and fits the failure-boundary leaf, but no source supports its crossover-specific interpretation or the asserted absence of a uniform forward-stability guarantee.

children.title: Crossover Recovery Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions separating recoverable crossover trouble from fallback-worthy failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Crossover Recovery Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical acceptance boundary for a basis recovered for a standard-form minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), let \(I\) contain \(m\) candidate basic indices, \(B=A_I\), \(x_I=B^{-1}b\), \(x_{I^c}=0\), \(y=B^{-\top}c_I\), and \(r_{I^c}=c_{I^c}-A_{I^c}^\top y\). Given tolerances \(\tau_p,\tau_d\ge0\) and conditioning limit \(\kappa_{\max}\), the recovered state lies inside the acceptance boundary precisely when \(B\) is nonsingular, \(\kappa(B)\le\kappa_{\max}\), \(\|Ax-b\|_\infty\le\tau_p\), \(\|(-x)_+\|_\infty\le\tau_p\), and \(\|(-r_{I^c})_+\|_\infty\le\tau_d\). Violation of any predicate places recovery outside this boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recovered basis is accepted only when it is nonsingular, adequately conditioned, and satisfies prescribed primal and dual feasibility tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\) is accepted exactly when all displayed conditioning and feasibility predicates hold.

notation.meaning: componentwise positive part of a vector

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predicates define a plausible implementation boundary, but their necessity and sufficiency, conditioning threshold, and tolerance policy are uncited. The plain statement also expresses only necessity whereas the LaTeX statement asserts an exact characterization.

knowledge_statements.title: Advanced-Basis Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of a previous simplex basis after compatible LP data changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a modified standard-form LP \(\min\{c'^\top x:A'x=b',\ x\ge0\}\) and old basic indices \(I\), form \(B'=A'_I\). Reject reuse if dimensions or column identities changed incompatibly or \(B'\) is singular. Otherwise compute \(x'_I=B'^{-1}b'\), set \(x'_{I^c}=0\), solve \(B'^\top y'=c'_I\), and compute \(r'_{I^c}=c'_{I^c}-A_{I^c}'^\top y'\). If \(x'_I\ge0\), initialize primal simplex; if \(r'_{I^c}\ge0\), initialize dual simplex; if both hold, return the optimal basis. When neither holds, send the basis to repair or construct a fresh basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse an old basis only after rebuilding its primal and dual states for the modified LP and selecting a compatible simplex mode.
assumptions_latex: \(A'\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reused basis initializes primal simplex, dual simplex, or repair according to its recomputed feasibility.

notation.meaning: basis matrix in the modified LP

source_refs.locator: 2. The Primal Simplex Method p. 91; 4. The Dual Simplex Method p. 100

source_witnesses.locator: 2. The Primal Simplex Method p. 91; 4. The Dual Simplex Method p. 100

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simplex sections support primal- and dual-feasible starts, but the cited locators do not specifically support the data-compatibility checks, basis-reuse procedure, or repair routing asserted here.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Iterate Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior-point warm start using a compatible primal–dual state from a related LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the modified pair \(Ax=b,\ x\ge0\) and \(A^\top y+s=c,\ s\ge0\), take a dimension-compatible old state \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\). Choose \(\delta>0\), set \(x^0_i=\max\{\bar x_i,\delta\}\), \(s^0_i=\max\{\bar s_i,\delta\}\), and \(y^0=\bar y\). Recompute \(r_p=Ax^0-b\), \(r_d=A^\top y^0+s^0-c\), and \(\mu=(x^0)^\top s^0/n\). Accept the state only if these quantities are finite and satisfy configured residual and complementarity limits; then start the primal–dual corrector from \((x^0,y^0,s^0)\). Otherwise route it to repair or cold initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip a compatible old iterate into the positive orthant, recompute all diagnostics, and reuse it only when residual and complementarity limits pass.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\)
\(\delta>0\)
\((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\) has compatible dimensions
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted initialization satisfies \(x^0>0\), \(s^0>0\), and the configured diagnostic bounds.

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8; Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8; Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited interior-point sections support primal-dual residual and complementarity notation, but not the particular clipping, diagnostic thresholds, or warm-start acceptance and fallback policy.

children.title: Numeric Factorization Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of previously computed numeric factorization data across related solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Numeric Factorization Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward-error criterion for reusing stored numerical factors of a simplex basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let stored factors satisfy \(P B Q\approx LU\), and let \(B'\) be the basis matrix required by the new solve. Direct numerical reuse is admissible only when the stored permutations retain their meaning and the recomputed relative backward error \(\eta=\|PB'Q-LU\|/\max\{\|B'\|,1\}\) does not exceed a prescribed \(\tau_f\). If \(B'\) differs through supported low-rank column changes, each change must first be incorporated by a stable factor update and \(\eta\) recomputed. Otherwise numerical refactorization is required. A small residual from one right-hand side alone does not validate the factors for subsequent solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stored numerical factors may be reused only after their indexing and backward error are validated against the current basis matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(B'\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\)
\(\tau_f\ge0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Numeric reuse is accepted only if \(\eta\le\tau_f\) after all supported updates.

source_refs.locator: FIVE: SPECIAL SIMPLEX IMPLEMENTATIONS AND OPTIMALITY CONDITIONS p. 201

source_witnesses.locator: FIVE: SPECIAL SIMPLEX IMPLEMENTATIONS AND OPTIMALITY CONDITIONS p. 201

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The general simplex-implementation citation does not specifically substantiate the proposed factor-reuse test or low-rank update policy. The matrix norm used in the backward-error formula is also unspecified.

children.title: Symbolic-State Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of sparsity analysis, ordering, or symbolic factorization state.

knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic-State Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural criterion for reusing sparse-factorization ordering and symbolic analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S(B)=\{(i,j):B_{ij}\ne0\}\) denote the stored basis sparsity pattern. For fixed permutations \(P,Q\) and a factorization procedure whose symbolic phase depends only on sparsity, symbolic state may be reused for \(B'\) when dimensions and index mappings agree and \(S(PB'Q)=S(PBQ)\). Numerical values must nevertheless be refactorized or validly updated. If the method performs value-dependent pivoting, the reused symbolic state is only provisional: any pivot outside the predicted structure, structural zero appearing at a required pivot, or unallocated fill invalidates it and triggers fresh symbolic analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symbolic analysis is reusable when dimensions, indexing, and permuted sparsity agree, subject to invalidation by value-dependent pivoting or unexpected fill.
assumptions_latex: \(B,B'\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\)
\(P,Q\) are fixed permutations
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pattern-preserving changes permit symbolic reuse, but do not by themselves permit numerical-factor reuse.

notation.meaning: structural nonzero pattern of a matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The structural distinction between symbolic and numerical reuse is plausible and fits the condition leaf, but no inspectable source supports the exact pattern-equivalence criterion and value-dependent invalidation rules.

children.title: Reusable-State Invalidation
children.top_down_role: Model changes or numerical conditions that invalidate stored linear-algebra state.

knowledge_statements.title: Reusable-State Invalidation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invalidation predicates for cached basis, symbolic, and numerical factorization state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cached state is invalid for a requested basis \(B'\) if at least one applicable predicate holds: its dimensions or row/column identities differ; its stored basic-index map no longer identifies \(B'\); its symbolic pattern disagrees with the permuted pattern of \(B'\); its numerical factors have backward error above \(\tau_f\); a required pivot is singular or below \(\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}\); or recomputed solve residuals exceed \(\tau_s\). Invalidation is componentwise: invalid numerical factors need not discard a still-compatible ordering, while an invalid index map invalidates every state derived from that map. No cached component may be used before its own predicates are checked.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invalidate each cached component when its indexing, structure, factor error, pivots, or solve residuals fail; retain independently valid components.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau_f,\tau_{\mathrm{piv}},\tau_s\ge0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every failed predicate invalidates its component and all cached components derived from it.

notation.meaning: basis matrix requested by the current solve

children.title: Warm-Start Acceptance Screening
children.top_down_role: Compatibility and quality screening for submitted warm-start state.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Acceptance Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type-specific screening before a simplex basis or interior-point iterate is reused.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given modified LP data and a tagged warm state, first verify finite entries, dimensions, variable identities, and scaling metadata. For a basis tag, rebuild \(B\), basic values, and reduced costs, then accept only if \(B\) passes rank and conditioning limits and the required primal or dual feasibility residual is within tolerance. For an iterate tag, recompute \(r_p=Ax-b\), \(r_d=A^\top y+s-c\), positivity violations, and \(\mu=x^\top s/n\), accepting only if all configured limits hold. Return the accepted state together with its diagnostics; otherwise return the failed predicates without silently modifying the state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check structural compatibility and recomputed method-specific diagnostics, returning either an accepted warm state or explicit failed predicates.
assumptions_latex: The warm state is tagged as a basis or primal–dual iterate
All acceptance tolerances are nonnegative
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance occurs if and only if every structural and tag-specific predicate passes.

source_refs.locator: 2. The Primal Simplex Method p. 91; 4. The Dual Simplex Method p. 100

source_witnesses.locator: 2. The Primal Simplex Method p. 91; 4. The Dual Simplex Method p. 100

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited sources cover underlying simplex and interior-point diagnostics, but they do not establish this unified tagged-state screening algorithm, metadata requirements, conditioning rule, or exact acceptance policy.

children.title: Warm-Start State Repair
children.top_down_role: Repair of incomplete, inconsistent, or numerically unsuitable warm-start state.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start State Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded repair procedure applied after a warm state fails acceptance screening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a rejected tagged state and repair budget \(K\), preserve its compatible identifiers. For a basis state, replace dependent or numerically unacceptable columns by rank-increasing eligible columns, recompute basic values and reduced costs, and rescreen after each of at most \(K\) replacements. For an iterate state, impose positive floors on \(x,s\), compute a primal–dual Newton or least-squares residual correction, choose a step preserving strict positivity, and rescreen after each of at most \(K\) corrections. Return the first state passing acceptance screening. If no state passes within the budget, return repair failure and leave cold initialization to rejection routing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply bounded, type-specific corrections and return only a state that subsequently passes the full acceptance screen.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb N\)
The state retains compatible variable identities
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Repair returns either a screened acceptable state within \(K\) corrections or an explicit failure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm combines basis-column replacement and primal-dual iterate correction into a specific bounded repair policy without a source supporting the correction choices, safeguards, or claimed interface behavior.

children.title: Warm-Start Rejection Routing
children.top_down_role: Fallback behavior when warm-start state cannot be accepted or repaired.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Rejection Routing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic fallback routing after screening or bounded repair rejects a warm state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Route a rejected warm state by its failed predicates. Incompatible dimensions, variable identities, or nonfinite data imply cold initialization. A singular or structurally invalid basis is sent to basis crash; a nonsingular basis with \(x_B\ge0\) but infeasible reduced costs starts primal simplex, while one with feasible reduced costs but infeasible \(x_B\) starts dual simplex. A compatible finite primal–dual iterate with excessive residuals or complementarity is sent to bounded repair. Any repair-budget exhaustion, repeated numerical breakdown, or state satisfying neither a supported simplex-start condition nor an iterate-repair condition is routed to cold initialization. The router returns exactly one destination and the triggering predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map each rejection cause to basis crash, primal simplex, dual simplex, bounded iterate repair, or cold initialization.
assumptions_latex: Each failed screening predicate is recorded
Solver fallback destinations are available
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every rejected state is assigned exactly one supported fallback destination.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simplex feasibility implications are standard, but the deterministic routing priorities, repair eligibility, numerical-breakdown handling, and exactly-one-destination guarantee are implementation-specific and uncited.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic partition of conditions under which reuse cannot safely initialize the requested LP method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a cached state \(w\), define \(F_{\mathrm{str}}\) by incompatible dimensions, identities, or sparsity; \(F_{\mathrm{num}}\) by nonfinite values, singular required matrices, or failed factor residuals; \(F_{\mathrm{feas}}\) by primal, dual, bound, positivity, or complementarity diagnostics exceeding their limits; and \(F_{\mathrm{prog}}\) by exhaustion of the repair budget or repeated failure to reduce the selected residual measure. Warm-start reuse fails whenever \(w\in F_{\mathrm{str}}\cup F_{\mathrm{num}}\cup F_{\mathrm{feas}}\cup F_{\mathrm{prog}}\). Structural failures require reconstruction or cold start; the other regimes may permit bounded repair, but reuse is prohibited until the full acceptance predicate holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Warm starts fail through structural incompatibility, numerical invalidity, excessive optimality residuals, or exhausted repair progress.
assumptions_latex: Acceptance limits and a finite repair budget are fixed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w\in F_{\mathrm{str}}\cup F_{\mathrm{num}}\cup F_{\mathrm{feas}}\cup F_{\mathrm{prog}}\) prohibits immediate reuse.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four-way diagnostic partition fits the failure-boundary container, but the taxonomy and its prescribed reconstruction, repair, and reuse consequences have no supporting source.

children.title: Revised Simplex Implementations
children.top_down_role: Architectures centered on revised-simplex linear-algebra state.

knowledge_statements.title: Revised Simplex Implementations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal revised-simplex iteration for a standard-form minimization LP in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), initialize a feasible basis \(I\), \(B=A_I\), and \(x_I=B^{-1}b\). Solve \(B^\top y=c_I\) and compute \(r_j=c_j-a_j^\top y\) for nonbasic \(j\). If every \(r_j\ge0\), return \(x\) as optimal. Otherwise select \(j\) with \(r_j<0\), solve \(Bd=a_j\), and, if \(d\le0\), return the ray proving unboundedness. Select a leaving index from \(\arg\min_{i:d_i>0}(x_I)_i/d_i\), pivot, update the basis factors, and repeat. With an anti-cycling selection rule, the exact-arithmetic procedure terminates finitely at an optimum or an unboundedness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Revised simplex computes multipliers, reduced costs, directions, and ratio tests through basis solves rather than maintaining the full tableau.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank
The initial basis is primal feasible
An anti-cycling pivot rule is used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration terminates with an optimal basic feasible solution or an unboundedness certificate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: BTRAN computation of simplex multipliers and reduced costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-form-inverse pricing operation in revised simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If B_t^{-1}=E_{t-1}E_{t-2}\cdots E_1, compute w=c_BB_t^{-1} by successively postmultiplying c_B by E_{t-1},E_{t-2},\ldots,E_1. Then compute z_j-c_j=wa_j-c_j for each nonbasic column a_j and use these quantities in the optimality test and entering-variable selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the stored elementary transformations to the basic-cost row in reverse chronological order. The resulting simplex multiplier gives the reduced-cost quantities used to stop or select an entering variable.
assumptions_latex: B_t\text{ is the current nonsingular basis matrix}
c_B\text{ is the row vector of current basic costs}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w=c_BB_t^{-1},\qquad z_j-c_j=wa_j-c_j\quad(j\text{ nonbasic}).

children.title: Tableau Simplex Implementations
children.top_down_role: Architectures centered on explicit or maintained tableau representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Tableau Simplex Implementations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense primal-simplex implementation for equality-form linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\), with nonsingular basis \(B=A_{\mathcal B}\), maintain a tableau containing \(B^{-1}A\), \(B^{-1}b\), and reduced costs \(\bar c^{\mathsf T}=c^{\mathsf T}-c_{\mathcal B}^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}A\). Choose a nonbasic \(j\) with \(\bar c_j<0\), set \(u=B^{-1}a_j\), and choose \(i\in\arg\min\{(B^{-1}b)_k/u_k:u_k>0\}\). If no \(u_k>0\) exists, report primal unboundedness. Otherwise pivot on row \(i\), column \(j\), updating every tableau entry by row operations. Stop with the current basic solution when every nonbasic reduced cost is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tableau implementation stores all transformed columns, right-hand sides, and reduced costs, then performs pricing, a ratio test, and full row-operation updates at each pivot; a finite anti-cycling pivot rule ensures termination.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
The current basis \(B\) is nonsingular and \(B^{-1}b\ge0\).
Entering and leaving choices use a pivot rule known to prevent cycling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates with an optimal basic feasible solution or a primal-unboundedness certificate.

children.title: Bound-Flipping Simplex Implementations
children.top_down_role: Architectures using bound flips to extend simplex movement.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Flipping Simplex Implementations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-simplex architecture for variables having finite lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \\(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\\), maintain each nonbasic variable at one of its bounds. After selecting an improving nonbasic variable \\(x_j\\), move it in its improving direction and compute the induced basic direction. Process encountered breakpoints at which a basic variable reaches a bound. An eligible nonbasic variable with finite opposite bound may instead be flipped directly from \\(\ell_j\\) to \\(u_j\\), or conversely, while its column contribution is accumulated into the basic right-hand side. Continue through flips until a basis exchange is required, the entering variable reaches its opposite bound, or the improving ray proves unbounded. Recompute or update the basis representation after an actual pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound-flipping simplex traverses finite-bound breakpoints, allowing nonbasic variables to change bounds without a basis exchange and pivoting only when necessary.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
The maintained basic solution satisfies \(Ax=b\) and \(\ell\le x\le u\).
Every performed flip has a finite opposite bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted move preserves primal feasibility and either improves the objective, changes the active-bound configuration, pivots, or detects unboundedness.

children.title: Full Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing regimes that inspect the complete eligible candidate set.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive entering-variable search in primal simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a primal-feasible basis \\(B\\) for \\(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\\), compute \\(y=B^{-\mathsf T}c_{\mathcal B}\\) and \\(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y\\) for every \\(j\notin\mathcal B\\). If \\(\bar c_j\ge-\tau\\) for every nonbasic index, stop and declare optimality to tolerance \\(\tau\ge0\\). Otherwise select an entering index from the complete eligible set \\(E=\{j\notin\mathcal B:\bar c_j<-\tau\}\\) according to the configured pricing rule, then perform the ratio test. Thus every pricing iteration examines the entire nonbasic set before either selecting a column or declaring optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full pricing evaluates every nonbasic reduced cost, selects from all improving columns, and declares optimality only after the complete scan finds none.
assumptions_latex: The current basis is primal feasible.
The problem is a minimization problem in equality standard form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An empty full-scan eligible set certifies reduced-cost optimality to tolerance \(\tau\).

children.title: Partial Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing regimes that inspect restricted candidate subsets.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise entering-variable search in primal simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the nonbasic indices into blocks \\(S_1,\ldots,S_q\\). At a primal-feasible basis, scan the current block and compute \\(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}B^{-\mathsf T}c_{\mathcal B}\\) only for its members. If some \\(j\\) satisfies \\(\bar c_j<-\tau\\), choose an eligible member by the configured local rule and perform a simplex iteration. Otherwise advance to another block. An optimality declaration is permitted only after every current nonbasic index has been examined, without an intervening basis change invalidating its reduced cost, and no eligible column has been found. After a pivot, restart or invalidate the accumulated scan as required by the implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial pricing scans nonbasic columns in blocks, reducing per-search work while requiring complete valid coverage before it may declare optimality.
assumptions_latex: The current basis is primal feasible.
The blocks cover every current nonbasic index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scheme selects an improving column when found and declares optimality only after a valid exhaustive block cycle.

children.title: Pricing-Coverage Switching
children.top_down_role: Conditions motivating transitions between full and partial candidate coverage.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Coverage Switching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive switching between partial and full reduced-cost scans.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a pricing mode \\(M\in\{\mathrm{partial},\mathrm{full}\}\\). In partial mode, inspect configured blocks and record search-effort diagnostics such as consecutive unsuccessful blocks or pivots since the last complete scan. Switch to full mode when a prescribed deterministic trigger is met, whenever partial coverage finds no eligible column, and before any optimality declaration. In full mode, evaluate every current nonbasic reduced cost; pivot if some \\(\bar c_j<-\tau\\), otherwise stop. The implementation may return to partial mode after a pivot or a prescribed number of full scans. Any reduced costs invalidated by a basis change are discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive controller uses partial scans for economy but forces full coverage after search failures and before certifying reduced-cost optimality.
assumptions_latex: Each switching trigger is fixed independently of uncomputed reduced costs.
A full scan covers every current nonbasic index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Switching cannot produce a false optimality declaration when termination requires a valid full scan with \(\bar c_j\ge-\tau\) for all nonbasic \(j\).

children.title: Dantzig Pricing
children.top_down_role: Candidate selection using the classical Dantzig pricing criterion.

knowledge_statements.title: Dantzig Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical most-negative-reduced-cost rule for primal minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a primal-feasible basis \\(B\\) for an equality-form minimization problem, compute nonbasic reduced costs \\(\bar c_j=c_j-c_{\mathcal B}^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}a_j\\). With eligibility tolerance \\(\tau\ge0\\), form \\(E=\{j\notin\mathcal B:\bar c_j<-\tau\}\\). If \\(E=\varnothing\\), report reduced-cost optimality to tolerance. Otherwise choose \\(j^*\in\arg\min_{j\in E}\bar c_j\\), resolve multiple minimizers by a fixed tie rule, and pass \\(j^*\\) to the primal ratio test. This is Dantzig's pricing rule under the minimization sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dantzig pricing enters a nonbasic variable having the most negative eligible reduced cost, with a separate deterministic rule resolving ties.
assumptions_latex: The current basis is primal feasible.
Reduced costs use the minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected entering variable maximizes the predicted objective decrease per unit increase among eligible nonbasic variables.

children.title: Largest-Reduced-Cost Pricing
children.top_down_role: Candidate selection based on reduced-cost magnitude.

knowledge_statements.title: Largest-Reduced-Cost Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum signed reduced-cost violation pricing for bounded-variable primal simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\), suppose each movable nonbasic variable is at an active bound. Define its feasible movement sign by \(d_j=1\) when \(x_j=\ell_j<u_j\) and \(d_j=-1\) when \(x_j=u_j>\ell_j\). If \(\bar c_j\) is its reduced cost, define the improvement score \(s_j=-d_j\bar c_j\). Given \(\tau\ge0\), let \(E=\{j\notin\mathcal B:s_j>\tau\}\). If \(E\ne\varnothing\), choose \(j^*\in\arg\max_{j\in E}s_j\), resolve ties by a fixed rule, and submit the movement \(d_{j^*}\) to the applicable primal ratio test. In lower-bound standard form, \(d_j=1\), so this rule chooses the most negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Largest-reduced-cost pricing chooses the feasible nonbasic bound movement with the greatest signed reduced-cost improvement; in lower-bound standard form it coincides with Dantzig pricing.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c,\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\ell\le u\).
The current basis is primal feasible, and every considered nonbasic variable has a nonzero feasible movement away from its active bound.
Reduced costs use the minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected movement has maximum first-order objective improvement per unit variable displacement among eligible nonbasic movements.

notation.meaning: sign of the feasible movement away from the active bound

children.title: Reduced-Cost Tie Regimes
children.top_down_role: Selection behavior when multiple candidates have comparable reduced-cost priority.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Tie Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic resolution of equal or numerically indistinguishable pricing scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite nonempty eligible pricing set, let \(s_j\in\mathbb R\) be the score maximized by the pricing rule for each \(j\in E\), and let \(\delta\ge0\). Define the numerical tie set by \(T=\{j\in E:s_j\ge\max_{k\in E}s_k-\delta\}\). A deterministic tie regime is a selector \(\phi(E,s,\delta)\in T\). Examples include choosing \(\min T\), choosing cyclically the first member of \(T\) after the previously selected index with wraparound, or minimizing a fixed secondary score over \(T\) with a further deterministic tie rule. Such a selector affects the pivot trajectory, but tie resolution by itself does not guarantee finite termination under degeneracy; that guarantee requires a complete anti-cycling pivot rule, such as Bland's entering-and-leaving ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced-cost tie regime deterministically selects one nearly maximal pricing candidate; tie resolution alone is not a complete anti-cycling guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The eligible set \(E\) is finite and nonempty.
Scores are compared using a fixed tolerance \(\delta\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selector returns an index in \(T\); finite termination follows only when the complete pivot rule has an independently established anti-cycling property.

children.title: Steepest-Edge Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing based on maintained steepest-edge weight information.

knowledge_statements.title: Steepest-Edge Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Euclidean edge-normalized pricing for primal simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a primal-feasible basis \\(B\\), each eligible nonbasic column \\(a_j\\) defines the full-space edge direction with nonbasic component one and basic components \\(-B^{-1}a_j\\). Its squared Euclidean length is \\(w_j=1+\lVert B^{-1}a_j\rVert_2^2\\). For minimization, form \\(E=\{j\notin\mathcal B:\bar c_j<0\}\\) and choose \\(j^*\in\arg\max_{j\in E}(-\bar c_j)/\sqrt{w_j}\\). Apply a deterministic tie rule and then the primal ratio test. If \\(E\\) is empty, the current basic feasible solution is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Steepest-edge pricing divides each predicted objective improvement by the Euclidean length of its simplex edge and chooses the largest normalized improvement.
assumptions_latex: The current basis is primal feasible.
Edge lengths are measured in the full variable-space Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The chosen entering column gives the greatest first-order objective decrease per unit Euclidean movement among eligible adjacent edge directions.

children.title: Devex Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing based on approximate edge-weight information.

knowledge_statements.title: Devex Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate steepest-edge pricing with inexpensive maintained weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a primal-feasible basis, maintain positive estimates \\(\widehat w_j\\) of the exact squared edge lengths \\(w_j=1+\lVert B^{-1}a_j\rVert_2^2\\). For the eligible set \\(E=\{j\notin\mathcal B:\bar c_j<0\}\\), choose \\(j^*\in\arg\max_{j\in E}(-\bar c_j)/\sqrt{\widehat w_j}\\). After the pivot, update the approximate weights using the pivot row and transformed entering column, enforcing a positive lower safeguard. Periodically, or when approximation-quality diagnostics fail, reinitialize the weights from the current reference framework. If \\(E\\) is empty, stop with the current basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Devex pricing approximates steepest-edge scores using safeguarded, cheaply updated edge weights and periodically resets them when their quality deteriorates.
assumptions_latex: The current basis is primal feasible.
Every maintained weight satisfies \(\widehat w_j>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pricing is well-defined and approximates exact steepest-edge selection without recomputing every exact edge norm after each pivot.

children.title: Edge-Weight Accuracy Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Implementation regimes balancing weight fidelity against maintenance cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Edge-Weight Accuracy Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of approximate edge weights on pricing scores and implementation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let exact and approximate positive squared edge weights satisfy \\((1-\varepsilon)w_j\le\widehat w_j\le(1+\varepsilon)w_j\\) for all eligible \\(j\\), where \\(0\le\varepsilon<1\\). If \\(q_j=(-\bar c_j)/\sqrt{w_j}\\) and \\(\widehat q_j=(-\bar c_j)/\sqrt{\widehat w_j}\\), then \\[\frac{q_j}{\sqrt{1+\varepsilon}}\le\widehat q_j\le\frac{q_j}{\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}}.\] Consequently, if \\(\widehat j\\) maximizes \\(\widehat q_j\\) and \\(j^*\\) maximizes \\(q_j\\), then \\[q_{\widehat j}\ge\sqrt{\frac{1-\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}}\,q_{j^*}.\] Tighter weights improve fidelity to exact steepest-edge selection but generally require more computation or more frequent reinitialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly accurate edge weights yield a quantified approximation to exact steepest-edge pricing; cheaper weight maintenance may weaken that selection fidelity.
assumptions_latex: Every eligible reduced cost is negative.
Exact and approximate weights are positive and satisfy the displayed relative-error bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Approximate pricing attains at least \(\sqrt{(1-\varepsilon)/(1+\varepsilon)}\) of the best exact normalized score.

children.title: Primal Ratio Tests
children.top_down_role: Ratio-test families used within primal simplex pivot selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Ratio Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving step selection for primal standard-form simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \\(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\\), let the current basic vector be \\(x_{\mathcal B}=B^{-1}b\ge0\\), and let eligible nonbasic variable \\(x_j\\) increase from zero. Compute \\(u=B^{-1}a_j\\), so \\(x_{\mathcal B}(\theta)=x_{\mathcal B}-\theta u\\). If \\(u_i\le0\\) for every \\(i\\), the improving edge is unbounded. Otherwise set \\(\theta^*=\min_{i:u_i>0}(x_{\mathcal B})_i/u_i\\), choose a leaving index among the minimizers using the configured tie or anti-degeneracy rule, and pivot. The step \\(\theta^*\\) is the largest nonnegative step preserving primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal ratio test takes the largest feasible step along an entering edge, selects a limiting basic variable, or certifies an improving unbounded ray.
assumptions_latex: The current basis is primal feasible.
The entering variable has an improving reduced cost under the minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The test returns a feasibility-preserving pivot step and leaving row, or an unboundedness certificate when no positive pivot component exists.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.8 The Simplex Method in Tableau Format p. 125

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Leaving-variable selection during a primal-simplex pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: During a primal-simplex pivot with entering-column index \(\beta\), the ratio test chooses a leaving variable \(x_{k_\alpha}\) whose admissible ratio \(-p_\alpha/q_{\alpha\beta}\) is minimal among the eligible leaving-variable indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal simplex ratio test selects a leaving basic variable that attains the smallest eligible blocking ratio, minus p-alpha divided by q-alpha-beta.
assumptions_latex: \beta\text{ is the entering-column index}
\alpha\text{ ranges over eligible leaving-variable indices}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\gamma\ \mathrm{eligible}}\left(-\frac{p_\gamma}{q_{\gamma\beta}}\right).

children.title: Dual Ratio Tests
children.top_down_role: Ratio-test families used within dual simplex pivot selection.

assumptions_latex: \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\) has a nonsingular basis matrix \(B\).
The current basis is dual feasible: \(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\ge 0\) for every nonbasic \(j\).
Some basic component \((B^{-1}b)_p<0\) is selected to leave.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\in\arg\min_{j:\bar a_{pj}<0}\bar c_j/(-\bar a_{pj})\), with infeasibility declared when this index set is empty.

notation.meaning: Simplex tableau coefficient in the selected leaving row.
Reduced cost of nonbasic variable j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form dual-simplex ratio test under the minimization and nonnegative-reduced-cost convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(x_B=B^{-1}b\), select a row \(p\) with \((x_B)_p<0\), and form \(J_p=\{j\in N:\bar a_{pj}<0\}\). If \(J_p=\varnothing\), the dual-feasible tableau certifies primal infeasibility. Otherwise choose \(q\in\arg\min_{j\in J_p}\bar c_j/(-\bar a_{pj})\), apply a deterministic tie rule, and pivot on \(\bar a_{pq}\). The ratio choice preserves nonnegativity of the updated reduced costs; iteration stops when \(x_B\ge0\), yielding a primal-and-dual feasible basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual ratio test chooses an entering column that repairs a negative basic variable while preserving reduced-cost feasibility; absence of an eligible column certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Ratio Tests

children.title: Primal–Dual Ratio-Test Contrasts
children.top_down_role: Structural differences in candidate eligibility, stability, and selection behavior.

assumptions_latex: The primal and dual simplex methods use the same nonsingular basis \(B\).
The primal convention maintains \(B^{-1}b\ge0\); the dual convention maintains nonnegative reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal test bounds a primal step by basic feasibility, whereas the dual test bounds a reduced-cost step by dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contrast for standard primal and dual simplex minimization conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In primal simplex, an improving entering column \(q\) is fixed and the ratio test selects \(p\in\arg\min_{i:d_i>0}(x_B)_i/d_i\), where \(d=B^{-1}a_q\); this preserves primal feasibility. In dual simplex, an infeasible leaving row \(p\) is fixed and the ratio test selects \(q\in\arg\min_{j:\bar a_{pj}<0}\bar c_j/(-\bar a_{pj})\); this preserves dual feasibility. Thus the tests interchange the roles of row and column selection and of primal values and reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal simplex fixes an entering column and protects basic feasibility; dual simplex fixes a leaving row and protects reduced-cost feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Ratio-Test Contrasts

assumptions_latex: A primal-feasible basis and entering column \(q\) are given, with \(d=B^{-1}a_q\).
Feasibility tolerances \(\delta_i\ge0\) are fixed for basic variables.
At least one component \(d_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected leaving row lies within the relaxed blocking interval and maximizes pivot magnitude among its admissible rows.

notation.meaning: Basic-variable change induced by the entering column.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal Harris test with rowwise feasibility tolerances and stability-oriented second-pass selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: First compute the relaxed bound \(\widehat\alpha=\min_{i:d_i>0}((x_B)_i+\delta_i)/d_i\). Form the admissible set \(H=\{i:d_i>0,\ (x_B)_i/d_i\le\widehat\alpha\}\). In the second pass choose \(p\in\arg\max_{i\in H}|d_i|\), using a deterministic tie rule, and take the feasible step \(\alpha=\max\{0,(x_B)_p/d_p\}\). Pivot on \(d_p\). The first pass limits tolerance violation; the second favors a numerically larger pivot without exceeding the relaxed blocking interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Harris testing first computes a relaxed feasible step, then chooses the largest stable pivot among rows that block within that interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Harris Two-Pass Ratio Test

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Harris two-pass algorithm is plausible, but the rowwise-tolerance formula, admissible set, and final step convention require an authoritative, specifically located source.

children.title: Bound-Flipping Ratio Tests
children.top_down_role: Ratio tests that permit eligible nonbasic variables to move between bounds.

assumptions_latex: Variables satisfy finite or infinite bounds \(\ell\le x\le u\), and a primal or dual simplex search direction is available.
Each encountered nonbasic bound crossing can be represented by moving that variable to its opposite finite bound.
Basis feasibility is monitored with prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All accepted flips precede the final blocking pivot and preserve the maintained simplex feasibility invariant within tolerance.

notation.meaning: Set of variables accepted for bound flips.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic bounded-variable simplex formulation; solver-specific flip acceptance rules are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute and sort all positive breakpoint lengths \(\tau_r\) at which eligible nonbasic variables reach their opposite finite bounds. Initialize \(F=\varnothing\). Traverse the breakpoints, tentatively flipping each encountered variable and incrementally updating the basic values, reduced costs, and accumulated direction. Accept the flip only while the maintained feasibility test remains satisfied; otherwise designate the associated row or column as the blocker. Perform one basis pivot at the resulting step \(\tau_*\), commit the flips in \(F\), and stop with the updated bounded-variable basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound-flipping test crosses eligible finite bounds without pivoting, updates the direction after each flip, and pivots only at the final blocker.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Flipping Ratio Tests

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Bound-flipping rules differ between primal and dual implementations. The generic update, acceptance, and final-pivot claims cannot be validated without a specifically located source.

children.title: Long-Step Ratio Tests
children.top_down_role: Ratio tests supporting extended movement through multiple limiting events.

assumptions_latex: A bounded-variable simplex direction induces finitely many positive feasibility breakpoints.
The state and search direction can be updated at every crossed breakpoint.
A deterministic acceptance rule identifies the first noncrossable breakpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned step \(\tau_*\) may exceed the ordinary nearest-breakpoint step while retaining every required feasibility invariant.

notation.meaning: Ordered positive breakpoints along the piecewise search path.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Long-step simplex ratio testing along a piecewise-linear bounded-variable path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\tau=0\) and compute the ordered positive breakpoints of the current direction. Advance to the next breakpoint, update \(z(\tau)\), and recompute the remaining direction and breakpoints whenever the crossed event changes an active bound or candidate set. Continue while the event is crossable under the maintained primal or dual feasibility test. At the first noncrossable event, choose its stable pivot candidate, pivot at \(\tau_*\), and return the state containing all accepted intermediate crossings. If no blocker exists, return the corresponding unboundedness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A long-step test traverses several crossable breakpoints, updating its direction after events, before pivoting at the first true blocker.
knowledge_statements.title: Long-Step Ratio Tests

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The piecewise long-step description and especially the no-blocker unboundedness conclusion depend on the precise simplex variant and require authoritative support.

children.title: Extended-Step Applicability
children.top_down_role: Problem structures and solver regimes favoring extended-step ratio-test variants.

assumptions_latex: The LP has explicit finite bounds for every variable intended to cross from one bound to the other.
Breakpoint states and direction changes can be updated without losing the maintained primal or dual invariant.
Tolerance-aware residual checks are available after each proposed crossing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An extended step is admissible exactly when every preceding event can be processed while the maintained invariant and residual tolerances remain satisfied.

notation.meaning: Ordered events before the proposed final step.
Maintained feasibility residual after event e.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applicability criterion for bounded-variable long-step and bound-flipping implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proposed endpoint \(\tau_*>0\), let \(E(\tau_*)\) be the bound events strictly preceding it. The extended step is applicable when every \(e\in E(\tau_*)\) concerns an eligible finite-bound variable, the post-event state and direction are computable, and \(\|r_e\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\) after the update. It is inapplicable if an event requires crossing an infinite bound, destroys the maintained feasibility invariant, produces an unacceptable residual, or leaves no well-defined continuation direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extended steps apply only when each intermediate finite-bound event can be updated while preserving the relevant feasibility invariant and numerical tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Step Applicability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed applicability criterion is implementation-dependent and its claimed exactness is unsupported. A source must specify the relevant invariant, event processing, and residual test.

children.title: Crash Procedures
children.top_down_role: Heuristic initialization strategies used before simplex iterations.

assumptions_latex: The constraint matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\).
Column scaling and numerical independence tolerances are fixed.
Optional logical or slack columns are identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns either a nonsingular crash basis \(B\) or a partial basis requiring artificial completion.

notation.meaning: Scaled numerical-independence score for candidate column j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic greedy simplex crash procedure, independent of a solver-specific scoring heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(S\) with structurally valid logical columns. Repeatedly score each unselected column by sparsity, coefficient scaling, and numerical independence from \(A_S\); choose a maximizer with \(\rho_j\) above tolerance and set \(S\leftarrow S\cup\{j\}\). Stop when \(|S|=m\), returning \(B=A_S\), or when no admissible column remains, returning the partial set for artificial completion. A factorization test must confirm \(\operatorname{rank}(B)=m\); otherwise reject the last selection and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A crash procedure greedily selects sparse, well-scaled, independent columns, then factorizes them to obtain a usable basis or requests artificial completion.
knowledge_statements.title: Crash Procedures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Crash scoring and artificial-completion behavior are solver-dependent. The stated greedy procedure requires a specific authoritative source.

children.title: Initial-Basis Construction
children.top_down_role: Construction routes for a usable starting basis.

assumptions_latex: The standard-form constraints are \(Ax=b\), with \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) of row rank \(m\).
Original variables satisfy \(x\ge0\).
Zero components of \(b\) use an arbitrary sign \(s_i\in\{-1,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Phase I either constructs an original-column basis with zero artificial variables or certifies infeasibility by a positive optimum.

notation.meaning: Diagonal sign matrix with s_i matching the sign of b_i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard artificial-variable Phase-I construction for equality-form linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(s_i\) so that \(s_i b_i\ge0\), set \(D=\operatorname{diag}(s_i)\), and initialize the augmented basis with \(D\), \(x=0\), and \(a=D^{-1}b\ge0\). Solve \(\min\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}a:Ax+Da=b,\ x\ge0,\ a\ge0\}\). If the optimum is positive, declare the original system infeasible. If it is zero, pivot zero-valued artificial basics out whenever possible, delete redundant rows if necessary, and return a nonsingular basis formed from original columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phase I starts from signed artificial columns, minimizes their sum, and extracts an original-column basis exactly when the optimum is zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Initial-Basis Construction

children.title: Initial-Basis Quality
children.top_down_role: Structural and numerical quality characteristics of constructed starting bases.

assumptions_latex: A candidate nonsingular basis \(B\) has been constructed for \(Ax=b\).
The objective vector \(c\), scaling convention, and feasibility tolerances are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Smaller feasibility residuals, reduced-cost violations, conditioning, and factor density indicate a higher-quality initial basis under the stated scaling.

notation.meaning: A condition estimate for the scaled basis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic vector for comparing initial simplex bases under a fixed scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent initial-basis quality by \(Q(B)=(v_p,v_d,\widehat\kappa(B),\eta)\), where \(v_p=\|\min(x_B,0)\|_\infty\), \(v_d=\|\min(\bar c_N,0)\|_\infty\) for the minimization convention, and \(\eta=(\operatorname{nnz}(L)+\operatorname{nnz}(U))/m^2\) for a factorization \(PBQ=LU\). Bases are compared only under common scaling and tolerances. Componentwise smaller \(Q(B)\) means no worse initial feasibility, dual compatibility, conditioning estimate, or factor density; incomparable vectors require a solver-specific weighting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initial-basis quality is summarized by primal and dual violations, a conditioning estimate, and factorization density under common scaling and tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Initial-Basis Quality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagnostic vector and componentwise quality ordering are reasonable but nonstandard and solver-dependent; they need a specifically located source.

children.title: Degeneracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Simplex regimes dominated by degenerate pivots or repeated zero-length movement.

assumptions_latex: A bounded-form LP has a basic feasible solution associated with a nonsingular basis \(B\).
Basic variables are classified relative to their active lower or upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Degeneracy is present exactly when at least one basic variable is active at a bound; its multiplicity is the number of such basic variables.

notation.meaning: Active bound value for basic variable i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal degeneracy regimes for bounded-variable simplex bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a basic feasible solution, define \(D_B=\{i\in\mathcal B:(x_B)_i=\ell_i\text{ or }(x_B)_i=u_i\}\) and \(d_B=|D_B|\). The basis is nondegenerate when \(d_B=0\) and degenerate when \(d_B>0\). A pivot is degeneracy-active when its admissible primal step is zero. Along an iteration sequence, degeneracy is isolated if degeneracy-active pivots do not occur consecutively, persistent if they form a consecutive run, and high-multiplicity when \(d_B\) exceeds a declared diagnostic threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basis is degenerate when a basic variable lies on a bound; regimes distinguish isolated zero steps, persistent runs, and high multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy Regimes

children.title: Simplex Stalling
children.top_down_role: Persistent lack of useful objective or feasibility progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Stalling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational stalling criterion separated from exact cycling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A simplex run is stalled over iterations \(k,\ldots,k+w\) if at least one basis change occurs while \(|z_{k+w}-z_k|\le\varepsilon_z\). Under exact arithmetic with \(\varepsilon_z=0\), consecutive zero-step degenerate pivots give constant objective value and hence stalling. Stalling need not be cycling: cycling additionally requires repetition of a previously visited basis. With positive \(\varepsilon_z\), the criterion is diagnostic and can also detect numerically negligible nonzero progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stalling means the solver changes bases but achieves no meaningful objective progress over a chosen window; unlike cycling, it need not repeat a basis.
assumptions_latex: A simplex implementation produces feasible bases \(B^0,B^1,\ldots\) and objective values \(z_k\).
An objective-progress tolerance \(\varepsilon_z\ge0\) and window length \(w\ge1\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The run stalls on window \(k{:}k+w\) when basis changes occur but \(|z_{k+w}-z_k|\le\varepsilon_z\).

notation.meaning: Objective value at simplex iteration k.
Number of iterations in the diagnostic window.

children.title: Perturbation Controls
children.top_down_role: Perturbation mechanisms used to mitigate degenerate or stalled behavior.

assumptions_latex: A simplex LP is represented in exact arithmetic or by a symbolic lexicographic comparison.
A fixed ordering of rows and columns is available.
The reported solution is evaluated against the unperturbed LP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Lexicographic perturbation selects a unique blocking candidate and prevents repetition of a basis under consistent improving pivots.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic lexicographic right-hand-side perturbation for primal simplex anti-degeneracy control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose distinct positive integers \(r_i\) and replace \(b_i\) symbolically by \(b_i(\epsilon)=b_i+\epsilon^{r_i}\). Initialize from a basis feasible for sufficiently small \(\epsilon>0\). At each ratio test, compare candidate ratios lexicographically by their coefficient vectors in ascending powers of \(\epsilon\), choose the unique lexicographic minimum, and pivot. Stop at perturbed optimality, discard the symbolic terms, and verify feasibility and optimality for the original data. Consistent lexicographic pivoting forbids a repeated basis in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symbolic, ordered perturbations break ratio ties lexicographically, prevent repeated bases in exact arithmetic, and are removed before validating the original LP.
knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation Controls

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The symbolic perturbation construction and no-repeated-basis conclusion require an exact authoritative source specifying the perturbation ordering and lexicographic pivot rule.

children.title: Cycling Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which repeated basis behavior escalates beyond routine degeneracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Cycling Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state cycling in exact-arithmetic primal simplex iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a primal simplex method for an LP in standard form, using deterministic entering- and leaving-variable rules. Cycling occurs when the algorithm revisits an identical basis without having terminated. Such repetition can occur only through degenerate pivots: every pivot in the repeated cycle has zero step length and leaves the objective value unchanged. Consequently, if every basic feasible solution encountered is nondegenerate, no basis can repeat and the method terminates after finitely many pivots. An anti-cycling rule, such as Bland's least-index rule, restores finite termination even when degeneracy is present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simplex cycling requires a repeated basis connected by zero-length degenerate pivots. Nondegeneracy excludes cycling, while Bland's rule guarantees finite termination despite degeneracy.
assumptions_latex: The LP has finitely many bases and computations use exact arithmetic.
Pivot selection is deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A repeated basis requires degeneracy; nondegenerate simplex paths and Bland-rule paths cannot cycle.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the assertion that every pivot in a repeated cycle has zero step length requires a pivot rule that excludes positive zero-reduced-cost pivots. Nondegeneracy alone does not establish the stated result for arbitrary deterministic entering rules. An authoritative cycling theorem with precise pivot assumptions is required.

children.title: Feasible Starting Points
children.top_down_role: Starting-point architectures requiring initial feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Starting Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly feasible primal-dual initialization for a standard-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), with \(n\geq1\). For the primal-dual pair \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\), a feasible interior starting point is a triple \((x^0,y^0,s^0)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ax^0=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y^0+s^0=c\), \(x^0>0\), and \(s^0>0\), where the inequalities are componentwise. Defining \(r_p^0=Ax^0-b\), \(r_d^0=A^{\mathsf T}y^0+s^0-c\), and \(\mu_0=(x^0)^{\mathsf T}s^0/n\), one has \(r_p^0=0\), \(r_d^0=0\), and \(\mu_0>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible interior start satisfies both primal and dual equalities and has strictly positive primal variables and dual slacks; its initial feasibility residuals vanish.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(n\geq1\).
The primal-dual pair admits a strictly feasible triple.

children.title: Infeasible Starting Points
children.top_down_role: Starting-point architectures permitting initial primal or dual infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Starting Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive but equality-infeasible initialization for infeasible-start primal-dual methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). For the primal-dual pair \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\), an infeasible interior starting point is a triple \((x^0,y^0,s^0)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(x^0>0\) and \(s^0>0\), but having at least one nonzero equality residual: \(r_p^0=Ax^0-b\neq0\) or \(r_d^0=A^{\mathsf T}y^0+s^0-c\neq0\). An infeasible-start primal-dual method permits these residuals while choosing step lengths that preserve \(x>0\) and \(s>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible interior start has positive primal variables and dual slacks but violates at least one primal or dual equality.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).

children.title: Embedding-Based Starting Points
children.top_down_role: Starting points organized through homogeneous or self-dual embedding structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Embedding-Based Starting Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization through an augmented homogeneous embedding of the LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An embedding-based starting point is an explicitly constructible strictly interior point \(z^0\) of an augmented primal-dual system \(F(z)=0\), where \(z\) contains the original variables \((x,y,s)\) and additional nonnegative homogenizing variables, commonly \((\tau,\kappa)\). The embedding is chosen so that \(z^0\) is available without a feasible point of the original LP, and any limiting solution with \(\tau>0\) yields an original primal-dual solution after scaling by \(\tau\); a limit with \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\) instead yields an infeasibility or unboundedness certificate under the embedding's normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An augmented homogeneous system supplies a known interior start without original feasibility and later recovers either a scaled solution or a status certificate.
assumptions_latex: The selected homogeneous embedding preserves the original primal-dual solution and certificate alternatives.
The augmented variables are initialized strictly inside their nonnegative cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau>0\) permits solution recovery by scaling, whereas \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\) identifies a certificate branch.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Homogeneous self-dual and related embeddings use different augmented equations, normalizations, and certificate alternatives. Without selecting and citing an exact embedding, the claims involving F, tau, kappa, and certificate recovery cannot be checked reliably.

knowledge_statements.title: Mehrotra Predictor–Corrector Implementations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard infeasible-start Mehrotra predictor-corrector iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an iterate \((x,y,s)\) with \(x,s>0\), set \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\). Solve the primal-dual Newton system with zero centering to obtain the affine direction \((\Delta x^{\rm aff},\Delta y^{\rm aff},\Delta s^{\rm aff})\). Compute maximal positivity-preserving affine steps and the resulting \(\mu_{\rm aff}\), then choose \(\sigma=(\mu_{\rm aff}/\mu)^3\). Reusing the same Newton matrix, solve a corrector system whose complementarity right-hand side includes \(\sigma\mu e-\Delta X^{\rm aff}\Delta S^{\rm aff}e\), with signs adjusted consistently to the chosen residual convention. Combine the predictor and corrector directions, choose fraction-to-boundary primal and dual steps, and update the iterate. Repeat these iterations until the prescribed scaled primal-residual, dual-residual, and complementarity tolerances are met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mehrotra's method repeatedly uses an affine predictor to select centering, adds a second-order corrector, and advances with positivity-preserving primal and dual steps until the stopping tests hold.
assumptions_latex: The Newton systems are solvable after any required rank treatment or regularization.
The current iterate satisfies \(x>0\) and \(s>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration produces a positivity-preserving updated iterate; the algorithm terminates only when its prescribed residual and complementarity tests hold.

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrices formed from x and s
Diagonal matrices formed from the affine primal and slack directions
Complementarity predicted by the affine step

children.title: Centrality Control
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms governing proximity to the central path.

knowledge_statements.title: Centrality Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise neighborhood condition around the primal-dual central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an interior primal-dual iterate with \(x,s>0\), define \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\). Given \(0<\theta<1\), the iterate satisfies the componentwise centrality condition when \(\lVert XSe-\mu e\rVert_\infty\leq\theta\mu\). Equivalently, every complementarity product obeys \((1-\theta)\mu\leq x_i s_i\leq(1+\theta)\mu\). A path-control implementation accepts a candidate step only if its updated variables remain positive and satisfy the selected neighborhood bound; otherwise it shortens the step or increases centering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Centrality control keeps every complementarity product near their average, shortening or recentering a step when the prescribed neighborhood would be violated.
assumptions_latex: \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert XSe-\mu e\rVert_\infty\leq\theta\mu\), equivalently \((1-\theta)\mu\leq x_i s_i\leq(1+\theta)\mu\) for every \(i\).

source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

source_witnesses.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

children.title: Barrier-Target Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection regimes for the barrier or complementarity target.

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier-Target Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection of the next complementarity target in a primal-dual Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an interior iterate, compute \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\). Choose a centering factor \(\sigma\in[0,1]\) and set the next barrier target to \(\mu_{\rm tar}=\sigma\mu\). In a predictor-corrector implementation, first compute an affine-scaling direction, its positivity-limited steps, and the predicted complementarity \(\mu_{\rm aff}\); then set \(\sigma=\min\{1,(\mu_{\rm aff}/\mu)^p\}\), typically with \(p=3\). Use \(XSe-\mu_{\rm tar}e\), together with any second-order correction, as the complementarity residual in the centered Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The next barrier target is a fraction of current complementarity, often selected adaptively from the affine predictor's expected reduction.
assumptions_latex: The current iterate satisfies \(x,s>0\).
The affine predictor supplies a nonnegative predicted complementarity \(\mu_{\rm aff}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu_{\rm tar}=\sigma\mu\) with \(0\leq\sigma\leq1\).

notation.meaning: Target complementarity for the centered step

children.title: Interior-Point Step Control
children.top_down_role: Safeguards and acceptance regimes governing interior-point step lengths.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Step Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fraction-to-boundary control for primal and dual interior-point steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x,s>0\), a search direction \((\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\), and \(\eta\in(0,1)\), define \(\beta_p=\min_{\Delta x_i<0}(-x_i/\Delta x_i)\) and \(\beta_d=\min_{\Delta s_i<0}(-s_i/\Delta s_i)\), interpreting an empty minimum as \(+\infty\). Set \(\alpha_p=\min\{1,\eta\beta_p\}\) and \(\alpha_d=\min\{1,\eta\beta_d\}\), then update \(x^+=x+\alpha_p\Delta x\), \(y^+=y+\alpha_d\Delta y\), and \(s^+=s+\alpha_d\Delta s\). Backtracking may further shorten the steps to enforce specified residual or centrality acceptance tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fraction-to-boundary control takes a full step when it remains safely interior and otherwise stays a fixed fraction short of the first primal or dual positivity boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\).
\((\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\) is a conformable search direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The controlled update satisfies \(x^+>0\) and \(s^+>0\).

notation.meaning: Raw primal and dual distances to the positivity boundary

source_refs.locator: Moving to a Solution from an Interior Point p. 55

source_witnesses.locator: Moving to a Solution from an Interior Point p. 55

children.title: Interior-Point Regularization
children.top_down_role: Regularization choices for ill-conditioned or singular interior-point systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal regularization of the reduced primal-dual Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After eliminating the complementarity direction, a primal-dual Newton equation may be represented as \(K(\Delta x,\Delta y)^{\mathsf T}=r\), where \(K=\begin{bmatrix}-D^{-1}&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(D=XS^{-1}>0\). Diagonal primal-dual regularization replaces this matrix by \(K_{\delta,\gamma}=\begin{bmatrix}-(D^{-1}+\delta I)&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&\gamma I\end{bmatrix}\), with \(\delta,
\gamma>0\). The added terms improve numerical definiteness and control near-null directions, but the computed direction solves a perturbed Newton equation; implementations must therefore monitor the unregularized residual \(r-K(\Delta x,\Delta y)^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal regularization stabilizes a reduced Newton system by shifting primal and dual blocks, while requiring monitoring of residuals for the original unregularized equations.
assumptions_latex: \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\), so \(D=XS^{-1}\) is positive diagonal.
\(\delta>0\) and \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The direction solves the shifted system \(K_{\delta,\gamma}d=r\), and its original-system defect is \(r-Kd\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind is plausible, but the precise shifted KKT blocks, signs, residual convention, and claimed numerical effects require an authoritative regularization source. No citation is supplied.

children.title: Rank Management
children.top_down_role: Detection and handling of deficient or changing numerical rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical detection and removal of redundant LP equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and a rank tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\rm rank}>0\), compute a rank-revealing QR factorization or singular-value decomposition and estimate \(r=\operatorname{rank}_{\varepsilon_{\rm rank}}(A)\). Select \(r\) independent rows, forming \(\widehat A\) and \(\widehat b\). Before deleting dependent rows, verify that every discarded equation is consistent with the selected equations to the prescribed feasibility tolerance. Solve the reduced system \(\widehat A x=\widehat b\), while evaluating final residuals against the original equation \(Ax=b\). If consistency fails, report primal infeasibility rather than silently reducing the row set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank management identifies independent equality constraints, removes only consistent redundancies, and validates the final solution against the original system.
assumptions_latex: A rank-revealing factorization is available.
Rank and consistency tolerances are fixed before row deletion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistent deletion preserves \(\{x:Ax=b\}=\{x:\widehat A x=\widehat b\}\); inconsistent dependence signals infeasibility.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but tolerance-based numerical dependence and approximate consistency do not imply the exact equality of feasible sets stated in the conclusion. A sourced formulation must distinguish exact redundancy from tolerance-based preprocessing decisions.

children.title: Regularization–Rank Interactions
children.top_down_role: Effects of regularization choices on rank detection and linear-system reliability.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularization–Rank Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of constraint rank and diagonal shifts on normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be positive diagonal. The primal-dual normal-equations matrix \(H=ADA^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv=\lVert D^{1/2}A^{\mathsf T}v\rVert_2^2\), so \(\ker H=\ker A^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(H)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\). Hence row-rank deficiency of \(A\) makes \(H\) singular regardless of positive diagonal scaling. For any \(\gamma>0\), the regularized matrix \(H_\gamma=ADA^{\mathsf T}+\gamma I\) is positive definite, but its solution is biased relative to the unregularized equations. Rank reduction removes exact null directions; regularization controls remaining numerical near-null directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive scaling cannot repair deficient constraint rank. A diagonal shift makes normal equations positive definite but perturbs them, whereas rank reduction removes exact dependencies.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
\(D\) is positive diagonal and \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker(ADA^{\mathsf T})=\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\), while \(ADA^{\mathsf T}+\gamma I\succ0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits and the kernel, rank, and positive-definiteness identities are mathematically correct for positive diagonal D. However, no evidence is supplied for this nontrivial knowledge record or for its implementation-level interpretation of rank reduction and regularization.

children.title: Barrier Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Barrier regimes with effectively arrested residual or complementarity improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed diagnostic for loss of complementarity progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu_k=(x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k/n>0\) be the complementarity measure at iteration \(k\). For a window length \(w\geq1\), required relative decrease \(\rho\in(0,1)\), and feasibility tolerance \(\varepsilon_f\), declare barrier stagnation at iteration \(k\geq w\) when \(\mu_k>(1-\rho)\mu_{k-w}\) while \(\max\{\lVert r_p^k\rVert,\lVert r_d^k\rVert\}\leq\varepsilon_f\), and the solver has not met its complementarity termination tolerance. This is an implementation diagnostic rather than an intrinsic LP property; its classification depends explicitly on \(w\), \(\rho\), scaling, norms, and tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier stagnation is flagged when complementarity fails to decrease sufficiently over a fixed window despite acceptable feasibility and unmet optimality tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(x^j,s^j>0\) for the monitored iterates.
\(w\), \(\rho\), residual scaling, and tolerances are fixed.
