knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Barrier stagnation holds when \(\mu_k>(1-\rho)\mu_{k-w}\), feasibility is acceptable, and complementarity termination has not occurred.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is appropriate for a diagnostic leaf, and the proposed rule is internally coherent. It is nevertheless a particular implementation-defined stagnation test rather than a canonical mathematical definition; a solver-diagnostics source or an explicitly documented local specification is required.

children.title: Barrier Slow Progress
children.top_down_role: Barrier regimes with sustained but operationally inadequate improvement.

assumptions_latex: The interior-point iterates satisfy \(x^k>0\), \(s^k>0\), and \(\mu_k=(x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k/n\).
Diagnostic constants satisfy \(0<\underline q<\overline q<1\), \(W\in\mathbb N\), and \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The window is classified as slow progress rather than stagnation when \(\Phi_{k+W}<\Phi_k\) but \(\underline q<\Phi_{k+W}/\Phi_k\leq\overline q\).

notation.meaning: combined primal, dual, and complementarity merit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed diagnostic for a primal-dual logarithmic-barrier iteration.

source_refs.locator: II The Logarithmic Barrier Approach p. 85
source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For residuals \(r_p^k=Ax^k-b\) and \(r_d^k=A^{\mathsf T}y^k+s^k-c\), define \(\Phi_k=\max\{\|r_p^k\|/(1+\|b\|),\|r_d^k\|/(1+\|c\|),\mu_k/(1+|c^{\mathsf T}x^k|)\}\). A completed window \([k,k+W]\) exhibits barrier slow progress when \(\Phi_{k+W}<\Phi_k\), \(\underline q<\Phi_{k+W}/\Phi_k\leq\overline q\), and \(\Phi_{k+W}>\tau\). Thus measurable improvement remains, but its contraction is insufficient for the configured progress target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier progress is slow when a window reduces the combined residual merit, remains above tolerance, and contracts by less than the configured target.
knowledge_statements.title: Barrier Slow Progress

source_witnesses.locator: II The Logarithmic Barrier Approach p. 85
source_witnesses.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited barrier chapter does not establish this particular combined merit, window ratio, tolerance, or slow-progress classification. A solver-diagnostics source or explicit documented policy is required.

children.title: Progress-Loss Classification
children.top_down_role: Evidence used to distinguish slow convergence from effective stagnation.

assumptions_latex: A positive diagnostic merit sequence \((\Phi_k)\), tolerance \(\tau>0\), window \(W\), and thresholds \(0<\underline q<\overline q<1\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every completed window receives exactly one label: converged, normal, slow, or stagnant.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mutually exclusive window classification for barrier-engine diagnostics.

source_refs.locator: 5.3 The primal logarithmic barrier function p. 90
source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At the end of window \([k,k+W]\), first return converged if \(\Phi_{k+W}\leq\tau\). Otherwise set \(q_k=\Phi_{k+W}/\Phi_k\). Return normal if \(q_k\leq\underline q\), slow if \(\underline q<q_k\leq\overline q\), and stagnant if \(q_k>\overline q\). The ordered tests make the labels disjoint and exhaustive for \(\Phi_k>0\); implementations may require the same nonconverged label on several consecutive windows before changing solver policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify each barrier window by tolerance and merit contraction into converged, normal progress, slow progress, or stagnation.
knowledge_statements.title: Progress-Loss Classification

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 The primal logarithmic barrier function p. 90
source_witnesses.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic kind fits the classification leaf, but the cited logarithmic-barrier section does not support the four-label window classifier or its thresholds.

assumptions_latex: The LP operator is \(Kx=Ax\) with sparse \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
The first-order method requires only products by \(A\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\), plus vector operations and proximal projections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One iteration can be implemented without factorization or explicit normal equations, using \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(A)+m+n)\) arithmetic and \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(A)+m+n)\) stored scalars.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration storage and arithmetic for sparse matrix-free first-order LP updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Store \(A\) once in a sparse format supporting kernels \(u\mapsto Au\) and \(v\mapsto A^{\mathsf T}v\). If an iteration performs at most \(p\) forward products and \(q\) transpose products, where \(p,q\) are constants independent of \(m,n\), then its operator cost is \(O((p+q)\operatorname{nnz}(A))\), its remaining vector cost is \(O(m+n)\), and its storage is \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(A)+m+n)\). No matrix factorization or explicit formation of \(A^{\mathsf T}A\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse first-order LP iterations need only matrix-vector kernels, linear auxiliary storage, and work proportional to the stored nonzeros.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Sparse Kernels

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated bound is plausible under the explicit constant-product assumptions, but the broad implementation chapter does not inspectably support this matrix-free first-order LP complexity claim.

children.title: Diagonal Preconditioning
children.top_down_role: Diagonal preconditioner choices for first-order LP iterations.

assumptions_latex: The saddle operator contains \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
Diagonal matrices \(T\succ0\) and \(S\succ0\) are chosen so that \(\|S^{1/2}AT^{1/2}\|_2<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The preconditioned primal-dual metric is positive definite and yields a well-defined diagonally scaled first-order update.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral admissibility condition for diagonal primal-dual preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For diagonal \(T=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\succ0\) and \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_m)\succ0\), diagonal preconditioning is admissible when \(\rho=\|S^{1/2}AT^{1/2}\|_2<1\). Equivalently, the symmetric block metric \(M=\begin{pmatrix}T^{-1}&-A^{\mathsf T}\\-A&S^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\) is positive definite. The diagonal entries define coordinatewise primal and dual steps while preserving the coupling stability condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal primal and dual steps are admissible when the norm of the correspondingly scaled constraint operator is below one.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Preconditioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral condition and Schur-complement equivalence are standard, and the condition kind fits the leaf, but no source is supplied for this primal-dual preconditioning formulation.

children.title: Iterative Rescaling
children.top_down_role: Rescaling policies applied during first-order solver execution.

assumptions_latex: The matrix \(A\) has no zero row or column on the subsystem being equilibrated.
A floor \(\delta>0\) and termination tolerance \(\varepsilon_{m eq}>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns positive diagonal scalings and a scaled matrix whose row and column norm imbalance is at most the requested tolerance when the stopping test succeeds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating row-column norm equilibration with safeguarded positive updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(D_r=I_m\), \(D_c=I_n\), and \(B=A\). At sweep \(k\), compute \(r_i=\max\{\|B_{i:}\|_2,\delta\}^{-1/2}\) and \(c_j=\max\{\|B_{:j}\|_2,\delta\}^{-1/2}\). Update \(D_r\leftarrow\operatorname{diag}(r)D_r\), \(D_c\leftarrow D_c\operatorname{diag}(c)\), and \(B\leftarrow\operatorname{diag}(r)B\operatorname{diag}(c)\). Stop when the maximum logarithmic deviation of all nonzero row and column norms from one is at most \(\varepsilon_{m eq}\), or at a prescribed sweep limit; output \((D_r,D_c,B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly normalize row and column norms, accumulate the diagonal scalings, and stop when norm imbalance is sufficiently small.
knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Rescaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a specific simultaneous row-column rescaling algorithm whose update exponents and convergence behavior depend on the equilibration variant. An authoritative algorithm source is required.

children.title: Preconditioner–Scaling Interactions
children.top_down_role: Compatibility and performance effects between diagonal preconditioners and scaling policies.

assumptions_latex: The original LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\).
Positive diagonal variable and constraint scalings \(D_c\) and \(D_r\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Preconditioning the scaled operator must be transformed with the scaling maps; otherwise steps in original coordinates differ from the intended metric.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-consistent transformation of scaling and diagonal preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(x=D_c\widehat x\) and left constraint scaling by \(D_r\), the scaled operator is \(\widehat A=D_rAD_c\). If scaled-coordinate increments use diagonal metrics \(\widehat T\) and \(\widehat S\), then the corresponding original-coordinate metrics are \(T=D_c\widehat T D_c\) for primal increments and \(S=D_r\widehat S D_r\) for dual increments under \(\widehat y=D_r^{-1}y\). Hence admissibility must be tested on \(\widehat S^{1/2}\widehat A\widehat T^{1/2}\), not on independently chosen untransformed diagonals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row and column scaling change the coordinate metric, so diagonal preconditioners must be transformed consistently with the scaled LP variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner–Scaling Interactions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinate transformations depend on the precise primal-dual update and metric convention. No source is supplied to validate the asserted transformations and admissibility test.

assumptions_latex: A first-order fixed-point map \(T_\eta\) is available for every trial stepsize \(\eta>0\).
A nonnegative merit \(\Phi\), constants \(0<\beta_-<1<\beta_+\), and acceptance parameter \(\sigma>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted step satisfies the configured sufficient-decrease inequality; failure after finitely many trials returns a stepsize diagnostic rather than an unchecked iterate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Merit-based safeguarded stepsize controller for a first-order LP map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((z_k,\eta_k)\), set the first trial \(\eta=\min\{\eta_{\max},\beta_+\eta_k\}\). Compute \(z^+=T_\eta(z_k)\) and \(R_\eta(z_k)=(z_k-z^+)/\eta\). Accept when \(\Phi(z^+)\leq\Phi(z_k)-\sigma\eta\|R_\eta(z_k)\|^2\); otherwise replace \(\eta\leftarrow\beta_-\eta\) and retry. Stop with \(z_{k+1}=z^+\) and \(\eta_{k+1}=\eta\) at acceptance, or report stepsize failure after a prescribed number of trials or when \(\eta<\eta_{\min}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the trial stepsize cautiously, backtrack until a sufficient merit decrease occurs, and report failure if safeguards are exhausted.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Stepsize Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the sufficient-decrease rule is not valid for an arbitrary fixed-point family without additional regularity assumptions. A source specifying the method and hypotheses is required.

assumptions_latex: A first-order method generates states \(z_k\) and a nonnegative normalized merit \(\Phi_k=\Phi(z_k)\).
A checkpoint \(\bar z\), factor \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), window \(W\), and restart limit are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every restart resets algorithmic memory at a selected state while preserving the best checkpoint merit observed by the controller.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified controller for scheduled, sufficient-progress, and stagnation-triggered restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\bar z=z_0\), \(\bar\Phi=\Phi(z_0)\), and \(\ell=0\). After each base-method step, increment \(\ell\). Trigger a restart if a scheduled epoch ends, if \(\Phi_k\leq\gamma\bar\Phi\), or if \(\ell\geq W\) and \(\min_{k-W<j\leq k}\Phi_j>\gamma\bar\Phi\). At a trigger, choose the lowest-merit state since the checkpoint, reset momentum and averaged-state memory there, set it as \(\bar z\), update \(\bar\Phi\), and set \(\ell=0\). Stop at solver tolerance or the restart limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart on a schedule, sufficient merit reduction, or failed window progress, resetting momentum at the best recent state.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Restart Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record combines scheduled, sufficient-progress, and stagnation triggers into a particular controller without a source establishing that family or its checkpoint-preservation behavior.

children.title: Feasibility Polishing
children.top_down_role: Postprocessing focused on reducing primal or dual feasibility defects.

assumptions_latex: The LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\).
An approximate solution \(\widetilde x\) and a candidate free index set \(F\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output minimizes primal equality violation over the selected face and is exactly primal feasible whenever the restricted system admits a nonnegative solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-feasibility correction on a face inferred from an approximate LP solution.

source_refs.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(x^+_{F^c}=0\) and solve \(x_F^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\geq0}\|A_Fu-b\|_2^2\), optionally using \(\widetilde x_F\) to break ties by minimum correction norm. Return \(x^+\) only if its normalized primal residual is no larger than that of \(\widetilde x\); otherwise retain \(\widetilde x\). If some \(u\geq0\) satisfies \(A_Fu=b\), then the subproblem attains zero residual and the returned candidate is primal feasible on the selected face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project onto a guessed nonnegative face to reduce equality violation, accepting the correction only when primal feasibility improves.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Polishing

source_witnesses.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited optimality-conditions section does not support the proposed nonnegative least-squares polishing routine. Moreover, if the routine retains the original approximate point, the output need not minimize violation over the selected face as claimed in conclusion_latex.

children.title: Optimality Polishing
children.top_down_role: Postprocessing focused on improving objective or complementarity quality.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual LP conditions are \(Ax=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(x,s\geq0\), and \(x_i s_i=0\).
A candidate support \(F\) and its complement \(F^c\) are inferred from an approximate solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A zero-residual polished solution satisfies primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity, and is therefore LP-optimal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality polishing and certification on an inferred complementary active set.

source_refs.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Impose \(x^+_{F^c}=0\) and \(s^+_F=0\), and compute nonnegative \(x_F^+\), \(s_{F^c}^+\), and \(y^+\) minimizing \(\|R\|_2\), where \(R=(Ax^+-b,\ A^{\mathsf T}y^++s^+-c)\). The imposed zeros give \((x^+)^{\mathsf T}s^+=0\). If \(R=0\), then \((x^+,y^+,s^+)\) is a directly checkable primal-dual optimality certificate; with nonzero \(R\), accept it only if the configured feasibility and gap merit improves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the KKT equations on a guessed complementary support; zero residual and nonnegativity provide a directly checkable optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Polishing

source_witnesses.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-residual KKT certificate is standard, but the exact leaf is Optimality Polishing and the statement primarily specifies a polishing algorithm. The cited section supports KKT optimality, not the inferred-support residual-minimization routine or acceptance policy.

children.title: Polishing-Goal Selection
children.top_down_role: Regimes determining which solution-quality deficit receives polishing priority.

assumptions_latex: Normalized primal infeasibility \(p\), dual infeasibility \(d\), and relative gap \(g\) are available for an approximate primal-dual point.
Tolerances \(\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_g>0\) and deterministic tie-breaking priorities are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule selects feasibility, optimality, or no polishing from the residuals that still violate their requested tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-driven dispatch between feasibility and optimality polishing goals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(v_p=p/\tau_p\) and \(v_o=\max\{d/\tau_d,g/\tau_g\}\). If \(v_p\leq1\) and \(v_o\leq1\), select no polishing. If \(v_p>v_o\), select feasibility polishing; otherwise select optimality polishing. Run the selected routine and accept its output only if it does not worsen any already satisfied tolerance and strictly decreases the selected violation score. Resolve equality \(v_p=v_o>1\) by the fixed priority, so the selection is deterministic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare normalized primal, dual, and gap violations, polish the dominant unmet goal, and reject corrections that damage already satisfied tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Polishing-Goal Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This deterministic residual-driven dispatch rule is a solver policy rather than a standard LP consequence. It requires a source or documented implementation specification.

children.title: Slow Accuracy Tail
children.top_down_role: Late-stage regimes where additional accuracy becomes disproportionately costly.

assumptions_latex: A first-order LP method produces a positive normalized error sequence \((E_k)\).
Constants \(0<\underline q<\overline q<1\), window \(W\in\mathbb N\), and tolerance \(\tau>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A slow accuracy tail has persistent but subtarget error reduction; it is distinct from stagnation because every classified window still contracts.

notation.meaning: number of consecutive slow windows required

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed diagnostic separating a contracting accuracy tail from first-order stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_k=\max\{p_k,d_k,g_k\}\), where the three terms are normalized primal infeasibility, dual infeasibility, and gap. Define \(q_k=E_{k+W}/E_k\). The run has a slow accuracy tail at iteration \(k+JW\) when \(E_{k+jW}>\tau\) and \(\underline q<q_{k+(j-1)W}\leq\overline q\) for every \(j=1,\ldots,J\). Thus each window reduces error, but no window reaches the normal-progress contraction threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slow accuracy tail consists of consecutive above-tolerance windows that keep reducing error, but never at the target contraction rate.
knowledge_statements.title: Slow Accuracy Tail

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the progress-loss leaf, but the combined error, consecutive-window definition, and policy thresholds have no supporting source.

children.title: First-Order Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Regimes with negligible useful improvement across continued iterations.

assumptions_latex: \(M_j>0\) is recorded at every completed iteration \(j\).
\(w\in\mathbb{N}\), \(w\ge 1\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(0<\eta_{\mathrm{stag}}<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Stag}(k)=1\).

notation.meaning: maximum normalized primal residual, dual residual, and duality gap at iteration k
largest accepted average logarithmic improvement under stagnation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: stagnation is operationally defined by persistently inadequate reduction of a normalized optimality merit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational finite-window stagnation test for a first-order LP iteration log.

source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a completed iteration \(k\ge w\), define the average logarithmic progress over the last \(w\) iterations by \[P_{k,w}=\frac{1}{w}\log\!\left(\frac{M_{k-w}}{M_k}\right).\] Define the finite-window stagnation indicator by \[\operatorname{Stag}(k)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad M_k>\varepsilon\quad\text{and}\quad P_{k,w}\le\eta_{\mathrm{stag}},\] and set \(\operatorname{Stag}(k)=0\) otherwise. The diagnosis concerns failure to reduce the monitored optimality merit sufficiently over a declared finite window; it does not by itself assert infeasibility, unboundedness, or nonconvergence of the exact-arithmetic algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagnation is flagged when the normalized residual-gap merit remains above tolerance and its average logarithmic improvement over a fixed window is too small.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Stagnation

source_witnesses.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

children.title: Tail–Stagnation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic evidence separating costly residual progress from effective stagnation.

assumptions_latex: \(w\in\mathbb{N}\), \(w\ge1\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(0<\delta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_{k,w}=1-\delta\) is the tail–stagnation boundary.

notation.meaning: normalized residual-gap merit at iteration k
observed geometric contraction factor over w iterations

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the boundary is a declared diagnostic threshold on observed contraction, not a universal convergence constant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational boundary separating continued slow contraction from finite-window stagnation.

source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the observed geometric contraction factor by \[q_{k,w}=\left(\frac{M_k}{M_{k-w}}\right)^{1/w}.\] While \(M_k>\varepsilon\), classify the window as a slow accuracy tail when \(q_{k,w}<1-\delta\), and as stagnating when \(q_{k,w}>1-\delta\). The diagnostic boundary is \[q_{k,w}=1-\delta.\] Values on this boundary are assigned by a documented tie rule. The classification is relative to \(w\), \(\delta\), the normalization defining \(M_k\), and the requested tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The boundary occurs when the observed geometric contraction equals the declared minimum material contraction; better contraction is a slow tail, while worse contraction is stagnation.
knowledge_statements.title: Tail–Stagnation Boundary

source_witnesses.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

children.title: Solver Diagnostic Evidence Architecture
children.top_down_role: Evidence used to isolate modeling, transformation, numerical, method, and resource failures and to compare configurations reproducibly.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Does My Model Have Numerical Issues?

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Benchmarking Optimization Software with Performance Profiles
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Benchmarking Optimization Software with Performance Profiles

children.title: Presolve Log Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Log evidence concerning reductions, eliminations, substitutions, or presolve termination.

assumptions_latex: The presolver records original and reduced dimensions and every reversible transformation.
All reported counts are nonnegative integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed count, replay, and postsolve checks provide an internal-consistency certificate for the presolve log.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: count conservation and transformation replay are directly checkable presolve-log invariants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Internal-consistency certificate for a reversible LP presolve log.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_m\) and \(r_n\) be the logged numbers of removed constraints and variables. The following checks provide an internal-consistency certificate for a presolve log: \[m_p=m_0-r_m,\qquad n_p=n_0-r_n,\] every element of \(\mathcal{T}\) has valid input indices at the time it is applied, and replaying \(\mathcal{T}\) from the original model reproduces the logged reduced model. If postsolve is claimed, applying the recorded inverse transformations to a reduced solution must reconstruct an original-space vector satisfying the logged substitution identities. These checks certify the stated aspects of log coherence, not preservation of feasibility or optimality unless each transformation is separately validated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolve log passes these coherence checks when removal counts match reduced dimensions, transformations replay correctly, and claimed postsolve inverses reconstruct the recorded substitutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Log Diagnostics

children.title: Scaling Log Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Log evidence concerning scaling choices and reported coefficient improvement.

assumptions_latex: Positive diagonal row and column scalings \(D_r,D_c\) are logged.
Each matrix whose dynamic range is evaluated has at least one nonzero entry.
Dynamic ranges are computed only over nonzero matrix entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaling warning predicate satisfies \(\mathcal{W}_{\mathrm{scale}}=1\) exactly under either displayed threshold violation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scaling diagnostics compare coefficient ranges and diagonal-factor spreads using declared thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Thresholded diagnostic for the numerical effect and extremity of diagonal LP scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R(B)=\max_{B_{ij}\ne0}|B_{ij}|/\min_{B_{ij}\ne0}|B_{ij}|\) and \(\widehat A=D_rAD_c\), record \(R(A)\), \(R(\widehat A)\), and the spreads \[S_r=\frac{\max_i(D_r)_{ii}}{\min_i(D_r)_{ii}},\qquad S_c=\frac{\max_j(D_c)_{jj}}{\min_j(D_c)_{jj}}.\] Given declared thresholds \(\theta\ge1\) and \(\Gamma\ge1\), define \[\mathcal{W}_{\mathrm{scale}}=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R(\widehat A)>\frac{R(A)}{\theta}\quad\text{or}\quad \max\{S_r,S_c\}>\Gamma,\] and set \(\mathcal{W}_{\mathrm{scale}}=0\) otherwise. The first condition reports insufficient range reduction; the second reports extreme scaling that may amplify data or recovery errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling diagnostics warn when diagonal scaling fails to reduce coefficient range enough or requires row or column factors with excessive spread.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Log Diagnostics

children.title: Presolve–Scaling Interaction Signals
children.top_down_role: Log patterns linking presolve transformations to subsequent scaling behavior.

assumptions_latex: Presolve and scaling can each be run first from the same original LP.
Both execution orders report comparable reduced models and numerical metrics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_{PS}=1\) identifies an order-sensitive presolve–scaling interaction.

notation.meaning: reduced dimensions under execution order X
postprocessing coefficient range under execution order X

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: order sensitivity is observable by controlled comparison of presolve and scaling pipelines
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled order-sensitivity signal for presolve and diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For declared tolerances \(\tau_R\ge1\) and \(\tau_N\ge0\), define an interaction signal by \[I_{PS}=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad |m_{PS}-m_{SP}|+|n_{PS}-n_{SP}|>\tau_N\quad\text{or}\quad \max\!\left\{\frac{R_{PS}}{R_{SP}},\frac{R_{SP}}{R_{PS}}\right\}>\tau_R,\] with \(I_{PS}=0\) otherwise. A disagreement in detected terminal status also forces \(I_{PS}=1\). The signal establishes that the logged behavior is materially order-sensitive; it does not identify which order is mathematically or numerically preferable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interaction is flagged when reversing presolve and scaling materially changes reduced dimensions, coefficient range, or detected terminal status.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve–Scaling Interaction Signals

assumptions_latex: Each completed iteration reports primal and dual iterates and cumulative work.
Residual and objective normalizations are fixed before comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k\) is the iteration-progress diagnostic record at iteration \(k\).

notation.meaning: normalized primal residual, dual residual, and relative gap

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: residual, gap, step, objective, and work histories form the standard checkable progress interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-neutral representation of the quantities needed to interpret iterative LP progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A method-neutral iteration-progress record is \[d_k=\bigl(k,W_k,r_p^k,r_d^k,g_k,f_p^k,f_d^k,s_k\bigr),\] where \(f_p^k\) and \(f_d^k\) are the reported primal and dual objectives and \(s_k\) is a declared step or iterate-change norm. A valid diagnostic series preserves the same residual and gap normalizations for all \(k\), has nondecreasing \(W_k\), and explicitly marks unavailable components. Progress comparisons are made through histories or windowed ratios of components of \(d_k\), rather than iteration count alone, because iterations may have unequal computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteration diagnostics record normalized residuals, gap, objectives, step size, and cumulative work under fixed conventions, enabling comparable progress histories.
knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Progress Diagnostics

children.title: Factorization Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Log evidence concerning refactorization, fill, pivoting, or factorization failure.

assumptions_latex: A computed factorization is used to solve \(Kz=b\).
The residual and norm calculations use declared floating-point precision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_F=1\) denotes a factorization-quality warning.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: backward error and pivot growth are directly computable factorization diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical warning predicate for LP basis or Newton-system factorization solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the normwise backward error of a factorization solve by \[\eta_b=\frac{\|b-K\widehat z\|}{\|K\|\,\|\widehat z\|+\|b\|},\] with \(\eta_b=0\) when numerator and denominator both vanish. For declared limits \(\tau_b>0\), \(\tau_\rho>0\), and \(N_{\max}\in\mathbb{N}\), set \[W_F=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \eta_b>\tau_b\ \text{or}\ \rho>\tau_\rho\ \text{or}\ N_{\mathrm{ref}}>N_{\max},\] where \(N_{\mathrm{ref}}\) counts numerical refactorizations or failed update attempts. This warning concerns the computed linear algebra, not the LP's mathematical status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factorization diagnostics warn when solve backward error, pivot growth, or repeated refactorization exceeds declared limits.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Diagnostics

children.title: Conditioning Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Log evidence concerning ill-conditioning or numerical sensitivity.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is nonsingular in the selected norm.
A condition estimator returns \(\widehat\kappa(K)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_\kappa=1\) flags conditioning-induced loss of trustworthy digits.

notation.meaning: estimated condition number of the linear system

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: condition estimates combined with backward error bound expected forward sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition-estimate diagnostic for linear systems arising inside an LP solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\) be unit roundoff and let \(\eta_b\) be the measured relative backward error. Define the conditioning-risk score \[Q_\kappa=\widehat\kappa(K)\max\{u,\eta_b\}.\] For a declared limit \(\tau_f\in(0,1)\), issue a conditioning warning when \[W_\kappa=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Q_\kappa>\tau_f.\] A large \(\widehat\kappa(K)\) indicates sensitivity even if the factorization is backward stable, whereas a small backward error alone does not guarantee a small forward error. The estimate, norm, precision, and threshold must accompany the warning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditioning diagnostics combine an estimated condition number with rounding or backward error and warn when their product exceeds the allowed forward uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Diagnostics

children.title: Factorization–Conditioning Linkage
children.top_down_role: Patterns connecting conditioning deterioration to factorization behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(Kz=b\) has exact solution \(z\ne0\).
The computed solution \(\widehat z\) satisfies a normwise backward perturbation bounded by \(\eta_b\).
\(\kappa(K)\eta_b<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widehat z-z\|/\|z\|\le \kappa(K)\eta_b/(1-\kappa(K)\eta_b)\).

notation.meaning: condition number in the selected subordinate norm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise perturbation linkage between factorization backward error and conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the factorization solve is backward stable in the sense that \(\widehat z\) exactly solves \((K+\Delta K)\widehat z=b\) with \(\|\Delta K\|/\|K\|\le\eta_b\). If \(\kappa(K)\eta_b<1\), then its forward error obeys \[\frac{\|\widehat z-z\|}{\|z\|}\le\frac{\kappa(K)\eta_b}{1-\kappa(K)\eta_b}.\] Consequently, a small factorization residual is reliable evidence of solution accuracy only when paired with an acceptable condition estimate; large conditioning can convert a small backward error into substantial forward uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factorization backward error controls solution error only after amplification by conditioning; a small residual can coexist with large forward error for an ill-conditioned system.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization–Conditioning Linkage

children.title: Termination Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Evidence explaining why solver execution stopped.

assumptions_latex: The solver declares tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g>0\).
Normalized residuals and gap are evaluated at the returned iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful termination is valid only when \(T_{\mathrm{opt}}=1\); resource termination is recorded separately.

notation.meaning: normalized primal residual, dual residual, and relative duality gap
iteration, time, or work limit predicate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of accuracy-based successful termination from resource-based stopping.

source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the successful optimality termination predicate by \[T_{\mathrm{opt}}=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad r_p\le\varepsilon_p,
\quad r_d\le\varepsilon_d,
\quad g\le\varepsilon_g.\] Define \(T_{\mathrm{lim}}=1\) when a declared iteration, time, or work budget is exhausted. A termination diagnostic must record which predicate fired, the corresponding measured values, and whether all quantities were evaluated before or after postsolve. If \(T_{\mathrm{lim}}=1\) while \(T_{\mathrm{opt}}=0\), the run stopped without an accuracy-based success certificate and must not be reported as successfully optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Termination diagnostics distinguish meeting primal, dual, and gap tolerances from merely exhausting an iteration, time, or work budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Termination Diagnostics

source_witnesses.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

children.title: Status Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Interpretation and cross-checking of reported solver statuses.

assumptions_latex: The primal LP is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
The dual LP is \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reported status is certified only by the corresponding displayed witness checks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic witness checks for principal LP solver statuses.

source_refs.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The status \(\mathrm{OPTIMAL}\) is certified by \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), \(A^Ty+s=c\), \(s\ge0\), and \(c^Tx=b^Ty\). The status \(\mathrm{PRIMAL\_INFEASIBLE}\) is certified by a vector \(y_I\) satisfying \[A^Ty_I\ge0,
\qquad b^Ty_I<0.\] The status \(\mathrm{PRIMAL\_UNBOUNDED}\) is certified by a feasible point \(x_0\) and direction \(d\) satisfying \[Ax_0=b,
\quad x_0\ge0,
\quad Ad=0,
\quad d\ge0,
\quad c^Td<0.\] In floating-point logs, every equality and inequality requires an explicitly stated verification tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal, infeasible, and unbounded statuses require respectively a primal-dual zero-gap witness, a Farkas witness, or a feasible improving recession ray.
knowledge_statements.title: Status Diagnostics

source_witnesses.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

children.title: Solution-Quality Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Reported residual, objective, basis, or certificate quality evidence.

assumptions_latex: The primal LP is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), and its dual is \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
A returned primal-dual triple \((x,y,s)\) is available in original-model coordinates.
A vector norm is selected, and all residuals use the displayed fixed normalizations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x,y,s)\) is an independently checkable solution-quality certificate vector.

notation.meaning: normalized primal and dual nonnegativity violations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-vector certificate for assessing a returned LP solution independently of status text.

source_refs.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the stated standard-form primal-dual pair and the selected norm, define \[r_p=\frac{\|Ax-b\|}{1+\|b\|},\qquad r_d=\frac{\|A^Ty+s-c\|}{1+\|c\|},\qquad g=\frac{|c^Tx-b^Ty|}{1+|c^Tx|+|b^Ty|}.\] Define the nonnegativity violations by \[v_x=\frac{\|(-x)_+\|}{1+\|x\|},\qquad v_s=\frac{\|(-s)_+\|}{1+\|s\|}.\] The quality certificate vector is \[Q(x,y,s)=(r_p,r_d,g,v_x,v_s).\] A declared quality level is attained exactly when every component lies below its corresponding declared tolerance; solver status text alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solution quality is certified by normalized primal feasibility, dual feasibility, gap, and nonnegativity violations evaluated in original-model coordinates against declared tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Quality Diagnostics

source_witnesses.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

source_witnesses.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

children.title: Termination–Status Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency checks across stop cause, reported status, and achieved quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Termination–Status Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate-based consistency rules for standard-form maximization LP statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a solver status and its numerical evidence, call the report termination-status consistent when the evidence meets the predicate attached to that status. For the stated primal-dual pair, optimality uses approximate primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and duality-gap agreement. Primal infeasibility uses the Farkas certificate \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\), interpreted with declared tolerances. Unboundedness requires both an approximately feasible primal point \(x\) and an improving recession direction \(d\). Resource-limit and numerical-failure exits carry no mathematical solution-status conclusion unless a separate certificate is returned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A status is consistent only when its logged evidence satisfies the corresponding predicate; in particular, unboundedness requires primal feasibility as well as an improving recession direction, while limits and numerical failures alone certify no mathematical LP status.
assumptions_latex: The primal LP is \(\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\), with dual \(\min\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c\}\).
All residuals and sign tests use declared finite tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reported termination status is consistent when its accompanying evidence satisfies the corresponding predicate: \(\mathrm{OPTIMAL}\) requires \(\|Ax-b\|\le\varepsilon_p\), \(x\ge-\varepsilon_p\mathbf 1\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y-c\ge-\varepsilon_d\mathbf 1\), and \(|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|\le\varepsilon_g\); \(\mathrm{PRIMAL\_INFEASIBLE}\) requires a vector \(y\) with \(\|A^{\mathsf T}y\|\le\varepsilon_d\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<-\varepsilon_g\); \(\mathrm{UNBOUNDED}\) requires a point \(x\) satisfying \(\|Ax-b\|\le\varepsilon_p\) and \(x\ge-\varepsilon_p\mathbf 1\), together with \(d\ge-\varepsilon_p\mathbf 1\), \(\|Ad\|\le\varepsilon_p\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d>\varepsilon_g\). A limit, interruption, or numerical-failure status is not an optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness certificate.

notation.meaning: Primal and dual feasibility tolerances and the duality-gap tolerance.
Candidate primal solution, dual multiplier, and primal improving ray.

children.title: Unit Consistency Audit
children.top_down_role: Review of dimensional consistency across variables, constraints, and objective terms.

assumptions_latex: Each variable, constraint right-hand side, coefficient, and objective value has a declared physical unit.
Only nonzero coefficients are subjected to term-level dimensional tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model passes the unit consistency audit if and only if \([A_{ij}][x_j]=[b_i]\) for every \(A_{ij}\ne0\), and there exists an objective unit \(U_f\) such that \([c_j][x_j]=U_f\) for every \(c_j\ne0\). For bounds, \([\ell_j]=[u_j]=[x_j]\). Any violated equality identifies a dimensionally inconsistent term; passing these equalities does not establish favorable numerical scaling.

notation.meaning: Physical dimension or unit class of a quantity.
Coefficient matrix, right-hand side, and objective vector.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensional homogeneity of LP rows, bounds, and objective terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an LP with constraints \(Ax=b\), bounds \(\ell\le x\le u\), and objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\), assign a unit class to every modeled quantity. A row is unit-consistent when every nonzero term \(A_{ij}x_j\) has the same unit as \(b_i\). A bound is consistent when its unit equals that of its variable. The objective is consistent when all nonzero terms \(c_jx_j\) share one objective unit. The audit consists of checking these equalities symbolically rather than comparing numerical magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every term in a constraint must match its right-hand-side unit, every bound its variable, and every objective term a common objective unit.
knowledge_statements.title: Unit Consistency Audit

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the unit-consistency leaf and is internally coherent, but no inspectable source is supplied for the dimensional-homogeneity convention or its application to LP rows, bounds, and objectives.

children.title: Magnitude Distribution Audit
children.top_down_role: Review of typical numerical scales across model components.

assumptions_latex: The finite nonzero numerical data are partitioned into declared classes such as matrix, right-hand side, objective, and bounds.
A logarithm base and reporting quantile levels are fixed before inspection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each class \(S\), the audit returns \(n_S\), \(\min L(S)\), selected quantiles of \(L(S)\), \(\max L(S)\), and \(R(S)=\max L(S)-\min L(S)\), where \(L(S)=\{\log_{10}|s|:s\in S,\ s\ne0\}\). Empty classes are reported as empty, and zeros are counted separately rather than assigned a logarithm.

notation.meaning: A declared class of finite model coefficients.
Base-ten log-magnitudes of nonzero entries in a class.
Logarithmic spread of a coefficient class.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descriptive log-scale audit; it does not by itself classify a model as unstable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the finite model data into semantically distinct classes \(S\). For every class, count zeros and nonzeros, transform each nonzero magnitude to \(\log_{10}|s|\), sort the transformed values, and report the minimum, fixed quantiles, maximum, and logarithmic spread. Report positive and negative counts separately when sign is diagnostically relevant. The output retains class labels, because combining matrix, right-hand-side, objective, and bound magnitudes can conceal a problematic distribution in one class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute classwise log-magnitude counts, quantiles, extrema, and spreads, while reporting zeros separately and preserving coefficient-class labels.
knowledge_statements.title: Magnitude Distribution Audit

children.title: Unit-Driven Scaling Risks
children.top_down_role: Numerical risks caused by unit choices that induce unfavorable model scales.

assumptions_latex: A physically equivalent change of units replaces variables by \(x=D\hat x\), where \(D\) is positive diagonal.
Feasibility and optimality tests use fixed absolute and relative floating-point tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under \(x=D\hat x\), the data become \(AD\), \(D^{\mathsf T}c\), and \(D^{-1}\ell\le\hat x\le D^{-1}u\). Although the represented physical decisions are unchanged, large ratios \(\max_jD_{jj}/\min_jD_{jj}\) can enlarge coefficient ranges and make fixed numerical tolerances correspond to unequal physical errors. Therefore a unit choice is flagged as a scaling risk when it creates declared range or tolerance-amplification thresholds; this flag predicts exposure, not solver failure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between physical equivalence and numerically consequential unit scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Changing measurement units is an algebraic variable scaling: with \(x=D\hat x\), the feasible decisions correspond bijectively, but the stored coefficients and bounds change magnitude. The audit computes the induced coefficient ranges and translates solver feasibility tolerances back into the original physical units. A unit-driven scaling risk is present when the conversion produces extreme ranges or makes a common numerical tolerance represent materially different physical errors across rows or variables. Such a risk is conditional on finite precision and the solver's scaling and tolerance policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent unit choices can create extreme stored coefficients and unequal physical meanings for fixed tolerances, creating numerical risk without changing the modeled decisions.
knowledge_statements.title: Unit-Driven Scaling Risks

children.title: Coefficient-Range Audit
children.top_down_role: Review of minimum, maximum, and outlying coefficient magnitudes.

assumptions_latex: The audit receives finite LP data \(A,b,c,\ell,u\).
Zeros and infinite bound sentinels are excluded from positive-magnitude minima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each declared class \(S\in\{A,b,c,\ell,u\}\), the audit reports \(m_S=\min\{|s|:s\in S,\ 0<|s|<\infty\}\), \(M_S=\max\{|s|:s\in S,\ |s|<\infty\}\), and \(\rho_S=M_S/m_S\) when the defining set is nonempty. It also returns the indices attaining \(m_S\) and \(M_S\), zero counts, and nonfinite-data errors.

notation.meaning: Smallest and largest finite nonzero magnitudes in the class.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classwise extrema and ratios for raw LP input data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the LP input into the matrix, right-hand-side, objective, lower-bound, and upper-bound classes. Validate finiteness except for explicitly supported infinite bounds. For each class, scan all entries, count zeros, and find the smallest and largest finite nonzero absolute values and their locations. When both extrema exist, return their ratio. Do not merge classes when computing the primary ranges, because a moderate global range can obscure a problematic class and a large global range can merely reflect legitimately different data roles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report classwise smallest and largest finite nonzero magnitudes, their ratio and locations, zero counts, and invalid nonfinite entries.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Range Audit

children.title: Dynamic-Range Audit
children.top_down_role: Review of scale separation within and across model components.

assumptions_latex: Each audited class contains finite numerical entries, with structural zeros recorded separately.
The machine precision \(u>0\) and warning threshold \(\tau>1\) are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every nonempty nonzero class \(S\), define \(\rho_S=\max_{s\in S}|s|/\min_{s\in S,\,s\ne0}|s|\) and \(d_S=\log_{10}\rho_S\). The audit reports \((\rho_S,d_S,u\rho_S)\) and flags the class when \(\rho_S>\tau\) or \(u\rho_S\ge1\). These tests are scale diagnostics only: neither inequality is a necessary or sufficient condition for ill-conditioning of the complete LP.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Thresholded interpretation of coefficient ranges under finite precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dynamic-range audit converts each classwise coefficient ratio into both a multiplicative range and a decimal-order span. It additionally compares the range with machine precision through \(u\rho_S\), which measures potential loss of relative resolution in a worst-case magnitude comparison. A warning is issued according to declared thresholds, while the report explicitly distinguishes this inexpensive magnitude screen from a condition-number analysis. Zeros are excluded from the ratio because including them would make every sparse class have infinite range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure each coefficient class's multiplicative and decimal-order span, compare it with declared thresholds and machine precision, and avoid interpreting the screen as conditioning.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic-Range Audit

children.title: Coefficient-Outlier Patterns
children.top_down_role: Localized coefficient structures responsible for extreme reported ranges.

assumptions_latex: A coefficient class \(S\) has at least three finite nonzero entries.
Outlier parameters \(k>0\) and \(\delta\ge0\) are fixed before examining indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Let \(z_s=\log_{10}|s|\), \(m=\operatorname{median}_{s\in S}z_s\), and \(q=\operatorname{median}_{s\in S}|z_s-m|\). A coefficient \(s\) is a magnitude outlier when \(|z_s-m|>kq+\delta\). If \(q=0\), the additive floor \(\delta\) prevents every distinct magnitude from being classified automatically. The audit reports outlier indices, signs, values, and deviation scores, separately for each coefficient class.

notation.meaning: Base-ten logarithmic magnitude of a coefficient.
Median log-magnitude and median absolute deviation.
Multiplier and additive floor defining the audit threshold.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust classwise pattern for detecting isolated coefficient magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Within each semantic coefficient class, transform finite nonzero values to logarithmic magnitudes and compute their median and median absolute deviation. Declare an entry an outlier when its logarithmic deviation exceeds the fixed robust threshold. Preserve the original index and sign so the flagged entry can be traced to the model. This definition detects isolation relative to its class, not mathematical incorrectness; a valid structural coefficient may be an outlier, while a uniformly badly scaled class may contain none.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flag coefficients whose log-magnitudes lie beyond a fixed median-deviation threshold, preserving class, index, sign, value, and score.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Outlier Patterns

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The robust log-magnitude rule is mathematically explicit and fits the leaf, but it is a particular audit convention with no cited source. The choices of median absolute deviation, strict inequality, and additive floor require support.

children.title: Redundancy Audit
children.top_down_role: Review of duplicate or structurally implied rows, columns, and bounds.

assumptions_latex: The feasible region is \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\).
Auxiliary LPs are solved to a declared feasibility and objective tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For row \(i\), let \(P_{-i}=\{x:a_j^{\mathsf T}x\le b_j,\ j\ne i\}\) and \(v_i=\sup_{x\in P_{-i}}(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i)\). If \(P_{-i}\ne\varnothing\), row \(i\) is redundant exactly when \(v_i\le0\). The numerical audit classifies it as certified redundant when an auxiliary solve supplies a valid upper bound \(U_i\le	au\), and as nonredundant when it supplies a feasible \(x\in P_{-i}\) with \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i>\tau\). Other outcomes remain unresolved.

notation.meaning: Feasible region after deleting row i.
Maximum violation of the deleted inequality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-LP test for redundancy of inequality rows.

source_refs.locator: 5.2. Global dependence on the right-hand side vector p. 212

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Audit each inequality by deleting it and maximizing its violation over the remaining system. Exact redundancy means that the resulting supremum is nonpositive, so deleting the row does not enlarge the feasible region. In finite precision, accept redundancy only from a solver-provided valid upper bound within the declared tolerance; a merely feasible candidate objective is insufficient. A feasible point violating the deleted row certifies nonredundancy. Infeasible, unbounded, interrupted, or numerically uncertain auxiliary solves are recorded according to their certificates rather than forced into either class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete each inequality and maximize its violation; an upper bound proves redundancy, while a feasible violating point proves nonredundancy.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy Audit

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2. Global dependence on the right-hand side vector p. 212

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The auxiliary-LP criterion is mathematically sound when the reduced system is nonempty, but the cited section on global right-hand-side dependence does not clearly support this row-deletion redundancy algorithm or its certified numerical classification.

children.title: Near-Dependence Audit
children.top_down_role: Review of rows or columns exhibiting approximate linear dependence.

assumptions_latex: The audited row matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has no zero rows after declared row scaling.
A norm, row normalization, and numerical threshold \(\tau>0\) are fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Normalize each row to \(\hat a_i=a_i/\|a_i\|_2\), form \(\hat A\), and compute singular values \(\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r\), where \(r=\min(m,n)\). The audit reports \(\sigma_r\), \(\sigma_1/\sigma_r\) when \(\sigma_r>0\), and associated singular vectors. It flags near dependence when \(0<\sigma_r\le\tau\sigma_1\); \(\sigma_r=0\) denotes exact rank deficiency in exact arithmetic.

notation.meaning: Largest and smallest reported singular values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular-value screen for near linear dependence among scaled constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: First reject or separately classify zero rows, then normalize nonzero constraint rows to remove arbitrary scalar multiples. Compute a singular-value decomposition of the normalized matrix. Exact rank deficiency is indicated by a zero smallest singular value in exact arithmetic; near dependence is flagged when the smallest singular value is positive but small relative to the largest under a declared threshold. The corresponding singular vector supplies the approximate linear combination. Because the result depends on scaling, norm, threshold, and arithmetic precision, all four are included in the audit record.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize constraint rows and use the smallest relative singular value and singular vector to identify approximate linear dependence.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Dependence Audit

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and the formula is not valid for general row dependence when m>n: all m rows are then dependent, yet rank(A)=min(m,n) and the listed smallest singular value may be positive. The record needs a dimension restriction or an SVD formulation that includes the left-nullspace modes.

children.title: Redundancy–Dependence Boundary
children.top_down_role: Evidence distinguishing exact structural redundancy from numerically fragile dependence.

assumptions_latex: Constraint rows are represented by a scaled matrix \(\hat A\).
A relative numerical threshold \(\tau>0\) and arithmetic precision are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact boundary is \(\operatorname{rank}(\hat A)<\min(m,n)\), equivalently \(\sigma_r(\hat A)=0\). Numerical near dependence occupies \(0<\sigma_r(\hat A)\le\tau\sigma_1(\hat A)\), while the screened independent region is \(\sigma_r(\hat A)>\tau\sigma_1(\hat A)\). Since positive perturbations can move \(\sigma_r\) across zero or \(\tau\sigma_1\), only exact algebraic evidence establishes dependence; threshold classification establishes proximity under the stated scaling.

notation.meaning: Scaled constraint matrix with m rows and n columns.
Extreme singular values, with r equal to the smaller dimension.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rank deficiency separated from threshold-based numerical near dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Redundancy and dependence must be separated from their numerical approximations. For a scaled row matrix, exact linear dependence is the algebraic event that the smallest singular value vanishes. Near dependence is a thresholded neighborhood of that event in which the smallest singular value remains positive but is small relative to the largest. Outside that neighborhood, the selected singular-value screen reports independence, without proving that every optimization basis is well conditioned. Rescaling or changing precision can alter the near-dependence label but not exact rank in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact dependence means rank deficiency; near dependence means a positive but threshold-small relative singular value under explicitly stated scaling and precision.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy–Dependence Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank criterion rank(A)<min(m,n) does not characterize dependence among rows when m>n, and algebraic row dependence is not itself constraint redundancy because right-hand sides and inequality implication matter. An authoritative source and a corrected boundary statement are required.

children.title: Artificial-Bound Audit
children.top_down_role: Review of imposed surrogate bounds and their influence on solver behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Artificial-Bound Audit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-perturbation audit for bounds introduced as modeling surrogates for infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Identify every finite variable bound introduced solely as a surrogate for infinity. Solve the LP with the recorded bound \(M\), measure its activity, then enlarge it to \(\gamma M\), where \(\gamma>1\), and resolve under the same solver tolerances. Compare the relevant primal solution components, objective, and status. An active artificial bound or a material change after expansion indicates possible truncation of the intended feasible region. An inactive, insensitive bound passes this finite perturbation audit but does not prove that no larger bound could matter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Test artificial bounds for activity, enlarge them, and re-solve; activity or material solution change signals possible truncation of the intended model.
assumptions_latex: A finite bound \(M>0\) was introduced only to replace an intended unbounded side of a variable domain.
The model can be resolved with an expanded bound \(\gamma M\), where \(\gamma>1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solve at \(M\) and at \(\gamma M\). For each artificial upper bound, report its slack \(s_j(M)=M-x_j(M)\), activity test \(s_j(M)\le\tau_M\), and changes \(|x_j(\gamma M)-x_j(M)|\) and \(|z(\gamma M)-z(M)|\). The audit passes only when the bound is inactive by the declared tolerance and the expanded-bound solve preserves the relevant solution and objective within declared tolerances. Activity, material change, or an uncertified re-solve is flagged; passing is sensitivity evidence, not proof for all larger bounds.

notation.meaning: Artificial bound and its expansion factor.
Solution and objective obtained with bound M.
Declared activity tolerance for the artificial bound.

children.title: Penalty-Coefficient Audit
children.top_down_role: Review of penalty magnitudes and their numerical or modeling influence.

assumptions_latex: The penalized LP minimizes \(f(x)+M\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}v\) over a polyhedron with violation variables \(v\ge0\).
A continuation factor \(\gamma>1\) and comparison tolerances are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solve the model at penalties \(M\) and \(\gamma M\), recording \(v(M)\), \(v(\gamma M)\), the unpenalized values \(f(x(M))\), \(f(x(\gamma M))\), and statuses. The penalty is empirically adequate only if both solves satisfy \(\|v\|\le\tau_v\) and their unpenalized decisions and values agree within declared tolerances. It is flagged as too small when material violation persists or decreases materially after multiplication; it is flagged as dominance-risk when penalty terms exceed a declared magnitude ratio or the enlarged solve loses numerical reliability.

notation.meaning: Positive penalty coefficient and continuation multiplier.
Nonnegative vector of penalized violations or artificial variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuation audit balancing penalty adequacy against numerical dominance.

source_refs.locator: 4.5 The Single Artificial Variable Technique p. 173

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Separate the genuine objective from terms introduced to penalize violations or artificial variables. Solve at the recorded penalty, multiply the penalty by a fixed factor, and resolve. Compare violations, unpenalized objectives, decisions, statuses, and coefficient ranges. Persistent violations or material improvement after increasing the penalty indicates inadequate enforcement. Conversely, a penalty whose terms dominate ordinary objective coefficients by a declared ratio, especially when accompanied by degraded residuals or status, is recorded as a numerical dominance risk. Finite continuation agreement is evidence, not universal exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Re-solve with a larger penalty and compare violations, genuine objectives, decisions, residuals, and status to detect under-penalization or numerical dominance.

children.title: Artificial-Value Dominance
children.top_down_role: Regimes where surrogate bounds or penalties dominate genuine model structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Artificial-Value Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational dominance test for artificial variables in an augmented minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an augmented objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x+p^{\mathsf T}a\), where \(a\ge 0\) are artificial variables and \(p\ge 0\) are penalty coefficients. For a computed point \((x,a)\), define \(V_{\mathrm{art}}=p^{\mathsf T}a\), \(V_{\mathrm{true}}=|c^{\mathsf T}x|\), and \(\rho_{\mathrm{art}}=V_{\mathrm{art}}/\max\{1,V_{\mathrm{true}}\}\). Given a declared threshold \(\tau_{\mathrm{dom}}>0\), artificial-value dominance is the predicate \(\rho_{\mathrm{art}}\ge\tau_{\mathrm{dom}}\). An audit must additionally report \(\|a\|_{\infty}\), because dominance can arise from a large penalty, a materially positive artificial variable, or both.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Artificial values dominate when their penalized objective contribution exceeds a declared multiple of the original objective scale; the audit also reports the largest artificial variable.
assumptions_latex: \(a\ge 0\) and \(p\ge 0\).
\(\tau_{\mathrm{dom}}>0\) is fixed before inspecting the computed solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathrm{art}}\ge\tau_{\mathrm{dom}}\).
review_flags: No supplied locator supports this operational dominance threshold.
Term may alternatively denote domination caused by artificial bounds or Big-M constants.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits this audit leaf, and the notation is delimited and internally coherent. However, the ratio, denominator normalization, threshold predicate, and required infinity-norm report are project-specific choices with no cited source. The available inventory does not resolve whether the title concerns artificial variables, artificial bounds, or Big-M values.

children.title: Near-Infeasibility Audit
children.top_down_role: Evidence that small perturbations could alter feasibility classification.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Infeasibility Audit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-relaxation audit for equality and bound feasibility under finite tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\) and \(l\le x\le u\), choose positive scales \(s\), \(d_l\), and \(d_u\), then solve for the minimum \(\eta\ge0\) satisfying \(|Ax-b|\le\eta s\), \(x\ge l-\eta d_l\), and \(x\le u+\eta d_u\), componentwise. Let the optimum be \(\eta_*\). Given \(0\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{near}}\), report near-infeasibility when \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}<\eta_*\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{near}}\). Report the active relaxed rows and bounds, together with their normalized violations, as the diagnostic output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a scaled common relaxation. The model is near-infeasible when the required relaxation exceeds feasibility tolerance but remains within a declared near-infeasibility band.
assumptions_latex: \(s>0\), \(d_l>0\), and \(d_u>0\) componentwise for finite rows and bounds.
\(0\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{near}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}<\eta_*\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{near}}\).
review_flags: No supplied source directly specifies this near-infeasibility audit.
Threshold and scaling conventions require project-level standardization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the audit leaf, but the common-relaxation formulation, scaling vectors, threshold band, and active-set output are an uncited operational specification. A source is needed to establish the intended normalization and meaning of near-infeasibility.

children.title: Near-Unboundedness Audit
children.top_down_role: Evidence that weak limiting structure could alter boundedness classification.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Unboundedness Audit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate recession-direction audit for a bounded-form minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(l\le x\le u\), seek a direction \(d\) satisfying \(c^{\mathsf T}d=-1\), \(d_i\ge0\) when only \(l_i\) is finite, \(d_i\le0\) when only \(u_i\) is finite, and \(d_i=0\) when both bounds are finite. Minimize \(\delta(d)=\|D_rAd\|_{\infty}\) over these conditions. If the optimum \(\delta_*\) satisfies \(0<\delta_*\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{dir}}\), report near-unboundedness; if \(\delta_*=0\), report an exact improving recession direction instead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search for a bound-compatible improving direction and minimize its scaled equality residual. A small nonzero residual indicates near-unboundedness; zero gives an exact unboundedness direction.
assumptions_latex: The LP is a minimization problem with equality constraints and componentwise bounds.
\(D_r\) is a fixed positive diagonal row-scaling matrix.
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{dir}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0<\delta_*\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{dir}}\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this approximate-direction audit.
Direction normalization and residual threshold require source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the audit leaf, and the proposed bound-compatible direction test is mathematically plausible. The objective normalization, scaled residual minimization, and small-nonzero classification are nevertheless uncited conventions whose exact form cannot be validated from the supplied inventory.

children.title: Status-Ambiguity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes where infeasibility, unboundedness, or indeterminate status is difficult to distinguish.

knowledge_statements.title: Status-Ambiguity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where feasibility and recession diagnostics cannot robustly distinguish solver status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\eta_*\) be the minimum normalized feasibility relaxation and \(\delta_*\) the minimum normalized residual of an improving recession direction. For declared tolerances \(\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_d>0\) and uncertainty widths \(w_f,w_d>0\), define the status-ambiguity boundary by \(|\eta_*-\varepsilon_f|\le w_f\) or \(|\delta_*-\varepsilon_d|\le w_d\). Within this set, perturbing either diagnostic by its uncertainty width can cross a classification threshold; therefore a unique status among feasible, infeasible, bounded, and unbounded is not numerically robust without stronger certificates or higher-precision recomputation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Status is ambiguous when a feasibility or recession diagnostic lies within its uncertainty width of the corresponding classification threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_d,w_f,w_d>0\).
\(\eta_*\) and \(\delta_*\) use fixed scaling conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\eta_*-\varepsilon_f|\le w_f\ \lor\ |\delta_*-\varepsilon_d|\le w_d\).

notation.meaning: Certified or estimated diagnostic uncertainty widths.

review_flags: This operational boundary is not supported by the supplied source locators.
The intended solver-status taxonomy and uncertainty model remain source-dependent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the terminal container. The uncertainty widths and disjunctive boundary are project-defined and uncited, and proximity of either score to one threshold does not by itself justify ambiguity among all four listed statuses without a specified status logic and uncertainty model.

children.title: Presolve Ablation

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Ablation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Paired diagnostic experiment isolating the effect of presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an LP instance, solver version, algorithm, scaling policy, tolerances, precision, resource limits, and random seed. Run configuration \(C_1\) with presolve enabled and configuration \(C_0\) with presolve disabled, changing no other declared setting. For each run record the status, objective value, normalized primal and dual residuals, complementarity residual, iterations, time, and any certificate. The presolve ablation output is the paired difference vector \(\Delta=m(C_1)-m(C_0)\), augmented by an indicator that statuses or certificate validity disagree. Interpret \(\Delta\) only as a controlled presolve effect under the fixed configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run otherwise identical solves with presolve on and off, then compare statuses, certificates, residuals, objective values, and resource measures as paired observations.

Recorded diagnostic metric vector for configuration C.

children.title: Scaling Ablation

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Ablation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Paired diagnostic experiment isolating solver scaling transformations.

The scaling-ablation output is \(\Delta_s=m(C_s)-m(C_u)\), plus indicators for status disagreement and loss of certificate validity in original coordinates.

children.title: Joint Transformation Ablation

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Transformation Ablation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factorial experiment separating presolve, scaling, and interaction effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix all solver settings other than presolve and scaling, and run the four configurations \(C_{00},C_{10},C_{01},C_{11}\), where the indices indicate presolve and scaling being disabled or enabled. Evaluate every diagnostic vector \(m_{ij}=m(C_{ij})\) in original model coordinates. Define the presolve effect \(E_p=m_{10}-m_{00}\), scaling effect \(E_s=m_{01}-m_{00}\), and interaction \(E_{ps}=m_{11}-m_{10}-m_{01}+m_{00}\). Report these vectors together with all status and certificate-validity disagreements; a nonzero \(E_{ps}\) means the joint effect is not additive under the selected metrics.

All metric vectors have common definitions and original-coordinate normalization.

Diagnostic vector from configuration indexed by i and j.

children.title: Solver-Method Cross-Checks

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Method Cross-Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled comparison of mathematically distinct LP solution methods.

\(\varepsilon_v>0\), with common residual and certificate tolerances declared in advance.

children.title: Algorithm-Configuration Cross-Checks

knowledge_statements.title: Algorithm-Configuration Cross-Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled comparison across solver algorithms and parameter configurations.

Independently evaluate each output in original coordinates to obtain a signature \(S_i=(\sigma_i,v_i,r_{p,i},r_{d,i},r_{c,i},q_i)\), containing status, objective, primal, dual, and complementarity residuals, and certificate-validity flag. The cross-check returns the signatures, configuration differences, and a disagreement matrix whose entry is one exactly when any required status, metric, or certificate predicate fails.

children.title: Cross-Check Disagreement Triage
children.top_down_role: Classification of status, quality, or performance disagreements exposed by cross-checks.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Check Disagreement Triage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered classification of disagreements among controlled LP solver runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given disagreeing run signatures, first reevaluate every candidate solution, ray, and certificate against the original LP data. Assign the first applicable class in the ordered list: invalid certificate; original-coordinate residual failure; status disagreement with valid competing certificates; objective disagreement among feasible optimal claims; transformation-only disagreement; tolerance-sensitive disagreement; precision-sensitive disagreement; or unresolved execution variability. For tolerance and precision classes, require that changing only the named control removes the disagreement. Output the class, failed predicates, reproducing configurations, and the smallest controlled intervention observed to restore agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Revalidate original-coordinate evidence, then classify disagreements by certificate failure, residuals, status, objective, transformations, tolerances, precision, or unresolved variability.
assumptions_latex: Run signatures and original LP data are available.
Comparison predicates and their tolerances were fixed before triage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{class}(D)\) is the first applicable category in the declared ordered list.
review_flags: The triage order and category definitions lack direct support in supplied sources.

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Sensitivity Experiments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled tolerance sweep for detecting unstable statuses and numerical outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an ordered grid \(T=\{\tau_1>\cdots>\tau_k\}\) of solver tolerances and hold the LP, solver version, method, transformations, precision, seed, and resource limits fixed. For each \(\tau_i\), solve once or under a declared repetition policy and independently recompute an original-coordinate signature \(S_i\). Report every adjacent transition \(S_i\to S_{i+1}\), including status changes, certificate-validity changes, and normalized metric differences. A conclusion is tolerance-stable on \(T\) only if all statuses and certificate predicates agree and every monitored metric remains within its declared comparison band.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sweep an ordered tolerance grid while fixing other controls, then report adjacent changes and whether status, certificates, and metrics remain stable.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau_1>\cdots>\tau_k>0\).
All non-tolerance controls and independent evaluation rules remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_1\sim S_2\sim\cdots\sim S_k\) under the declared agreement predicates.

notation.meaning: Ordered grid of tested solver tolerances.
Original-coordinate diagnostic signature at tolerance i.

review_flags: No supplied source directly specifies this tolerance-sensitivity experiment.
Tolerance coupling across solver criteria requires implementation-specific sourcing.
